children.text: tattvacintāmaṇau śabdākāṅkṣāvādapūrvapakṣaḥ
children.translated_text: In the <s>Tattvacintāmaṇi</s>, the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) of the section on verbal expectancy (<s>śabdākāṅkṣāvāda</s>).

children.text:
atha keyamākaṅkṣā, na tāvadavinābhāvaḥ, nīlaṃ sarojamityādāvabhāvāt /
vimalaṃ jalaṃ nadyāḥ kacche mahiṣa ityatra jalānvitanadyā avinābhāvāt kacche sākāṅkṣatāpatteḥ /
nāpi samabhivyāhṛtapadasmāritapadārthajijñāsā, ajijñāsorapi vākyarthabodhāt viśvajitā yajeta dvāraṃ ityatrāpadārthayopyadhikāriṇo 'pyāhṛtasya pidhānasya cākāṅkṣitatvācca, tatra śabdakalpanapakṣe 'pi ghaṭaḥ karmatvamānayanaṃ kṛtirityatra jijñāsitasyānayanāderākāṅkṣitatvāpatteḥ /
atha jijñāsāyogyatā, sā jijñāsā ca viśeṣājñāne bhavati, yogyatā ca śrotari taduccāraṇajanyasaṃsargāvagamaprāgabhāvaḥ, vimalaṃ jalaṃ nadyāḥ kacche mahiṣa ityatra tātparyavaśāt kadācit nadyāḥ kacche saṃsargāvagamāt tatprāgabhāvasattve 'pi śrotari taduccāraṇena tātparyavaśāt jalānvitanadyāḥ kacche saṃsargāvagamoneti na tatpragābhāvaḥ, ghaṭaḥ karmatvamānayanamityatrāpi tatheti cet /
na /
nirākāṅkṣe taduccāraṇajanyasaṃsargāvagamaprāgabhāvasya siddhyasiddhiparāhatatvāt /
kiñca yatraikovimalaṃ jalamityaśrutvaiva tātparyabhrameṇā vā nadyāḥ kacchānvayaparatvamavaiti, aparaḥ samastena śrutvā nadyā jalānvayaparatvamavadhārayati, tatrobhayarapi taduccāraṇajanyasaṃsargāvagamāt nadyā ityubhayasākāṅkṣaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: Now, what is this <s>ākāṅkṣā</s> (syntactic expectancy)? It is not, first of all, invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>), since that is absent in cases such as 'the blue lotus' and the like. In 'the clean water, the river, the bank, the buffalo,' there is invariable concomitance between the river and water, so the absurd consequence would arise that 'bank' is also expectant [of the river]. Nor is it the desire to know the referent recalled by a co-uttered word, because verbal cognition of the sentence-meaning arises even for one who has no desire to know; because in 'one should sacrifice with the Viśvajit [rite]—the door,' although the door is not a referent [of the ritual instruction] and although the one qualified [for the rite] is also not expressed, both are nonetheless expected; and even on the theory that words create [their meanings], in 'pot—objectness—bringing—verbal activity,' the absurd consequence would arise that the desired [items like] bringing are already expected. Now if [ākāṅkṣā is] the capacity for the desire to know — that desire to know occurs when there is ignorance of the specific [connection], and the capacity consists in the prior absence of the cognition of connection generated by that utterance in the listener — in 'the clean water, the river, the bank, the buffalo,' through the force of the speaker's intention, since sometimes there is cognition of the connection with 'the bank of the river,' even though the prior absence [of that cognition] exists in the listener, the speaker's intention does not [produce] the cognition of connection with 'the bank of the water-bearing river' from that utterance, so there is no such prior absence. And the same in 'pot—objectness—bringing—verbal activity.' Objection: No, because in one free from expectancy, the question of whether the prior absence of the cognition of connection generated by that utterance exists or not is irrelevant. Moreover, where one person, without hearing 'the clean water,' through confusion about the speaker's intention, understands [the words] as having their connection with 'the bank of the river,' while another person, having heard the whole [sentence], determines the intention to be 'the water-connection with the river' — for both of them, since there is cognition of the connection generated by the utterance 'of the river,' that [word] would be expectant for both.

children.text:
api ca pragābhāvābhāvasya kāraṇāntarābhāvavyāptatvāt tata eva kāryābhāva iti kimākāṅkṣayā /
evañca yogyatāsattī api na hetū ayogye anāsanne ca taduccāraṇajanyasaṃsargajñānābhāvena tatprāgabhāvābhāvāt /
na caivaṃ bādhābhāvasyānumityādāvapi hetutvaṃ, prāgabhāvābhāvenaiva kāryābhāvāt prāgabhāvasya ca kāryamātrahetutvāt /
śabde nāsādhāraṇyaṃ utthitotthāpyākāṅkṣayorutkarṣāpakarṣau na syātāṃ prāgabhāve tadabhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, since the absence of the prior absence is pervaded by the absence of any other cause, from that alone follows the absence of the effect — so what is the use of <s>ākāṅkṣā</s>? And thus, <s>yogyatā</s> (semantic fitness) and <s>āsatti</s> (contiguity) would also not be causes, since in the case of the unfit and the non-contiguous, the absence of that prior absence [already entails] the absence of the cognition of connection generated by that utterance. Nor can it be objected that absence of defeater (<s>bādhā</s>) would similarly not have causal status in inference and such, since the absence of the effect already follows from the absence of the prior absence alone, and the prior absence is merely a cause of the effect [in general]. This is not unique to verbal testimony. The degrees of strong and weak expectancy, whether actualized or potential, would not exist, since in prior absence there is no such [gradation].

children.text:
atha jñāpya-taditarānvayaprakārakajijñāsānukūlapadārthopasthitijanakatve satyajanitatātparyaviṣayānvayabodhatvamākāṅkṣā, ghaṭamānayatītyatra ghaṭamityukte kimānayati paśyati vā, ānayatītyukte kiṃ ghaṭaṃ anyadveti jijñāsā bhavati /
ghaṭaḥ karmatvamānanayanaṃ kṛtirityatrābhedena nānvayo 'yogyatvāt, ghaṭasyānayanamiti tu nānvayabodhaḥ ghaṭa itipadāt sambandhitvena ghaṭasyānupasthiteḥ /
rājña iti putreṇa janitānvayabodhatvāt na puruṣamākāṅkṣatīti cet, tarhi nāma-vibhakti-dhātvākhyātārthānāṃ ghaṭa-karmatvānayana-kṛtīnāṃ svarūpeṇopasthitirnānvayanvayaprakārakajijñāsānukūleti tatra nākāṅkṣā syāt /
ghaṭaḥ karmatvamānayanaṃ kṛtirityatra ghaṭamānayatītyatrevānvayabodhaḥ syāt, na hi tatra padārthasvarūpāṇāṃ etadvailakṣaṇyenopasthitiḥ, trayāṇāṃ tulyavat smaraṇe prathamaṃ
children.translated_text: Now if [ākāṅkṣā is defined as]: that property of not having generated the cognition of connection that is the object of the speaker's intention, while being such that it generates the presentation of word-meanings conducive to the desire to know the connection with something other than what is to be known — in 'he brings the pot,' when 'pot' is uttered, the desire arises: 'does he bring it or see it?'; when 'brings' is uttered: 'the pot or something else?' In 'pot—objectness—bringing—verbal activity,' there is no connection through identity since that would be unfit; and 'the bringing of the pot' is not a cognition of connection, since from the word 'pot,' the pot is not presented as a relatum. If it is objected that 'of the king' does not expect 'person' because the cognition of connection with 'son' has already been generated — then the presentation of the word-meanings in their own form, namely pot, objectness, bringing, and verbal activity — the referents of noun-stem, case-ending, verbal root, and conjugated verb — would not be conducive to the desire to know the connection, and so there would be no expectancy there. In 'pot—objectness—bringing—verbal activity,' the cognition of connection would arise only from 'he brings the pot,' since there is no presentation of the word-meanings in their own form with any distinctiveness [in the former]; and when three [words] are recalled equally, first

children.text: yato rājña iti puruṣeṇa nānveti kintu putreṇa tata evāgrre 'pi vyarthamajanitānvayabodhatvamiti /
children.translated_text: since 'of the king' connects not with 'person' but with 'son,' the claim that it has not generated a cognition of connection is useless even going forward.

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 208)
children.translated_text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 208)

children.text: śabdākāṅkṣāvādasiddhāntaḥ
children.translated_text: The established doctrine (<s>siddhānta</s>) of the theory of verbal expectancy (<s>śabdākāṅkṣā</s>)

children.text:
ucyate /
abhidhānāparyavasānamākāṅkṣā yasya yena vinā na svārthānvayānubhāvakatvaṃ tasya tadaparyavasānaṃ, nāma-vibhaki-dhatvākhyāta-kriyā-kārakapadānāṃ parasparaṃ vinā na parasparasya svārthānvayānubhavajanakatvaṃ /
paramate nīlaghaṭo 'sti nīlaṃ ghaṭamānayetyādau nāmārthānāṃ kārakāṇāñca na parasparamanvayabodhaḥ viśeṣaṇānvitavibhaktyarthānanvayāditi na viśiṣṭavaiśiṣṭyenānvayaḥ kintvārthaḥ samājaḥ /
asmākantu nīla-ghaṭayorabhedānubhavabalādabheda eva saṃsargaḥ viśeṣavibhaktiḥ sādhutvārthaṃ /
children.translated_text: It is stated: <s>Ākāṅkṣā</s> is the incompleteness of denotation — for that without which a word is not capable of producing the experience of its own meaning's connection, that [other word] constitutes its incompleteness. The words for noun-stems, case-endings, verbal roots, conjugated verbs, actions, and <s>kārakas</s> (case-relations), without each other, are not capable of producing the experience of each other's connection with their own meaning. According to the rival view, in 'there is a blue pot' and 'bring the blue pot' and similar cases, the noun-meanings and the <s>kāraka</s> meanings do not produce mutual cognition of connection, since there is no connection with the case-ending meaning conjoined with the qualifier — so the connection is not through qualified qualification, but rather the meaning is a collection. For us, however, the connection between 'blue' and 'pot' is precisely identity, by the force of the experience of non-difference, and the specific case-ending serves the purpose of grammatical correctness (<s>sādhutva</s>).

children.text:
yadvā samānavibhaktikayorabhedānubhavabalāt viśeṣaṇānvitavibhakterabhedārthakatvaṃ ato viśeṣaṇa-viśeṣyabhāvānubhāvakatvaṃ tatpadayoḥ, na parasparaṃ vinā /
dvāramityatrādhyāhāraṃ vinā pratiyogyalābhāt na svārthānvayānubhāvakatvaṃ, viśvajitā yajetetyatra mamedaṃ kāryamiti pravarttakatātparyaviṣayajñānaṃ nādhikāriṇāṃ vineti tadākāṅkṣā /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, by the force of the experience of non-difference between two words with the same case-ending, the case-ending conjoined with the qualifier denotes identity — hence the capacity of those words to produce the experience of the qualifier-qualificand relation is not without each other. In 'the door,' without supplying [an implied verb], since the correlate is not obtained, there is no capacity to produce the experience of one's own meaning's connection. In 'one should sacrifice with the Viśvajit [rite],' the cognition 'this is my duty' that is the object of the speaker's intention regarding the impeller does not [arise] without the qualified person — hence that is expected.

children.text:
yadvā kartturivādhikāriṇo 'pi ākṣepādeva lābha iti tadanvayo na śābdaḥ kintvānumānikaḥ, gauṇalākṣaṇikayorananubhāvakatvapakṣe tadupasthāpitasyādhyāhṛtasyevetarapadaṃ vinā nānubhāvakatvaṃ /
ghaṭaḥ karmatvaṃ ānayanaṃ kṛtirityādau abhedena nānvayabodho 'yogyatvāt tattatpadebhyastātparyaviṣayatattatpadārthasvarūpajñānañca padāntaraṃ vinaiva / ghaṭamānayatītyatreva bhrameṇa tathānvayatātparye 'pi kriyā -kārakabhāvena nānvayaḥ nāma-vibhaki-dhātvākhyāta-kriyā-kārakapadānāṃ anvayabodhe tānyeva padāni samarthāni na tu tadarthakāni padāntarāṇi /
agniḥ karaṇatvaṃ odanaḥ karmatā pākaḥ kṛtiḥ iṣṭasādhanatā ityādipadebhyaḥ agnirnodanaṃ pacetetyatreva anvayābodhāt, agnikaraṇakaudanakarmakapākaviṣayakakṛtiriṣṭasādhanaṃ iti tu vākyaṃ na padaṃ, ata eva dvāramityatra pidhehipadādhyāhāraḥ, kriyāpadārthasyānyata upasthitau api kārakānanvayāt asāmarthyañca svabhāvāt /
anāsannamapi āsannatādaśāyāṃ āsannatvabhrameṇa vā anvayabodhasamarthameva /
vahninā siñcatītyatra kriyā-kārakapadayoranvayabodhe sāmarthye 'pi ayogyatājñānaṃ pratibandhakaṃ dāhe samarthasyāpyagnermaṇiriva /
ata eva yogyatābhramāt pratibandhakābhāve tato 'pyanvayabodhaḥ /
nahi svabhāvato 'samarthaṃ āropitasāmarthyaṃ vā dahati pacati veti, prakṛte tu padārthasvarūpajñānaṃ na tvanvayabhramo 'pi /
purūṣapadaṃ vināpi rājñā ityasya putreṇa samaṃ svārthānvayānubhāvakatvaṃ iti na tadākāṅkṣā /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, just as the agent, the qualified person too is obtained through implication alone, so its connection is not verbal but inferential. On the view that figurative and indirect expressions are not productive [of verbal cognition], it is only the word that is either implicitly supplied or presented through them, and the other word without it is not productive [of cognition of connection]. In 'pot—objectness—bringing—verbal activity' and such, there is no cognition of connection through identity since that is unfit; and the cognition of the respective word-meanings in their own form from the respective words is [obtained] without any other word. The cognition of connection arises only from 'he brings the pot'; for it is not the case that there is any presentation of the word-meaning essences differently [there]; and when three are recalled equally — noun-stem, case-ending, verbal root, conjugated verb, action, and <s>kāraka</s> words alone are capable of producing the cognition of connection, not other words synonymous with their meanings. From the words 'fire—instrumentality—rice—objecthood—cooking—verbal activity—being a means to the desired' — the cognition of connection arises only in 'he cooks rice with fire'; but 'the verbal activity whose content is cooking, whose instrument is fire, whose object is rice, and which is a means to the desired' is a sentence, not a word. Hence in 'the door,' the word 'close' is supplied; for even when the action-meaning is presented from elsewhere, there is incompetence due to the non-connection of the <s>kārakas</s>, and this is by nature. Even what is not contiguous, in a state of contiguity or through the false impression of contiguity, is indeed capable of producing the cognition of connection. In 'he sprinkles with fire,' even though the action and <s>kāraka</s> words have the capacity to produce the cognition of connection, the cognition of unfitness acts as an obstruction — like a gem [that blocks] fire, even though fire is capable of burning. Hence, from the absence of the obstruction through a false impression of fitness, the cognition of connection arises even from that. For it is not the case that what is naturally incapable, or whose capability is superimposed, burns or cooks; but in the present case, [there is] cognition of the word-meaning in its own form, not even a false impression of connection. Even without the word 'person,' the word 'of the king' has the capacity to produce the experience of its own meaning's connection together with 'son' — hence there is no expectancy for that.

children.text:
yadvā trayāṇāṃ smaraṇo 'janitānvayabodhadaśāyāṃ puruṣānvaye tātparyābhāvāt nānvayabodha ityagre 'pi tathā /
na ca putrasyotthitākāṅkṣatvāt tenaivānvayabodha iti /
vācyam /
tātparyavaśāt puruṣeṇaiva prathamamanvayabodhāt /
ata evānvayabodhasamarthatve sati ajanitatātparyaviṣayānvayabodhatvamākāṅkṣeti kecit /
prakṛti-pratyayābhyāmanvayabodhe janite 'pi vākyaikavākyatāvat kriyā-kārakapadayorajanitānvayabodhatvamākāṅkṣā /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, in the state where three [words] are recalled and cognition of connection has not yet been generated, there is no cognition of connection with 'person' due to the absence of the speaker's intention for that connection — and the same going forward. Nor should it be said that since 'son' is the actualized expected [word], the cognition of connection is produced by it alone. [This must be rejected] because by the force of the speaker's intention, the cognition of connection arises first with 'person' alone. Hence some [hold that] <s>ākāṅkṣā</s> is the property of not having generated the cognition of connection that is the object of the speaker's intention, while having the capacity to generate the cognition of connection. Even when the cognition of connection is generated from the stem and suffix together, <s>ākāṅkṣā</s> is the property of the action and <s>kāraka</s> words not having generated the cognition of connection — just as in a sentence that forms a single syntactic unit.

children.text: navyāstu padaviśeṣajanyapadārthopasthitiḥ ghaṭaḥ karmatvaṃ ānayanaṃ kṛtirityevambidhapadājanyapadārthopasthitirvā
children.translated_text: The <s>Navya</s> (New) [logicians], however, [hold that ākāṅkṣā is]: the presentation of word-meanings generated by specific words — or the presentation of word-meanings generated by words of such-and-such a kind, like 'pot—objectness—bringing—verbal activity' —

children.text: āsattiranvayabodhāṅgamityāsattyabhāvādevambidhaśabdānnānvayabodhaḥ tvayāpyevambipadārthopasthite rākāṅkṣāhetutvenāvaśyamabhyupeyatvāt, janitānvayabodhāt nānvayāntarabodhaḥ tātparyābhāvādityākāṅkṣāyāḥ kāraṇatvameva nāsti, kintu svajanakopasthiteḥ paricāyakatvamātramiti /
children.translated_text: since <s>āsatti</s> (contiguity) is a factor in the cognition of connection, from the absence of contiguity alone there is no cognition of connection from words of such-and-such a kind; and since you too must necessarily accept [contiguity] as a cause of expectancy when word-meanings are presented from such-and-such words, there is simply no causal status of <s>ākāṅkṣā</s> from the principle 'since the cognition of connection has been generated, there is no further cognition of connection due to the absence of the speaker's intention.' Rather, [ākāṅkṣā] is merely an identifier of its own cause, namely presentation.

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 245)
children.translated_text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 245)

children.text: tattvacintāmaṇau yogyatāvādaḥ
children.translated_text: The discussion of <s>yogyatā</s> (semantic fitness) in the <s>Tattvacintāmaṇi</s>

children.text: pūrvapakṣaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (opponent's position)

children.text:
nanu kā yogyatā, na tāvat sajātīye 'nvayadarśanaṃ, yathākathañcit sājātyasyāvyāvarttakatvāt /
padārthatāvacchedakena sājātyasyādyajātaḥ payaḥ pibatītyadāvabhāvāt vākyārthasyāpūrvatvācca /
nāpi samabhivyāhṛtapadārthasaṃsargavyāpyadharmavattvaṃ, vākyārthasyānumeyatvāpatteḥ /
na ca vastugatyā saṃsargavyāpyo yo dharmastadvastaṃ tacca na jñātumupayujyate iti nānumeyaḥ saṃsarga iti vācyam /
yogyatābhramācchābdabhramānupapatteḥ /
ata evānvayaniścayaviraha eva yogyatā svarūpasattī hetuḥ tatra taddharmābhāvaniścaye tatprakārakaśābdajñānānudayāt iti parāstam /
nāpi samabhivyāhṛtapadārthasaṃsargābhāvavyāpyadharmaśrūnyatvam, prameyamabhidheyamityādau saṃsargābhāvasyāprasiddhyā tadanirūpaṇāt gehaniṣṭhaghaṭābhāve pramite ghaṭo 'stītivākyāttanniścaye 'pyanvayajñānānudayācca /
nāpi bādhakapramāṇābhāvaḥ, anyacca yadbādhakaṃ tadabhāvasyāyogye 'pi sattvāt / nāpi prakṛtasaṃsargabādhakasyābhāvaḥ, pratiyogisiddhyasiddhivyāghātāt /
na ca prakṛtasaṃsarge anyatra siddhasya bādhakapramāṇasyābhāvaḥ, prakṛtasaṃsargasya prathamapratīteḥ ayogye 'pi tatsatvācca /
children.translated_text: Now, what is <s>yogyatā</s> (semantic fitness)? It is not the observation of connection (<s>anvaya</s>) in something of the same class, since same-classness in any manner whatsoever is non-excluding; and because, by the delimitor of the category-status (<s>padārthatāvacchedaka</s>), same-classness is unestablished in cases such as 'milk drinks water' (<s>payaḥ pibati</s>), and because the sentence-meaning [in any new sentence] is unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>). Nor is it the possession of a property pervaded by the connection of the co-uttered word-meanings, since [then] the sentence-meaning would wrongly become an object of inference (<s>anumeya</s>). And it should not be said that the connection (<s>saṃsarga</s>) is not inferred [on the ground] that the property which, by the way things really are, is pervaded by the connection, and that real thing — these are not employed in being cognized; because, were the [fitness] a mere error (<s>bhrama</s>), the verbal cognition [arising from it could] not be an error [in the requisite way]. For this very reason the [view] is refuted that <s>yogyatā</s> is merely the absence of a determination of connection (<s>anvayaniścaya-viraha</s>) — that this, present as a [mere] essential nature (<s>svarūpasat</s>), is the cause; for there, when the absence of that property is determined, no verbal cognition having that as its qualifier-mode (<s>prakāra</s>) arises. Nor is it the being empty of a property pervaded by the absence of the connection of the co-uttered word-meanings, since in cases such as 'the knowable is nameable' (<s>prameyam abhidheyam</s>) the absence of connection is unestablished and so cannot be characterized; and because, when 'the absence of a pot located in the house' has been cognized, even though one determines [the fitness] from the sentence 'there is a pot', the relational cognition still fails to arise. Nor is it the absence of a sublating means of valid cognition (<s>bādhaka-pramāṇa-abhāva</s>), since the absence of some other thing which is a sublater is present even in what is unfit (<s>ayogya</s>). Nor is it the absence of a sublater of the connection under discussion, since [that view] is contradicted by the establishedness-or-unestablishedness of the counter-correlate (<s>pratiyogin</s>). And it should not be said that it is the absence of a sublating means of valid cognition established elsewhere with regard to the connection under discussion, since the connection under discussion is what is first cognized, and since that [absence] is present even in what is unfit.

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 256)
children.translated_text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 256)

children.text:
tatra bādhakamapyastīti cet, tarhi prakṛtasaṃsargabādhakasyābhāvaḥ taccāprasiddham /
ata eva tatra bādhakasyāpyanirūpaṇam /
nāpītarapadārthasaṃsargābhāvapramāviṣayatvābhāvo 'padapadārthe, kevalānvayinyaprasiddheḥ /
etena yatrāsambandhagrāhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ nāsti tadyogyamiti nirastam /
nāpi bodhanīyasaṃsargābhāvapramāvirahaḥ, pratiyogyaprasiddheḥ, bodhanīyasaṃsargasya prāgapratīteḥ yogyatā ca na svarūpasatyupayujyate ityuktam, ayogye tat sattvasyānirūpaṇācca /
api ca svīyabādhakapramāvirahasyāyogye 'pi sattvāt bādhakapramāmātravirahasya yogye 'pi jñātumaśakyatvāt parapramāyā ayogyatvāt /
na ca svarūpasannevāyaṃ hetuḥ, svīyabādhakapramāvirahadāśāyāṃ yogyatābhrameṇa śābdabhramānupapatteḥ, anvayaprayojakarūpavattvena bādhakapramāmātraviraho 'numeya iti cet / na /
sekānānvitatoye dravadravyatve satyapi bādhakasattvena vyabhicārāt upajīvyatvena tasyaiva yogyatātvāpatteśca /
na caivameveti vācyam /
ākāṅkṣāsattyanvayaprayojakarūpavattve satyapyanāptavākye bādhakapramāyāmanvābodhāt, bādhakapramāviraho heturiti cettarhyāvaśyakatvāt saiva yogyatā /
children.translated_text: If it be said that there too a sublater exists — then [we say] there is an absence of a sublater of the connection under discussion, and that [sublater] is unestablished. For this very reason, there too even the sublater cannot be characterized. Nor is it, with respect to a non-word's word-meaning, the absence of being an object of the valid cognition of the absence of connection with the other word-meaning, since with regard to a purely positive concomitant (<s>kevalānvayin</s>) [such an absence] is unestablished. By this, the [view] that 'whatever has no means of valid cognition apprehending the lack of relation is fit' is refuted. Nor is it the lack of the valid cognition of the absence of the connection that is to be conveyed (<s>bodhanīya-saṃsarga</s>), since the counter-correlate is unestablished, [and] since the connection that is to be conveyed has not been cognized before; and it has been said that <s>yogyatā</s>, present as mere essential nature (<s>svarūpasat</s>), is not employed [as cause], and because the presence of that [absence] in what is unfit cannot be characterized. Moreover, since the lack of one's own sublating valid cognition is present even in what is unfit, and since the lack of any sublating valid cognition whatsoever cannot be known even in what is fit, [and] since another's valid cognition is unfit [for this role]. And this cause is not merely something present as essential nature (<s>svarūpasat</s>), since on the condition that there be a lack of one's own sublating valid cognition, the verbal error cannot be accounted for by an error of fitness (<s>yogyatā-bhrama</s>). If it be said that the lack of any sublating valid cognition whatsoever is inferred through the possession of the form that is the prompter of connection (<s>anvaya-prayojaka-rūpa</s>) — no. For in 'the water that is unconnected with sprinkling' (<s>sekānanvita-toya</s>), even though there is the property of being a fluid substance (<s>drava-dravyatva</s>), there is deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>), since the sublater is present; and because, by reason of its being presupposed (<s>upajīvya</s>), that very [lack] would wrongly come to be <s>yogyatā</s> itself. And it should not be said that it is just so [for the [<s>yogyatā</s>] too]. For even when there is the possession of the form that prompts connection together with expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>), in the case of a sentence from an unreliable speaker (<s>anāpta-vākya</s>) there is relational cognition along with a sublating valid cognition. If it be said that the lack of a sublating valid cognition is the cause — then, since it is indispensable, that very [lack] is <s>yogyatā</s>.

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 262)
children.translated_text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 262)

children.text: yogyatāvādasiddhāntaḥ
children.translated_text: The established conclusion of the doctrine of <s>yogyatā</s>

children.text: ucyate bādhakapramāviraho yogyatā, sā cetarapadārthasaṃsarge 'parapadārthaniṣṭhātyantābhāvapratiyogitvapramāviśeṣyatvābhāvaḥ / prameyaṃ vācyamityatra prameyaniṣṭhātyantābhāvapratiyogitvapramāviśeṣyatvaṃ gotve prasiddhaṃ vācyatvasaṃsarge tadabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is stated: the lack of a sublating valid cognition (<s>bādhaka-pramā-viraha</s>) is <s>yogyatā</s>. And that is, with regard to the connection of one word-meaning [with another], the absence of being-the-qualificand of the valid cognition of being-a-counter-correlate of an absolute absence (<s>atyantābhāva</s>) residing in the other word-meaning. In the sentence 'the knowable is expressible' (<s>prameyaṃ vācyam</s>), being-the-qualificand of the valid cognition of being-a-counter-correlate of an absolute absence residing in the knowable is established with regard to cowness (<s>gotva</s>); [hence] there is the absence of that [being-the-qualificand] in the connection [of the knowable] with expressibility (<s>vācyatva</s>).

children.text: vastutastvitarapadārthasaṃsarge 'parapadārthaniṣṭhātyantābhāvapratiyog itāvacchedakadharmaśūnyatvaṃ yogyatā lāghavāt śakyajñānatvāñca /
children.translated_text: But in truth, <s>yogyatā</s> is, with regard to the connection of one word-meaning [with another], the being-empty of the property that delimits being-a-counter-correlate of an absolute absence residing in the other word-meaning — because of lightness (<s>lāghava</s>) and because it is something that can be known.

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 274)
children.translated_text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 274)

children.text:
na ca naraśiraḥśaucānumānabādhāt tadaśaucabodhakaśabdāt anvayābodha iti vācyam /
upajīvyajātīyatvena śabdasya balavattvāt tenaiva tadanumānabādhāt /
nanvākāṅkṣāsattimattvena śabdasya pramāṇatā na tu yogyatāpi tanniveśino bādhābhāvasya pramāmātrahetutvāditi cet /
na /
bādhe hi pramāṇadoṣo 'vaśyaṃ vaktavyaḥ, anyathā pramāṇaviṣaye bādhāsambhavāt yathānumāne bādhādupādhikalpanadvārā vyāptivighātaḥ, nirūpādhau bādhānavakāśāt /
children.translated_text: And it should not be said that, because of the sublation by the inference of the purity of a man's head, there is no relational cognition from the word that conveys the impurity of that [head]. For, since the word is of the kind that is presupposed (<s>upajīvya</s>), it is stronger, and by that very [word] the inference of that [purity] is sublated. 'Now, the validity (<s>pramāṇatā</s>) of the word [belongs to it] through its possessing expectancy and proximity (<s>ākāṅkṣā-sannidhi</s>), but not <s>yogyatā</s> as well; rather, the absence of sublation that enters into it is merely a cause of the valid cognition.' — if so, no. For in the case of a sublation a flaw in the means of valid cognition must necessarily be stated; otherwise sublation could occur even within the domain of a valid cognition — as in inference, where through sublation, by way of postulating a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>), there is the breaking of the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>), since where there is no limiting condition there is no room for sublation.

children.text:
seyaṃ na svarūpasato prayojikā śābdabhāsocchedaprasaṅgāt /
tanniścayaśca na bhavatyupāyābhāvāt iti cet /
na /
saṃśaya-viparya-pramāsādhāraṇasya yogyatājñānamātrasya kāraṇatvāt /
ayogyatājñānasya pratibandhakasya sarvatrābhāvāt kvacittanniścayo 'pi yogyatānupalabdhā yatheha ghaṭo nāstīti /
children.translated_text: 'This [<s>yogyatā</s>], present as mere essential nature (<s>svarūpasat</s>), is not the prompter, because of the unwanted consequence of the cutting-off of verbal cognition; and the determination of it does not occur, because of the lack of a means [for it].' — if so, no. For the mere cognition of fitness (<s>yogyatā-jñāna</s>) — common to doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>), error (<s>viparyaya</s>), and valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>) — is the cause. Since the cognition of unfitness (<s>ayogyatā-jñāna</s>), which is the obstructer, is everywhere absent, in some case there is even the determination of that [fitness], [though it be] not an apprehension of [actual] fitness — as in the case 'here there is no pot' (<s>iha ghaṭo nāsti</s>).

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 286)
children.translated_text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 286)

children.text: āsattivādaparvapakṣaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (opponent's position) on the doctrine of proximity (<s>āsatti</s>)

children.text:
āsattiścāvyavadhānenānvayapratiyogyupasthitiḥ, sā ca smṛtirnānubhavo 'tonānyonyāśrayaḥ /
atha nānāviśeṣaṇaka-karma-karttṛ-karaṇādhikaraṇa-kriyādikramikapadajñānajanyakramikapadārthasmṛtīnāṃ na yaugapadyaṃ sambhavati āśutaravināśināṃ kramikāṇāṃ malakānupapatteriti kathaṃ tāvatpadārthānvayabodhaḥ viśeṣaṇajñānasādhyatvādviśiṣṭajñānasyeti cet, śrautrapratyekapadānubhavajanyasaṃskāramelakādekadaiva tāvatpadasmṛtiḥ tata ekadaiva tāvatpadārthasmṛtau satyāṃ vākyārthānubhavaḥ /
na cānyaviṣayakasaṃskāreṇa nānyatra smaraṇamiti vācyam /
vakyārthānupapattyā phalabalena saṃskārāṇāṃ parasparasahakāreṇa tatraikasmaraṇakalpanāt /
pratyekavarṇasaṃskārāṇāmivānanyagatikatayā padasmaraṇe /
atha ``yadyadākāṅkṣitaṃ yogyaṃ sannidhānaṃ prapadyate /
tena tenānvitaḥ svārthaḥ padairevāvagamyate'' /
na caivamanvayāntarābhidhānaṃ na syāt viramya vyāpārābhāvāditi vācyam /
evamapi prathamamananvaye hetvanupanyāsāt uttarasya hīdaṃ sāmagrīvaikalyaṃ na pūrvasyeti cet, astu tāvadevaṃ tathāpi caramaṃ tāvatpadārthaghaṭitavākyārthānubhave uktaiva gatirananyagatikatvāt /
atra vadanti, sannidhirna padajanyaivānyavabodhahetuḥ dvāramityādau adhyāhṛtenāpi pidhānādinā anvayabodhadarśanāt /
na ca pidhehīti śabda evādhyāhriyate, anupayogāt /
arthasyaivānvayapratiyogitvenopayogitvāt āvaśyakatvācca /
arthāpatterupapādakaviṣayatvāt /
na ca śabdamātramupapādakaṃ, api tu tadarthaḥ, avaśyakalpyārthasāhacaryeṇa daivavaśasampannaśabdasmṛteranyathāsiddheḥ, anyathā padabodhitasyaivārthasyānvayabodhakatvamiti niyamaśakikalpanāpatteḥ /
svārthānvayaparatvācchabdānāṃ dvāramiti na pidhānānvayabodhakamiti tadanvayabodhārthamavaśyaṃ śabdakalpanamiti cet /
na /
lakṣaṇānāṃ vyabhicārāt tavāpyākṣiptena kartrānvayabodhācca /
atha dvārapadasahabhāvamātraṃ pidhehiśabdasya kalpyate lāghavāt /
na ca pidhānābhidhāyakānekaśabdopasthitau vinigamakavirahaḥ, saṃskāratāratamyāt padaviśeṣasmṛteriti cet /
na /
ākāṅkṣādimatpratiyogyanvitasvārthaparatvasya krṛptatvāt lāghavenārthādhyāhārāt /
na ca śrutapadāni labdhaprayojanānīti kathamapyadhyāhṛte teṣāṃ tātparyamiti vācyam /
śrutārthānvayānupapattyā adhyāhṛte
children.translated_text: And proximity (<s>āsatti</s>) is the presentation, without interval, of the correlate of the connection; and that is recollection (<s>smṛti</s>), not direct experience (<s>anubhava</s>); hence there is no mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśraya</s>). 'Now, of the recollections of the word-meanings — which proceed in sequence from the sequential cognitions of the words denoting the several qualifiers, object, agent, instrument, locus, action, and so on — there can be no simultaneity, since for these sequential [recollections], which perish very swiftly, a coming-together (<s>melaka</s>) cannot be accounted for; so how can there be a relational cognition of so many word-meanings, given that a qualified cognition (<s>viśiṣṭa-jñāna</s>) is to be accomplished by the cognition of the qualifier?' — if so [we reply]: from the coming-together of the impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) produced by the auditory experience of each individual word, there arises at one and the same time the recollection of so many words; thereupon, when at one and the same time there is the recollection of so many word-meanings, there is the experience of the sentence-meaning. And it should not be said that by an impression having one object there is no recollection of another. For, by the force of the result (<s>phala-bala</s>), because the sentence-meaning would otherwise be unaccountable, it is postulated that there, through the mutual cooperation of the impressions, there is a single recollection — just as in the case of the recollection of a word [arising] from the impressions of the individual phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>), since there is no other recourse. Now [it is held]: 'Whatever fit (<s>yogya</s>) and proximate (<s>sannihita</s>) thing that is expected (<s>ākāṅkṣita</s>) comes near — connected with that, the own-meaning [of each word] is cognized by the words themselves.' And it should not be said that in this way there would be no denoting of a further connection, since after pausing there is no [further] operation. Even so, [the opponent says] since at the first [stage] in the case of non-connection no cause is adduced, this deficiency of the totality of conditions (<s>sāmagrī-vaikalya</s>) belongs to the later [step], not to the earlier. — Granted it be so; even so, in the experience of the sentence-meaning which is composed of so many word-meanings up to the last, the recourse already stated [applies], since there is no other recourse. Here they say: proximity (<s>sannidhi</s>), as that which produces the cognition of the other, is not produced by the word alone, since in cases such as 'the door' (<s>dvāram</s>) the relational cognition is seen [to occur] even by means of a supplied [word] 'cover' (<s>pidhāna</s>) and the like. And it should not be said that the word 'cover it' (<s>pidhehi</s>) itself is supplied, since [the word] is of no use; for it is the meaning alone that is of use, by being the counter-correlate of connection, and because [the meaning] is indispensable. [And this] because postulation from circumstance (<s>arthāpatti</s>) has as its object that which accounts for [the fact]. And it is not the mere word that is the accounter, but rather its meaning; since the recollection of a word fortuitously occasioned by fate, through its mere accompaniment of the meaning that must necessarily be postulated, is otherwise-established (<s>anyathāsiddha</s>); otherwise there would be the unwanted consequence of postulating a rule of power (<s>śakti</s>) that only a meaning conveyed by a word has the capacity to convey connection. If it be said: since words have as their import the connection of their own meaning, 'door' (<s>dvāram</s>) is not what conveys the connection of 'cover'; therefore, for the sake of conveying that connection, a word must necessarily be postulated — no. Because the secondary significations (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) would [then] deviate, and because, even on your view, the relational cognition [arises] from an [agent] elicited by implication. Now [it is held]: through lightness (<s>lāghava</s>), merely the co-presence of the word 'cover it' (<s>pidhehi</s>) with the word 'door' is postulated. And it should not be said that, when several words denoting 'cover' are presented, there is a lack of a deciding factor (<s>vinigamaka</s>), [for we reply] that, owing to the gradation of impressions (<s>saṃskāra-tāratamya</s>), there is the recollection of a particular word — no. Because it is already established that [a word] has as its import the connection of its own meaning with a correlate possessed of expectancy and the rest, [and] because through lightness there is the supplying of the meaning. And it should not be said that the words that were heard have already accomplished their purpose, so how, even when something is supplied, can their import (<s>tātparya</s>) [apply to it]? For, because the connection of the heard meaning would otherwise be unaccountable, in the supplied

children.text:
tātparyāt /
kathaṃ tarhyedanaṃ pacatītyatra samabhivyāhṛtamātrānvayaḥ kalāyāderapi smṛtatvāt iti cet /
na /
tātparyaniyamādityavehi yatparaḥ śabdaḥ sa hi śabdārthaḥ, anyathā tavāpi daivavaśasmṛtakalāyapadopasthāpitenānvayabodhaḥ syāt ayaṃ devadatta odanamityādivākye kriyāpadādhyāhārabhāvena kartturanabhidhānāt tṛtīyā syāt iti cet /
na /
adhyāhṛtapacatipadenāpi kartturanabhidhānāt, karttusaṃkhyābhihiteti cet /
na /
devadattasya pāka ityatrāpi tṛtīyāpatteḥ, tātparyatastacca vyavastheti cet, tulyam /
nanu dvāraṃ pidhehītyādau pidhānaśabdānubhave pidhānopasthāpakapadatvena janakatvamiti cet /
na /
anvayapratiyogyupasthāpakapadatvena janakatvāt na tu tadupasthāpakayāvatatpadatvena gauravāt /
evaṃ pidhānānvayabodhe 'pi /
children.translated_text: [The connection is established] from the purport (<s>tātparya</s>). 'Then how, in the sentence "he cooks rice" (<s>edanaṃ pacati</s>), is the connection merely from co-utterance (<s>samabhivyāhāra</s>), since pulse (<s>kalāya</s>) and the like are also remembered [as possible objects]?' — if so objected, no, because the connection is determined by purport (<s>tātparyaniyama</s>) —

children.text: anyathā gauṇa-lākṣaṇikayoranvayabodho na syāt tayorananubhāvakatvāditi //
children.translated_text: Otherwise, there would be no relational cognition (<s>anvayabodha</s>) in the case of figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>) and secondary (<s>lākṣaṇika</s>) [meanings], since those [words] are non-generative [of primary meaning]. //

children.text: āsattivādasiddhāntaḥ
children.translated_text: The established conclusion of the doctrine of contiguity (<s>Āsattivāda</s>)

children.text: ucyate, kriyāpadopasthāpitā kriyā, kārakapadopasthāpitañca kārakaṃ parasparamākāṅkṣati na tūpasthitimātraṃ anyathā dvāraṃ karmatā pidhehi, dvāraṃ pidhānaṃ kṛtirityatrāpi kriyā-karmādhyāhāra ivānvayabodhaprasaṅgaḥ
children.translated_text: It is said: an action presented by a verb-word and a case-factor (<s>kāraka</s>) presented by a case-word mutually expect each other — not merely their presentation [in the mind]; otherwise even a door-panel —

children.text:
kriyāyāḥ karmaṇaścopasthitestulyatvāt /
evaṃ vidhapadopasthāpite parasparamākāṅkṣā nastīti cet, tarhyākāṅkṣāyāṃ padaviśeṣopasthāpitatvaṃ tantraṃ na tūpasthitimātraṃ, arthaviśeṣe 'sādhutvānnātrānvayabodha iti cet, na, pidhehīti padaṃ vinā dvāramityasyāpyasādhutvāt tadarthayoge sādhutvasya tulyatvāt sādhutvajñānasyānvayabodhe 'prayojakatvācca gauravādapabhraṃśādapyanvayabodhācca /
na cātrāsaṃsargāgrahaḥ, bādhakābhāvāt /

tasmāt kriyā padasya kārakapadena kārakapadasya kriyāpadena sahānvayabodhakatvaṃ na tvekaṃ vinā tṛtīyānupapattiḥ, nahi kriyāpadārthayoge dvitīyā, ghaṭa ānayanaṃ kṛtirityatrāpi dvitīyāpatteḥ, tathā ca puṣpebhya ityatra spṛhayatipadādhyāhāraṃ vinā caturthyanupapattiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, a verb-word has the capacity to generate relational cognition (<s>anvayabodhakatva</s>) together with a case-word, and a case-word together with a verb-word — but not that without the one the third [i.e., the connection] would be impossible; for indeed —

children.text: yadi spṛhayati padārthayoge caturtho tadā puṣpamicchatītyatrāpi syāt spṛhayatīcchatipadayorekārthatvāt /
children.translated_text: If the fourth case [dative] applies when there is desire (<s>spṛhayati</s>) for connection with a word-meaning, then in '<s>puṣpam icchati</s>' ('he desires a flower') it should also [take the dative], since <s>spṛhayati</s> and <s>icchati</s> have the same meaning.

children.text: atha sādhutvārtha dvāraṃ puṣpebhya ityatra pidhehi-spṛhayatipadādhyāhāro 'numanyate na tvanvayabodhārthaṃ tasyānvayapratiyogivijñānādevopapatteriti cet, tarhi kriyāpadayogaṃ vinā na kārakavibhakiḥ, kārakapadayogaṃ vinā na tadanvayayogyaṃ kriyāpadamiti kevalakārakapade kriyāpadādhyāhāraḥ, kevalakriyāyāñca kārakapadādhyāhāraḥ sādhutvārthamāvaśyaka iti tajjanyopasthitiranvayabodhaupayiko tasmāt kriyā-kārakapadopasthāpitayoreva kriyā-kārakayoḥ parasparamanvaya iti śabdādhyāhāra eva /
children.translated_text: But for the purpose of grammatical correctness (<s>sādhutva</s>), in '<s>puṣpebhyaḥ</s>' ('for the flowers'), the ellipsis of the words '<s>pidhehi</s>' ('close') or '<s>spṛhayati</s>' ('desires') is admitted — not, however, for the purpose of relational cognition, since that is a hindrance to [direct] connection —

children.text: kartrākṣepe tu vakṣyāmaḥ //
children.translated_text: But regarding the implication of an agent, we shall discuss [this] later. //

Because the presentation of the action and of the object is of equal [status]. If it be objected that 'there is no mutual expectancy in [meanings] presented by words of this kind,' then in [the analysis of] expectancy, a word-specific [distinction] —
