children.text: tātparyavādaḥ
children.translated_text: The doctrine of purport (<s>Tātparyavāda</s>)

children.text:
tātparyadhīnaṃ śabdapramāṇyaṃ tatra tatparatvaṃ na tatsādhyakatvaṃ padārtha-tatsaṃsargayoḥ śabdāsādhyatvāt /
atha taṅgocarapravṛttinivṛttisādhyakatvaṃ tatparatvaṃ, tacca bhāvyārthasya sākṣāt bhūtārthasya tu praśaṃsā-nindāvākyasya praśastaninditārthapratipādanadvārā lākṣaṇikasya lakṣaṇīyaviṣayapravṛtti-nivṛttijanakatvaṃ tatparatvamiti cet, na, tatparatve tajjñānaṃ janayitvā tatra pravarttakatvaṃ tatpravarttakatvañca tatparatvamiti parasparāśrayāt /
lākṣaṇikasyānanubhāvakatve 'pi lakṣaṇīyaparatvāt kāvyādeḥ svarūpākhyānamātraparatvenāpi paryavasānāñca /
nanu tatbuddhijanakatvaṃ tatparatvaṃ praśaṃsā-nindāvākyamapi praśasta-ninditasvārthadhīhetutvena tatparameva, tacca jñānaṃ praśaste sarvaḥ pravartate ninditāñca nivartate iti svaviṣaye pravṛttinivṛttau janayatīti tatparamucyata iti cet /
na /
gauṇa-lākṣaṇikayoranubhāvakatvāt tadbuddhijanane tatparatvamityanyonyāśrayācca /
tajjananayogyatvamiti cet, tarhyekatroccāraṇe nānārthe nānārthaparatvaṃ lakṣaṇāyāñca mukhyārthaparatvaṃ syāt yogyatāyāḥ sattvāt /
nāpi tatpratipādyakatvaṃ, tātparyaṃ vinā na tathetyanyonyāśrayāt /
praśaṃsā-nindāvākyasya pravṛttyādyapratipādakatvāt lākṣaṇikasyāpratipādakatvācca /
atha gaṅgāpadaṃ svārthāvinābhāvi tīraṃ pratipādayattatparamiti cet /
na /
mañcāḥ krośantītyatra tena vināpi puruṣe tātparyāt gaṅgādipadaṃ matsyādiparaṃ mukhye tīraparañca syāt avinābhāvasya tādavasthyāt /
mukhye bādhake satīti cet, tarhi mukhyārthaparataiva na syāt na syācca gaccha gacchasītyatra gamanābhāvaparatvaṃ /
ucyate /
tatprayojanakatvaṃ tatparatvaṃ tadarthaśca pratītiḥ pravṛtti-nivṛttī ca, prayojanatvañca na sādhyatvaṃanyonyāśrayāt /
nāpi pratipādyecchāviṣayatvaṃ, yasya yadicchāviṣayaḥ taṃ pratitatparatvāpatteḥ /
tadarthasāthyatvena icchāniyama iti cet /
na /
iha dhūma ityatra janya-jñāpyabhedena sādhyasya bahu vidhatayā vākyabhedaprasaṅgāt pumicchayā niyantumaśakyatvāt, kintu pratipādakecchāviṣayatvaṃ tatparatvaṃ, yaḥ śabdaḥ vaktā yadicchayā prayuktaḥ sa tatparaḥ, sā cecchā
children.translated_text: The validity of verbal testimony (<s>śabdapramāṇya</s>) depends on purport (<s>tātparya</s>). There, 'having that as its object' (<s>tatparatva</s>) does not mean 'having that as what is to be established,' because the word-meaning and its connection are not established by the word [alone]. If it be said that [purport is] what is intended (<s>gocaratva</s>) —

children.text:
pratipādyadhī-pravṛtti-nivṛttiviṣayeti tatparatvaṃ /
nānārthāt śrliṣṭādanekapadārthānvitaikakriyāpadāt mukhyalākṣaṇikaparāccāvṛttyā krameṇānekapadārthajñānaṃ na tvekadaiva, sakṛduccaritasya sakṛdarthaparatvaniyamenaikatroccaraṇe anekārthaparatvābhāvāditi sakalatāntrikaikavākyatayā vadanti /
children.translated_text: [Purport is] the object toward which the cognition of what is to be conveyed (<s>pratipādya</s>) prompts activity or cessation. From a word having multiple meanings, from a single verb-word connected with multiple case-meanings expressed in a compound, [the connection of] primary and secondary meaning —

children.text:
vayantu brūmaḥ /
anākapadārthapratītīcchayā ekamuccāraṇaṃ bhavatyeva pumicchāyāniyantumaśakyatvāt /
yadi ca taduccāraṇaṃ nānekārthaparaṃ tadāvṛttirapi na syāt tātparyanirvāhārthamātravṛttikalpanāt /
anyathaikapare 'pi tadāpatteḥ /
ata eva taduccāraṇasya ubhayaparatāyāṃ nāvṛttikalpaṇaṃ tasmāttulyavadanekārthopasthitau tātparyādijñāne yugapadanekānvayabodho bhavati sāmagrayāstulyatvāt prathamamekasyānvayabodho na tadanyasyeti niyantumaśakyatvacca /
atha vivādadhyāsitamakṣapadoccāraṇaṃ ekapadaikaśaktiviṣayamekamevānubhāvati ekatroccāraṇe nānāśaktyā nānārthānanubhāvakaṃ nānārthatvāt ekaparanānārthapadavaditi cet /
na /
anekārthānubhavasāmargrīvasattvena bādhitatvāt sāmagrīrahasyopādhitvācca /
ata evākṣamānayetyukte bhinnaprakaraṇādinā bhinne tātparyapramāyāṃ bhrame vā pratipādyayorekadaivāvṛttiṃ vinānekārthapratītirna tu tatraiko vilambate, evaṃ ghaṭaṃ paṭaṃ vā ānayetyatrānayanasyobhayaparatve ekadaivānvayabodho natvāvṛttiḥ vākyabhedastvarthabhedāt na jñānabhedāt /
gaṅgāyāṃ jalaṃ ghoṣaśca prativasatītyatra gaṅgāpadasya yugapatpravāha-tīrayostātparyagrahe tayordvayorapyekadopesthitau jala-ghoṣayorekadaivānvayabodhaḥ /
na ca yugapadvṛttidvayāpattiḥ, iṣṭatvāt, tātparyādvi vṛttiḥ, na tu vṛttyanurodhāt tātparyaṃ, gauṇalākṣaṇikayorucchedāpatteḥ tātparyanirvāharthaṃ vṛttitvena tayoḥ kalpanāt /
mukhya-lākṣiṇikayorekaikamātraparatve tu yugapadvṛttidvayavirodhaḥ /
anekānvayabodhaparatve vṛttidvayavirodhasya doṣatve paribhāṣāpatteḥ, yatra mukhyārthe śīghratvena prathamamanvayabodhaḥ anantaraṃ lākṣaṇikānvayabodhaḥ tatrāvṛttireva tasmāt yugapattātparyagrahe sati nāvṛttiḥ kintvanekārthaparatve satyeva yatra tātparyagrahakamādanvayabodhakramaḥ tatrāvṛttiḥ prathamoccāraṇasya paryavasitatvāditi /
evañca loke kḷptatvāt vede 'podaṃ tātparyamiti tasya pauruṣeyatvam /
children.translated_text: We, however, say: There is indeed a single utterance with the desire for the cognition of multiple word-meanings, since one cannot control a person's desire. And if that utterance is not directed toward multiple meanings, then there would be no repetition either, since repetition is postulated only for the sake of fulfilling the purport (<s>tātparya</s>). Otherwise, that consequence would follow even when directed toward a single [meaning]. For this very reason, when that utterance is directed toward both [meanings], there is no postulation of repetition. Therefore, when there is simultaneous presentation of multiple meanings, as in an equal [case], and when there is cognition of the purport and so forth, there is simultaneous cognition of multiple connections (<s>anvayabodha</s>), because the totality of conditions is equal, and because it cannot be controlled [to say] that there is first the cognition of the connection of one and not of the other. Now, if [it is objected that] the utterance of <s>Akṣapāda</s> [<s>Gautama</s>], which is the locus of dispute, produces only one [meaning] that is the object of one word's one denotative power, and that a single utterance does not produce multiple meanings through multiple denotative powers because of the multiplicity of meanings, like a word directed toward one meaning among multiple meanings—no. Because this is contradicted by the presence of all the conditions for the experience of multiple meanings, and because [the proposed restriction] would be a condition [that is merely] a secret of the totality of conditions. For this very reason, when 'bring the eye-salve' is said, if the purport-cognition regarding the two things to be conveyed is different due to different contexts and so forth, or there is error, then without repeating [the word] even once, there is the cognition of multiple meanings, but one [meaning] does not linger there. Similarly, in 'bring the pot or the cloth,' when 'bringing' is directed toward both, there is simultaneous cognition of the connection, not repetition. The distinction of sentences is due to the distinction of meanings, not the distinction of cognitions. In 'water and the cowherd dwell on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,' when the purport of the word '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' is simultaneously grasped as referring to both the stream and the bank, and when both are simultaneously presented, there is simultaneous cognition of the connection of 'water' and 'cowherd' [with their respective meanings]. Nor is there the undesirable consequence of two simultaneous denotative functions, since it is accepted; the denotative function follows from the purport, not the purport from the denotative function, because there would follow the destruction of secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>) and indicatory (<s>lākṣaṇika</s>) [meanings], since the postulation of those two as denotative functions is for the sake of fulfilling the purport. But when the primary and indicatory [meanings] are each directed toward one meaning only, then there is a contradiction of two simultaneous denotative functions. When directed toward the cognition of multiple connections, if the contradiction of two denotative functions is considered a defect, there would follow a restriction. Where the cognition of the primary meaning occurs first due to its rapidity, and then the cognition of the indicatory connection follows, there is indeed repetition. Therefore, when there is simultaneous apprehension of the purport, there is no repetition; rather, repetition occurs only when there is a directed-toward-multiple-meanings state and a sequential order of cognitions of the connection based on what produces the purport-apprehension, because the first utterance has been exhausted. And thus, since [the purport] is established [by convention] in ordinary usage, the purport in the <s>Veda</s> is unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>); therefore [the <s>Veda</s>] has personal authorship (<s>pauruṣeyatva</s>).

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 340)
children.translated_text: (Bibliotheca Indica 98, IV,1, p. 340)

children.text:
atra mīmāṃsakāḥ yathoccāraṇapūrvatvāt uccāraṇaṃ vede paratantraṃ tathā tātparyamapi tātparyapūrvakameveti paratantraṃ na tu kasyāpi prathamaṃ tātparyaṃ anāditvāt pūrvapūrvavākyārthajñānecchayoccāraṇamupajīvyāgrimasya tadicchayoccāraṇāt tadicchayā taduccāraṇameva hi tatparatvaṃ loka-vedasādhāraṇaṃ, sā cecchā svatantrā paratantrā veti na kaścidviśeṣaḥ, tadavadhāraṇāñcānādimīmāṃsāpariśodhitanyāyādveda ityubhayavādisiddhaṃ, atastātparyānurodhena vedasya na pauruṣeyatvam /
nanvarthajñānaṃ vinoccaritavedāt kathamarthayoḥ vākyārthajñānaṃ vinā tadicchayoccāraṇābhāvāt, pratipuruṣamuccāraṇabhedāditi cet, tarhi paṭhyamānabhāratādapi tathābhūtādarthadhīrna syāt vyāsena yatpratītīcchayā uccāraṇaṃ kṛtaṃ tajjātīyatvāt arthajñānaṃ vināpi paṭhyamānabhāratārthadhīriti cet, tarhi vede 'pi tulya, tattātparyakajātīyatvasya niyāmakatvāt anyathā paṭhyamānavedāttavāpyarthadhīrna syāt īśvarāpraṇītatvāt /
atha vedaḥ pauruṣeyaḥ vākyatvāt bhāratādivat iti cet, ko vedaḥ, anugatadharmābhāvena tasya śākhāsu nānārthatvāt, tathāhi na mukhyavedapaprayogaviṣayovedaḥ mukhyārthākathanāt /
nāpi śākhāsamudāyaḥ, tasya vedanirūpyatvāt samudāyasyāpratipādakatvena vākyatvāsiddheśca /
nāpi svargakāmādivākyaṃ, smṛti-bhāratāderapi tathātvāt /
children.translated_text: Here the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> [say]: Just as utterance, being preceded by [prior] utterance, is dependent [on a tradition] in the case of the <s>Veda</s>, so too purport, being preceded by purport, is dependent—there is no one's purport that is first, since [the process] is beginningless: the utterance of the prior person is made with the desire for knowledge of the meaning of prior sentences, and the utterance of the next person is made with that [same] desire. That very utterance made with that desire is indeed what constitutes being directed toward that [meaning]—[and this is] common to both ordinary usage and the <s>Veda</s>. Whether that desire is independent or dependent makes no difference. And the ascertainment of that [purport] is from the canons purified by beginningless <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>—'this is the <s>Veda</s>'—and this is accepted by both sides. Therefore, on account of the purport, the <s>Veda</s> does not have personal authorship. But if [it is objected that] without the knowledge of the meaning, how can there be knowledge of the sentence-meaning from the uttered <s>Veda</s>, since in the absence of the desire for that [i.e., to convey meaning] there would be no utterance, and since the utterance differs for each person—if so objected, then from the recited <s>Bhārata</s> too, which is of the same kind, there would be no cognition of meaning. If [it is claimed that] since [the <s>Bhārata</s>] is of the same kind as that which <s>Vyāsa</s> uttered with the desire for cognition, there is cognition of meaning even without [the hearer's own] knowledge of the meaning—then the same applies to the <s>Veda</s>, since being of the same kind as [that which has] that purport is what determines [meaning]. Otherwise, even from the recited <s>Veda</s>, there would be no cognition of meaning for you, since it was not composed by <s>Īśvara</s> (God). Now if [it is argued that] the <s>Veda</s> is of personal authorship because it is a sentence, like the <s>Bhārata</s> and so forth—what is the <s>Veda</s>? Since there is no common property [to define it], and since the branches (<s>śākhās</s>) have diverse meanings. For the <s>Veda</s> that is the subject of the primary usage of the word 'Veda' does not [exist as a unity], since its primary meaning is not stated. Nor is it the collection of branches, since that is determined by [what counts as] the <s>Veda</s>, and since the collection is not an expressive [entity], and hence the sentence-hood [of the <s>Veda</s>] is unestablished. Nor is it a sentence like 'one who desires heaven [should perform the sacrifice],' since <s>smṛti</s>, the <s>Bhārata</s>, and so forth are also of that kind.

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 344)
children.translated_text: (Bibliotheca Indica 98, IV,1, p. 344)

children.text:
nāpi sandigdhakartṛkavākyaṃ, vādinorniścayāt, /
vādyanumānayostulyatvena madhyasthasya saṃśaya iti cet, tarhyanumānābhyāṃ tasya saṃśayomadhyasthasaṃśayapraśrnānantarañcānumānamityanyonyāśrayaḥ /
nāpi vivādādhyāsitaṃ vākyaṃ, anugatadharmaṃ vinā vivādasyāpyabhāvāt bhāratādāvapi tatsamāvāñca /
nāpi mahānajanānāṃ vedākārānugatavyavahārāt vedatvaṃ jātiḥ, devadattīyatvādyanumāpakaśabdavṛttijātibhiḥ saṅkaraprasaṅgāt /
kiñca pauruṣeyatvaṃ na tadarthadhījanyatvaṃ taduccāraṇadhīprabhavatvaṃ vā, adhyāpaka-tadubhayadhījanyatvena siddhasādhanāt /
nāpyuccāraṇasya sāditvaṃ, pratyuccāraṇasya sāditvāt /
nāpi svatantrapuruṣapraṇītatvaṃ, paṭhyamānavedabhāratayostadabhāvāt /
tajjātīyaḥ svatantrapuruṣapraṇīta iti cet, tarhi paṭhyamānabhārataṃ vyāsasya na mameti kathaṃ syāt, svātantryañca yadyuccāraṇavyaktau tadā mamāpyuccāraṇasamānye na vyāsasyāpi /
kiñca svatantrapuruṣapraṇītajātīyatvaṃ yadi sādhyate tadādyabhārate smṛtau ca vākyatvamanaikāntikaṃ, na hi tajjātīyaṃ svatantrapuruṣapraṇītamiti sādhyamanirdhāritaviśeṣaṃ jīvī kvacidastīti vaditi cet /
children.translated_text: Nor is it 'a sentence whose author is in doubt,' since the disputant is certain [about authorship]. If [it is said that] the two sides are equal as between the proponent and the inference, and the neutral party has doubt—then by the two inferences, his doubt [would arise], and since the inference follows immediately after the neutral party's doubt has arisen, there is mutual dependence. Nor is it 'the sentence that is the locus of dispute,' since without a common property there would be no dispute either, and since the same [conditions] obtain in the <s>Bhārata</s> as well. Nor is Veda-hood a universal (<s>jāti</s>), established by the usage of great persons consistent with the form of the <s>Veda</s>—because there would follow a conflation with the word-denotation universals that indicate [things like] 'belonging to <s>Devadatta</s>' and so forth. Moreover, personal authorship (<s>pauruṣeyatva</s>) is not 'being produced by a cognition of that meaning,' nor 'being originated by a cognition of that utterance,' since [the <s>Veda</s>] is produced by the cognition of a teacher or of both [teacher and student], and [hence the proof] would be one whose probandum is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>). Nor is it 'the having-a-beginning of the utterance,' since each instance of utterance has a beginning. Nor is it 'being composed by an independent person,' since in the case of the recited <s>Veda</s> and <s>Bhārata</s>, that [independent authorship] is absent [in the reciter]. If [it is claimed to be] 'of the same kind as [that which was] composed by an independent person'—then how would the recited <s>Bhārata</s> be '<s>Vyāsa</s>'s and not mine'? And if independence pertains to the particular utterance [instance], then [the utterance] belongs to me too; in the universal [class of utterances], it does not belong to <s>Vyāsa</s> either. Moreover, if 'being of the same kind as composed by an independent person' is what is to be proved, then in the original <s>Bhārata</s> and in <s>smṛti</s>, the reason 'sentence-hood' would be inconclusive. For [the objection that] the probandum—'that which is of the same kind is composed by an independent person'—is one whose particular [instance] is undetermined, like 'there exists a living being somewhere'—if so objected,

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 348)
children.translated_text: (Bibliotheca Indica 98, IV,1, p. 348)

children.text:
na /
paṭhyamānabhārate vyabhicārāt /
athārthaṃ pratītya tadarthaparatayā pratisandhīyamānapadatvaṃ pauruṣeyatvaṃ tasya prathamamāvaśyakatvāt, ata evānuccārito 'pi sau mauniśrlokaḥ pauruṣeya iti cet /
na /
arthajñānavatādhyapakena siddhasādhanāt, anyathā paṭhyamānaveda-bhāratābhyāṃ vyabhicārāt /
ata eva vedatvaṃ svatantrapuruṣapraṇītavṛtti vākyavṛttidharmatvāt bhāratatvavaditi nirastam /
svatantrapraṇītatvaṃ hi vākyārthagocarayathārthajñānacikhyāpayiṣayoccaraṇaṃ tathā ca
children.translated_text: No. Because there is deviation in the recited <s>Bhārata</s>. Now if [it is claimed that] personal authorship is 'having words that are reconnected with the intention of conveying that meaning after having cognized the meaning,' since that is necessary in the first [instance], and for this very reason even an unspoken verse by a silent sage is of personal authorship—no. Because [the proof] would be one whose probandum is already established, since a teacher who knows the meaning [also has this property]; otherwise, there would be deviation in the recited <s>Veda</s> and <s>Bhārata</s>. For this very reason, [the argument that] 'Veda-hood is a property of the denotative function of sentences composed by an independent person, because it is a property of denotative function, like the property of being a <s>Bhārata</s>'—is refuted. For 'being independently composed' is 'utterance with the desire to convey veridical cognition regarding the sentence-meaning,' and thus

children.text:
tathāvidhādhyāpakena siddhasādhanam /
etena vaktṛtvānuvaktṛtvayorbhedasya lokasiddhatvāt savaktṛkatvaṃ sādhyamiti nirastaṃ /
nāpi sajātīyayoccāṇānapekṣoccāraṇaṃ pauruṣeyatvaṃ paṭhyamānavede bādhāt bhārate vyabhicārāt /
ucyate, śabda-tadupajīvipramāṇātirikapramāṇajanyapramityaviṣayārthakatve sati śabdajanyavākyārthajñānajanyapramāṇaśabdatvaṃ vedatvam, īśvarīyapramāyāḥ ajanyatvāt, vedārthasyānumānādiviṣayatve 'pi anumānādervedopajīvakatvāt /
children.translated_text: [the proof] would be one whose probandum is already established through such a teacher. By this, [the argument that] 'since the difference between an original speaker and a repeater is well-established in the world, what is to be proved is that [the <s>Veda</s>] has an original speaker'—is refuted. Nor is personal authorship 'utterance not dependent on a prior utterance of the same kind,' due to contradiction in the recited <s>Veda</s> and deviation in the <s>Bhārata</s>. It is said: <s>Veda</s>-hood is: being a word (<s>śabda</s>) that produces sentential cognition productive of valid cognition, whose content is not the object of valid cognition other than verbal testimony and [<s>pramāṇas</s>] dependent on it—[this is <s>Veda</s>-hood]—since <s>Īśvara</s>'s (God's) valid cognition is unproduced [and hence the <s>Veda</s> does not require a prior personal author]; and even though the Vedic content may be the object of inference and the like, inference and the like are dependent on the <s>Veda</s> [in this domain].

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 364)
children.translated_text: (Bibliotheca Indica 98, IV,1, p. 364)

children.text:
smṛtīnāṃ bhāratādibhāgasya ca vedasamānārthakatve 'pi śabdajanyadhījanyatvāt vedārthaṃ pratītya tat praṇayanāt /
sajātīyoccāraṇanapekṣoccāritajātīyatvaṃ pauruṣeyatvaṃ, ādyabhārate 'pi tajjatīyatvānna vyabhicāraḥ /
athavā vedatvaṃ sajītīyoccāṇānapekṣoccaritavṛtti pramāṇatāvacchedakavākyavṛttidharmatvāt smṛtitvavat /
yadvā vedāḥ śabdājanyavākyārthagocarayathārthajñānajanyāḥ pramāṇaśabdatvāt bhāratavat /
na ca paṭhyamāne vede bādhaḥ bhārate manvādismṛtau ca vyabhicāraḥ teṣāṃ dvikartṛkatvāt tādṛśajñānajanyajātīyatvaṃ vā sādhyaṃ, tavāpyetadabhāvādeva vede 'pauruṣeyatvavyavahāraḥ /
nanvaprayojakamidaṃ vākyārthagocarayathārthajñānapūrvakatvameva śabdapramāṇye tantraṃ na tu tādṛśajñānasya śabdājanyatvamapi gauravāt , anyathā vede 'pi tava dvikartṛkatvena pramāṇyaṃ syāt loke tathā darśanāt, evañca anādimīmāṃsāsiddhanyāyenāvagatatātparyāt vedārthaṃ pratītya pūrvapūrvādhyapakena uccaritādvedaduttarottarasyāpyadhyayanatadarthapratītirityanāditaivātaḥ kiṃ svatantrapuruṣeṇa tatprayojanasya paratantrādeva siddheḥ /
kiñca pūrvakalo na vedaśūnya ityuddeśyapratīterasiddheḥ nāṃśataḥ siddhasādhanaṃ, tathā pūrvakālīnaṃ vedādhyayanaṃ gurvadhyayanapūrvakaṃ adhyayanatvāt idānīntanādhyāyanavat /
na ca lipyanumitavedādhyayanena vyabhicāraḥ, liperadhyayanapūrvakatvāt /
na caivaṃ bhāratādhyayanamapi tathā syāt, tasya bhāratādāveva vyāsādikartṛkatvena kathanāditi /
ucyate /
vedaprāmāṇyādhīnaṃ tatprāmāṇyamityatmāśrayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Although the <s>Smṛtis</s> and sections of the <s>Bhārata</s> (Mahābhārata) have the same meaning as the <s>Veda</s>, [they are authoritative] because they are produced by cognition generated by the word [of the <s>Veda</s>], and because they were composed having apprehended the meaning of the <s>Veda</s>. Of the same kind —

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 369)
children.translated_text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 369)

children.text:
na ca pūrvavedaprāmāṇyādhīnamuttaravedapramāṇyamiti vyaktibhedamādāya nātmāśraya iti vācyam /
evaṃ tatpūrvasyāpi tatpūrvaprāmāṇyāt prāmāṇyamityanavasthānāt /
anāditvādayamadoṣa iti cet /
na /
mūlabhūtapramāṇāntarābhāvāt andhaparamparāpātāt /
svataḥ pramāṇaṃ veda eva sarvatra vede mūlamiti cet /
na /
sarveṣāmeva paravedāpekṣatvena svataḥ pramāṇatvābhāvāt /
ata evācārāt smṛtiḥ smṛterācāra ityatra viśvāsavījaparānapekṣamūlabhūtapramāṇābhāvādandhaparamparābhayena tatra vedamūlakatvakalpanā /
anādimahājanaparigrahādanādivedapravāhaprāmāṇyāvadhāraṇe 'pi tannirvāhaketarānapekṣamūlabhūtapramāṇābhāvenānāśvāsa eva anyathā smṛtyācārayorapyevaṃ pramāṇaṇyāvadhāraṇe pramāṇamūlakatvakalpanā na syāt /
tasmādāśvāsavījaparānapekṣeśvarapratyakṣamūlakatvādeva vedasya prāmāṇyaṃ mahājanaprarigrahādavadharyate /
etenānumānamapi nirastam /
mūlabhūtapratyakṣaṃ vinā vedaprāmāṇyānupapattyā sādhyābhāvasiddhau bādhāt /
children.translated_text: And it should not be said that the validity of a later <s>Veda</s> depends on the validity of an earlier <s>Veda</s> and hence, taking into account the difference of instances, there is no self-dependence (<s>ātmāśraya</s>). For in the same way, [the validity of] the one prior to that also [would depend on] the one prior to that —

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 371)
children.translated_text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 371)

children.text:
nanu vedo na pauruṣeyaḥ asmaryamāṇakartṛkatvāditi bādhakamastviti cet /
na /
kapila-kaṇāda-gautamaistacchiṣyaiścādyaparyantaṃ vede sakartṛkatvasmaraṇasya pratīyamānatvāt /
na ca mūlabhūtānubhavābhāvāt smaraṇānupapattiḥ, pauruṣeyatvānumānādevānubhavāt /
asmaraṇameva tatra bādhakamiti cet /
na /
evaṃ satyasmaraṇānanubhavayoranyonyāśrayāt /
children.translated_text: Objection: 'The <s>Veda</s> is not of human authorship (<s>apauruṣeya</s>), because its author is not remembered' — let this be the defeating argument (<s>bādhaka</s>). No. Because <s>Kapila</s>, <s>Kaṇāda</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, and their disciples up to the present day —

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 372)
children.translated_text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 372)

children.text:
agre tadarthasmaraṇābhāve 'pi pramāṇasyānubhāvakam /
''tasmāttapastepānāccatvāro vedā ajāyanta ṛcaḥ sāmāni jajñire'' iti kartṛśravaṇāt ``pratimanvantarañcaiṣā śrutiranyā vidhīyate'' ityādikartṛsmaraṇācca /
pauruṣeyatve bādhakaṃ vinā arthavādamātratvasya vaktṛmaśakyatvāt /
''svayambhūreṣa bhagavān vedo gītastvayā purā /
śivādyā ṛṣiparyantāḥ smarttāro 'sya na kārakāḥ'' iti mahābhāgavatapurāṇīyavākyasya śrutivirodhenānyacca tātparyāt /
na ca kāryaparameva pramāṇaṃ, kartṛsmaraṇasya sarvatrāvidhyarthatvāt sakartṛkatvārthavādasya svarga-narakārthavādasyeva ``īśvaramupāsīta'' iti vidhiśeṣatvācca /
sādhayiṣyate siddhārthasya prāmāṇyam /
na caivamānando 'pīśvare syāditi vācyam /
tatra mānāntaravirodhāt /
puruṣasya bhrama-pramādādibhūyiṣṭhatvena vede nāśvāsa iti cet /
na / dharmigrāhakamānena nityasarvajñatvena siddhe tatra doṣābhāvāditi /
children.translated_text: Even in the absence of subsequent recollection of its meaning, [there is] a <s>pramāṇa</s> that can produce [the cognition]. 'Therefore from <s>tapas</s> (austerity) having been performed, the four <s>Vedas</s> arose; the <s>Ṛk</s> verses and the <s>Sāman</s> chants were born' — thus [the Śruti itself states].

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 375)
children.translated_text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,1, p. 375)

children.text: śabdanityatāvādapūrvapakṣaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) of the doctrine of the eternality of words (<s>Śabdanityatāvāda</s>)

children.text:
nanu tathāpyaprayojakaṃ pauruṣeyatvānumānaṃ nityanirdeṣatvenaiva tatprāmāṇyopapatteriti cet /
na /
varṇānāṃ anityatvena tatsamūhasya sutarāmanityatvāt /
na ca tadasiddhaṃ, tathāhi varṇātmakaḥ śabdo 'nityaḥ samavetatve satyutpattimattvāt ghaṭavat /
na ca hetvasiddhiḥ, utpanno gakāraḥ haṭṭāyāmutpadyamāno 'sti kolāhala iti pratyayāt /
na ca vyañjakābhāvāt prāganupalabdhasyopalabdhimātraṃ tasya, utpanno gakāra iti pratyayāt /
na cāyamaupādhikaḥ, anyotpattāvagṛhyamāṇāyāmapi tadanubhavāt /
na ca smaryamāṇāropaḥ, bādhakābhāvāt /
anyathā ghaṭotpattirapi na siddhyet /
children.translated_text: Objection: 'Even so, the inference of human authorship (<s>pauruṣeyatva</s>) is inconclusive, because the validity [of the <s>Veda</s>] can be explained by its very eternality of utterance (<s>nityanirdeṣatva</s>).' No. Because of the non-eternality (<s>anityatva</s>) of phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>) —

children.text:
yattu śrotrānuvidhānāt padaṃ śṛṇomītyabādhitānuvyavasāyāt śrotrādanyena grahītumaśakyatvāñca śrotragrāhyaivānupūrvī sā ca dhamamānakālīnaprāgabhāvapratiyogitvaṃ ṭasyeti prāgabhāvapratiyogitvamutpattimattvaṃ varṇasya pratyakṣamiti, tanna, ghajñānānantarajñānaviṣayatva ṭasyānantaryaṃ tayorānupūrvī sā ca manasaiva gṛhyate ghaṭapaṭajñānayoriva /
tadupanītā ca śrotraviṣayaḥ /
nanu sa evāyaṃ gakāra iti pratyabhijñābādhitamidamityekaikā eva gakārādivyaktayaḥ /
yadyapi pratyabhijñāyāṃ nityatvaṃ na viṣayastathāpi nāśakatvābhimataśabdāntarādīnāṃ antarāsambhave 'pi tāvat kālīnatāṃ gakārasya gṛhṇātīti ``tāvatkālaṃ sthirañcainaṃ kaḥ paścānnāśayiṣyatīti parābhimatāśuvināśitvatirekānnityatāyāmeva paryavasyati /
na ca dharmiṇo gakārasya bhede 'pi ekajātīyatvena pratyabhijñā, tathā sati tajjātīyopamitiḥ syānna tu sa evāyamiti /
atha tāratva-mandatva-viruddhadharmādhyastaviṣayatvena sā na pramāṇam /
na ca tāratvādīnāṃ svābhāvikatvaṃ viruddhatvañcāsiddhaṃ, mandastāro gakārastārānmando 'nya ityananyathāsiddhapratyakṣāt tatsiddheḥ /
na hyapāṃ śaitya-dravatve svābhāvike ityatra pratyakṣādanyat pramāṇam /
tat kiṃ yo yadgatatvena bhāsate sa taddharma eva tathā sati raktaḥ paṭaḥ lohitaḥ sphaṭikaḥ ityādāvapi tathā syādaviśeṣāt, na, raktatvādīnāmanyadharmatvasthitau sphaṭikādīnāñca tadviruddhadharmatve sthite japākusumāderanvaya - vyatirekānuvidhānād bādhena tatra bhrāntatvāt /
na ceha tāratvāderanyadharmatvenopasthitiḥ /
nāpi gakārādīnāṃ tadviruddhadharmavattvam, nāpyanyasya tāratvādidharmaṇo 'nuvidhānam /
na cāvaśyaṃ svīkṛtavāyoreva dharmāstāratvādayogakārādigatatvena bhāsante iti vācyam /
sparśāgrahe tvaco vyāpārābhāvena tvacā tadagrahāt /
na ca śravasā tadgahaḥ, avāyavīyatvena vāyumātradharmāgrāhakatvāccakṣurvat /
tāratvādayo vā na vāyudharmāḥ śravaṇatvāt kādivāt, vāyurvā na śravaṇamātragrāhyadharmomūrttatvāt paṭavat, ata eva na tāratvādayo vāyudharmadhvanidharmāḥ vāyudharmasya dhvaneragrahāt /
na ca dhvanirūpaḥ śabdo nabhovṛttireva tathā sati taddharmatāratvādigrahaḥ śravaseti vācyam /
tāro 'yaṃ gakāra ityatra dhyanīnāmasphuraṇaṃ, tatkāraṇābhāvācca /
na ca vyaktyā vinā jātisphuraṇaṃ, tasyā vyaktisamānasaṃvit saṃvedyatvāt /
na ca smaryamāṇatāratvādyāropaḥ, bādhakābhāvāt prathamatastāratvādyagrahaprasaṅgācceti /
maivaṃ /
tāratvādayo na gakārādijātayaḥ gatvādinā saṅkaraprasaṅgāt /
na ca nānaiva tāratvaṃ, tārākarānugatapratyayābhāvaprasaṅgāt /
na ca sajātīyasākṣātkārapratibandhakatāvacchedakaśabdavṛttijātitvena nānātaratveṣṭhanugamaḥ, tadapratisandhāne 'pi tāratvānugatapratyayāt /
tāratva-mandatve ca na śabdavṛttijātī sapratiyogikatvāt /
nāpi tāratva-mandatvayorvirodhaḥ, ya eva gakārastāra āsīt sa evedānīṃ manda iti samayabhedena vaktṛbhedena ca tayorekatvapratīteḥ /
tāro 'yaṃ na tāratarastārānmando 'nya iti bhedapratītirastīti cet na, dharmiṇo 'bhede bhāsamāne viśiṣṭadharmibhedapratīterdharmabhedaviṣayatvāt /
ekatra ghaṭe lohito 'yaṃ na śyāmaidānīmiti pratītivat /
na ca tīvreṇa gakāreṇa mandagakārābhibhāvāt tayorbhedaḥ na hi tadeva tadabhibhāvakaṃ,tasyaiva tenaiva tadaiva grahaṇāgrahaṇayorvirodhāt iti vācyam /
tāratvavyañjakavāyorbalavattvena mandatvavyañjakavāyvabhibhāvāt mandatvasyāgrahaṇāt /
santu vā tāra-mandarūpādayobhinnā eva gakārāstatpratyayabhijñāne bādhakābhāvāt / tasmāt vāyudharmā eva tāratvādayaḥ śabdagatatvena bhāsante darpaṇadharmā iva sukhādau tadgrahaṇañca sparśapuraskāreṇa karṇaśaṣkulītvagindriyeṇa tāra-mandajanakavāyūnaṃ tvayāpyutkarṣāpakarṣasyodbhūtasparśasya ca svīkārāt śrotreṇaiva vā / cakṣurāderyanna vāyudharmagrahastatrāyogyatvamupādhiḥ, anyathā śrotreṇa svaguṇo na gṛhyeta indriye tathā darśanāt, cakṣurvā na pārthivarūpagrāhakaṃ apārthivendriyatvāt rasanavat ityadyapi syāt /
atha yogyo yogyena gṛhyate svaguṇaḥ paraguraṇo vā, yogyatā ca phalabalena kalpate, tarhi śrotrasyāpi vāyudharmagrahe tulyam /
na ca tāro gakāra ityatra vāyorapratītiḥ, vāyutvenāpratītāvapi tāratvādinaiva tatpratīteḥ, yathā agnitvenapratītāvapi ayogolake lohita iti pratītiḥ /
nanu vāyu-śabdayostvacā śrotreṇa vā grahe kena tāro 'yaṃ gakāraityāropa iti cet, na, ubhayendriyagrāhyayorasaṃsargāgrahāt saṃsargavyavahāraḥ /
astu vā tvagindriyopanītasya śrotreṇāropaḥ śrotreṇaiva vā tāratvagraho 'pītyuktaṃ, utpattimattvañcāsiddhaṃ tatpratīteḥ śrutapūrvo 'yaṃ gakāra iti pratyabhijñānabādhitatvāt /
nanu pratyabhijñaiva tayā bādhitā gatvajātyaupadhiko 'bhedapratyayo gakāre sambhavatītyuktamiti cet, na, gatvajāterasiddheḥ bhede bhāsamāne hyabhedapratītirjātimālambate /
na ca gakārabhedapratītirasti, tāratva-mandatve api na bhedahetū ya eva tāraḥ sa evedānīṃ manda iti pratyabhijñānāt, gakārānityatve 'pi tathā sambhavatīti cet, tarhi nityatve 'pi karṇaśaṣkulītvagindriyopanītavāyudharmotpatterupādhitvaṃ sambhavati /
na ca vāyorapratītiḥ, utpannatvenaiva tatpratīteḥ lohitatveneva japākusumasya sphaṭike /
children.translated_text: As for the argument that the sequential order (<s>ānupūrvī</s>) [of phonemes] is grasped by the ear, since it follows the ear's operation, since the judgment 'I hear a word' is uncontradicted, and since it cannot be grasped by any sense other than the ear — and that sequential order is the prior-absence-counterpositive-hood of the phoneme ṭa with respect to the moment of the phoneme dha being sounded, so that the prior-absence-counterpositive-hood, which entails being produced, is perceptible for the phoneme — this is not so. The sequentiality of ṭa, namely its being the object of the cognition immediately following the cognition of gha, and the sequential order of the two — these are grasped by the mind alone, just as [the order of] the cognitions of pot and cloth. And what is presented thereby has the ear as its object. Now, if [the opponent says] 'this is the very same ga-phoneme' — this [recognition] contradicts the claim, so there are only individual instances of the ga-phoneme and so forth. Even though in recognition the eternality is not the object [of the cognition], nonetheless, since when the allegedly destructive other sounds and such are absent, [the recognition] grasps the ga-phoneme as persisting for that duration — 'who will destroy this that is stable for that duration?' — this terminates in eternality alone, by exceeding the opponent's view of momentary destruction. Nor is the recognition based on the ga-phoneme being of one kind even though the substrate is different, for in that case there would be a comparative judgment 'similar to that kind,' not 'this is the very same one.' If it is objected that the recognition is not a valid means of knowledge because its object contains superimposed contradictory properties — sharpness and softness — then: neither is the natural status of sharpness and such established, nor is their being contradictory established, since from the perception 'the soft ga-phoneme is different from the sharp one' — which is not otherwise accountable — both are established. For there is no other <s>pramāṇa</s> than perception for [the claim that] the coldness and fluidity of water are natural. Then what — does that which appears as residing in something possess that as its property? If so, then in 'the red cloth, the red crystal' and similar cases, it should be so as well, without distinction. No, because when the status of redness and such as properties of something else is established, and when the status of crystal and such as possessing properties contradictory to that is established, from the concordance and discordance with the <s>japā</s> flower and such, the [attribution of redness to the crystal] is erroneous due to being contradicted. But here, neither is there a presentation of sharpness and such as properties of something else, nor is there [any evidence] that the ga-phoneme and such possess properties contradictory to those, nor is there concordance with any other [entity] possessing sharpness and such as its property. Nor should it be said that the properties of sharpness and such necessarily belong to air that has been accepted [as their substrate], and merely appear as residing in the ga-phoneme and such — because since the skin does not function in the absence of touch-perception, the skin does not perceive them; and the ear does not perceive them either, since, being non-composite, it cannot grasp only air-properties, just as the eye [cannot grasp air-properties]. Alternatively, sharpness and such are not air-properties, because they are audible — like the phoneme ka and such. Or, air is not a property grasped only by hearing, because it is corporeal — like cloth. Hence, sharpness and such are not properties of air or of sound [as air's property], since air-property sound is not [itself] grasped. Nor should it be said that sound, whose nature is resonance, is precisely an occurrence in ether — for in that case, its property sharpness and such would be grasped by the ear — because in 'this ga-phoneme is sharp,' there is no manifestation of resonance, and there is no cause for such [manifestation]. Nor is there manifestation of a universal without an individual, since the universal is cognizable only by a cognition co-extensive with the individual. Nor is this an imposition of remembered sharpness and such, because there is no defeater, and because there would be the absurd consequence of not grasping sharpness and such in the first instance. This should not be [objected to] thus. Sharpness and such are not universals of the ga-phoneme and such, because of the absurd consequence of confusion with ga-hood and such. Nor is sharpness a unitary [property], because there would be the absurd consequence of there being no cognition tracking what is common to [various] sharp [sounds]. Nor is the tracking accounted for by sharpness being a word-residing universal that delimits the obstructive capacity regarding homogeneous direct perception, because there is a cognition tracking sharpness even without recognizing that [obstructive capacity]. And sharpness and softness are not universals residing in sound, because they have counterpositive [i.e., they relate to opposites]. Nor is there contradiction between sharpness and softness, because the perception 'the very ga-phoneme that was sharp is now soft' — varying with occasions and speakers — establishes their identity. If it is objected that there is a perception of difference: 'this is sharp, not sharper, different from the sharp, the soft is other' — no, because when the substrate is appearing as non-different, the perception of qualified-substrate-difference has as its object the difference of properties. Just as in a single pot: 'this is red, not dark now' — a similar perception. Nor should it be said that because a sharp ga-phoneme overpowers a soft ga-phoneme, they are different — for the same thing cannot overpower itself, and since of the very same thing by the very same thing at the very same time, perception and non-perception would be contradictory — because the air that manifests sharpness, being more powerful, overpowers the air that manifests softness, and thus softness is not grasped. Or, let sharp and soft and such forms of ga-phonemes be entirely different, since there is no defeater for the recognition [of each as distinct]. Therefore, sharpness and such are indeed air-properties that appear as residing in sound, just as mirror-properties [appear to reside] in pleasure and such; and the perception of those [properties] is through the skin-sense of the ear-conch in association with touch, perceiving the airs that produce sharpness and softness — since even you accept degrees and manifested touch. Or, [they are perceived] by the ear alone. That the eye and such do not perceive air-properties — the unfitness there is the limiting condition; otherwise, the ear would not perceive its own [sound] quality — since the sense organ is seen to be so [fitted]. Or, the eye would not perceive earthly color, being a non-earthly sense organ — like the tongue. And so further [objections of this kind] would follow. Now if [the reply is that] a suitable [sense organ] grasps what is suitable, whether its own quality or another's, and the suitability is determined by the force of the result — then the same applies to the ear's grasping of air-properties. Nor is there non-perception of air in 'this ga-phoneme is sharp,' since even without perceiving it as air, it is perceived precisely through sharpness and such — just as red-hot iron is perceived [as hot] even without perceiving it as fire. If it is objected that since both air and sound are grasped by either the skin or the ear, by which [sense] is the imposition 'this ga-phoneme is sharp' [made]? No — from the non-apprehension of the connection between what is grasped by both sense organs, there is [still] conventional usage of connection. Or, let there be imposition by the ear of what is presented by the skin-sense; or, as stated, the ear alone grasps sharpness. And the claim of being-produced is not established, since that perception is contradicted by the recognition 'this ga-phoneme has been heard before.' If it is objected that the recognition itself is contradicted by that [perception], since the cognition of non-difference regarding the ga-phoneme is based on its ga-universal — as stated — no, because the ga-universal is not established. For the cognition of non-difference takes recourse to a universal [only] when difference is apparent. And there is no perception of difference among ga-phonemes; sharpness and softness too are not causes of difference, since by the recognition 'the very one that was sharp is now soft' — and even on [the assumption of] non-eternality of the ga-phoneme, this is still possible — then even on [the assumption of] eternality, it is possible that the production of air-properties is the limiting condition [rather than destruction of the phoneme]. Nor is there non-perception of air, since that is perceived precisely as something produced — just as [the redness of] the <s>japā</s> flower [is perceived] in the crystal through its red appearance.

children.text:
astu vā prāganulabhyamānatve sati upalabhyamānatvena utpannasya sādṛśyena smṛtotpattimattvāropaḥ /
na caivaṃ ghaṭādāvapi notpatteḥ siddhyediti vācyam /
kulālavyāpārānantaramanubhūyamānadhaṭasya tadvyāpārāt prāganubhūyamānena ghaṭena nābhedobhāsate kintu bheda eveti tatra prāgasattve sattvaṃ sidhyati, gakāre tūtpattipratītyanantaraṃ kaṇṭhatālvādivyāpārāt pūrvamanubhūyamānagakāreṇābhedapratyayāt pūrvamanubhūyagakāreṇābhedapratyayāt dīpavat sa vyañjaka eva /
atha śabda utpadyate utkarṣavattve sati apakarṣavattvāt mādhuryavat ata evānityatvamiti cet /
na /
tāratva-mandatvayorutkarṣāpakarṣayorgakāre pūrvanyāyenāsiddheḥ siddhau vā jātisaṅkarabhayenotkarṣāpakarṣayorjātyoḥ rasatva-śabdatvavyāpyayornānātvena rasaśabdasādhāraṇyābhāvāt /
ata eva sajātīyasākṣātkārapratibandhakatāvacchedakasāmānyamutkarṣaḥ tatpratibadhyasākṣātkāraviṣayatāvacchedakasāmānyamapakarṣa iti sādhāraṇo heturapāstaḥ /
tāratvādergakārajātitvāsiddheḥ /
sādhanāvacchinnasādhyavyāpakapūrttaguṇatatvasyāśrautratvasya copādhitvāt aprayojakatvācca /
na hi kāraṇādhīna eva utkarṣo 'pakarṣaśca, paramamahati paramāṇau ca parimāṇe pratyekaṃ sattvāt /
na cobhayasyaikatra sattvaṃ kāraṇaprayojyaṃ, ekaikavaddvayorapi pratyekamekatvāt /
syādetat /
śrotravyāpārānantaramidānīṃ śrutapūrvo gakāro nāsti vinaṣṭaḥ kolāhala iti pratīteḥ pratyakṣameva śabdānityatvaṃ vināśibhāvatvenotpattimattvānumānadvā, pratyakṣrapratiyogikābhāvatvena hi pratyakṣatvaṃ dhvaṃsasya ghaṭadhvaṃsavat na tu vināśagrahe pratiyogisamavāyipratyakṣatvaṃ tantraṃ dharmābhāvasya pratyakṣatvāpatteḥ /
tadindriyāgrāhye 'pi pratiyogisamavāyini gandha-rasābhāvayograhaṇācca /
nobhayaṃ gauravāt smṛtaghaṭasaṃyogadhvaṃsapratyakṣatvāpātācca /
na ca pratiyogiyogyatvasya tantratve vāyusparśadhvaṃso 'pi pratyakṣaḥ syāt iti vācyam /
āśrayanāśajanyasya tasya grāhakendriyasannikarṣābhāvāt /
kiñca yasya sattvaṃ yatrānupalabdhārthaḥ /
ata eva pṛthivītvābhāvo jalīyaparamāṇau na pratyakṣaḥ pratyakṣaśca vāyau rūpābhāvaḥ /
asti ca tathā śabde tasya sattve samavadhāne ca pratītiprasaṅgāt /
niradhikaraṇābhāvapratītirnāstīti cet, na, ihedānīṃ śabdo nāstīti pratīteḥ /
tasmāt yatrādhikaraṇe deśe samaye vā pratiyogyatra vartate tatra tadabhāvo nirūpyate /
ata eva sadbhyāmabhāvo nirūpyate ityuktaṃ, śabdābhāvasya ca svata evendriyasannikṛṣṭatvāt nāśraye sannikarṣāpekṣā /
indriyaviśeṣaṇatayā nābhāvagrahaṇamiti cet /
na /
ayogyatvasyāpadhitvāt /
anyathā guṇasya saṃyuktasamavāyena grahaṇadarśanāt na samavāyena śabdagrahaḥ syāditi /
maivaṃ /
sata eva hi śabdasya vyañjakavirahādanupalabdhimātraṃ na tu dhvaṃsaḥ, tattadvayāpetarasakalatadupalambhakasamavadhāne tadanupalabdhirūpayogyānupalabdherabhāvāt /
pratiyogyupalambhakavyañjakavāyusparśadhvaṃsopādhikaiva /
vāyurnotpādakaḥ kintu vyañjakaḥ ityatra kiṃ vinigamakamiti cet /
na /
idānīṃ śrutapūrvo gakāro nāsti vinaṣṭaḥ kolāhalaiti pratītyanantaraṃ punaḥ śravaṇe śrutapūrvo 'yaṃ gakāraḥ punaḥ sa evāyaṃ kolāhala iti pratyabhijñānameva, ghaṭadhvaṃsapratītyanantarañca sa evāyaṃ ghaṭa iti na pratyabhijñānamiti tatra vinaṣṭapratītyādhvaṃsa eva sidhyati /
ata eva tāratva-tārataratva-mandatva-mandataratvapratītīnāṃ bhramatvakalpanamityapāstam /
etāsu satīṣpyabhedapratyabhijñānāt /
syādetat /
śabdaḥ prayatnasādhyaḥ tadanabhivyañjakatvaṃ hi indriyasambandhapratibandhakāpanāyakatvādindriyasannidhāpakatvādvā kuḍyotsāraṇeneva paṭādīnāṃ, tadubhayamapi śabde na sambhavati nityasamavetatvenāvaraṇāpanayana-sannidhānapanayorabhāvāt /
nāpi śrotrasaṃskārāt, indriyasaṃskārasya unmīlanālokādeḥ sakṛdindrayasambandhayogyasarvārthopalabdhyanukūlasaṃskārajanakatvaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ tadvadvāyurapi sakṛdeva sarvaśabdopalabdhyanukūlalaṃ śrotre saṃskāramādadhyāt, tathāca sarvaśabdopalabdhiḥ syāt /
taduktaṃ ``sakṛcca saṃskṛtaṃ śrotraṃ sarvaśabdān prakāśyet /
ghaṭāyonmīlitaṃ cakṣuḥ paṭaṃ na hi na budhyate'' /
athānvaya - vyatirekābhyāṃ kārye pratiniyatajanakajanyatvavacchabde 'pi pratiniyatavyañjakavyaṅyāḥ ekāvacchedena samānadeśatve sati samānendriyagrāhyatvāt ghaṭaikatvaparimāṇavat /
na cāvayavasaṃyoga-bahutvavyañajakāvyaṅyenāvayavinotpalatvavyañjakadīpāvyaṅyena tannīlimnā ghaṭavṛttipṛthaktvavyañjakāvyaṅyenaikatvena vā vyabhicāraḥ / avayavasaṃyogāvayavinornīlatvotpalatvayoścāvyāpyavyāpyavṛttinorutpalatvasya cādhikavṛttitvenaikāvacchedena vṛttyabhāvāt /
bahutva-pṛthaktvavyañjakavyaṅyatvaṃ, ata eva nīlā balāketyatra
children.translated_text: Or let there be the superimposition of the property of having origination through similarity-based memory-generation upon what is being perceived, given that it was not perceived before. And it cannot be said that in this way, origination would not be established even for a pot and so forth—because the pot experienced immediately after the potter's activity does not appear as non-different from the pot experienced before that activity, but rather as different; hence there, existence is established where there was prior non-existence. But in the case of the <s>ga</s>-sound, immediately after the perception of its production, there is a cognition of non-difference with the <s>ga</s>-sound previously experienced through the activity of the throat, palate, and so on—like a lamp, it is merely a manifestor. Now, if [one argues]: sound is produced; because it has decrease while having increase, like sweetness; and hence impermanence follows—no, because increase and decrease, namely loudness and softness, are not established in the <s>ga</s>-sound by the previous reasoning; or if established, due to the fear of intermixture of universals, since the universals of increase and decrease are different, being pervaded by 'taste-hood' and 'sound-hood' respectively, there is no commonality between taste and sound. For this very reason, the argument that 'increase is the universal that delimits the obstruction of direct perception of the same kind, and decrease is the universal that delimits the content of the obstructed direct perception' is also a common [inconclusive] reason—because the universal-hood of loudness and so on with respect to the <s>ga</s>-sound is not established. And because the property of being a fulfilling quality that pervades the <s>sādhya</s> as delimited by the <s>sādhana</s> is a limiting condition, being non-Vedic, and is also non-productive. For increase and decrease do not depend solely on causes, since both exist in the case of the supremely large and the atomic dimensions respectively. Nor is the co-existence of both in one thing causally produced, since like each individually, both together also have individual unity. One might say: after the activity of the ear, the recognition 'the <s>ga</s>-sound heard before does not now exist—it has perished, the noise!' is a direct perception of the impermanence of sound; or through inference from the fact that what is destructible has origination. The directness of <s>dhvaṃsa</s> (destruction) is through being the absence whose counterpositive is directly perceived, like the destruction of a pot—but the direct perception of the substrate of the counterpositive is not the determining factor for the perception of destruction, since the absence of a property would then become directly perceptible. And because the absence of smell and taste, whose counterpositives are not grasped by that sense-organ even though they inhere in the substrate, is grasped. Neither [interpretation works] due to over-complexity and because the destruction of a remembered pot's conjunction would also become directly perceptible. And it cannot be said that if the fitness of the counterpositive is the determining factor, then the destruction of wind-touch would also be directly perceptible—because for that [destruction], which is caused by the destruction of its substrate, there is no sense-contact with a grasping sense-organ. Moreover, what is the purpose of the non-perception of something that exists [in some place]? For this very reason, the absence of earth-hood in aqueous atoms is not directly perceptible, but the absence of color in air is directly perceptible. And thus in the case of sound, if it existed and were in proximity, there would follow its perception. If [one says] there is no perception of an absence without a locus—no, because of the perception 'there is no sound here now.' Therefore, where—in whatever locus, place, or time—the counterpositive exists, there its absence is ascertained. Hence it is said that absence is ascertained from existing things; and the absence of sound, being intrinsically in contact with the sense-organ, does not require contact through its substrate. If [one says] absence is not grasped as a qualifier of the sense-organ—no, because the unfitness is a limiting condition; otherwise, since the grasping of a quality through contact-inherence is observed, the grasping of sound through inherence would not occur. Do not say so, because of the sound that exists, it is merely non-perception due to the absence of a manifestor, not destruction—because there is no qualified non-perception, which would be the non-perception of something whose every means of perception co-exists with everything devoid of both [manifestor and what it manifests]. It is subject to the limiting condition of the destruction of wind-touch, the manifestor for perceiving the counterpositive. If [one asks] what is the distinguishing mark that wind is not a producer but merely a manifestor—no, because after the perception 'the <s>ga</s>-sound heard before does not now exist—it has perished, the noise!', when it is heard again, there is recognition 'this is the same <s>ga</s>-sound heard before, the same noise'; but after the perception of the destruction of a pot, there is no recognition 'this is the same pot'—hence there, from the perception of destruction, only destruction is established. For this very reason, the supposition that the perceptions of loudness, louder, softness, and softer are erroneous is refuted, since even when these exist, there is recognition of non-difference. One might say: sound is effort-produced; its not being a manifestor is because it is not a remover of obstructions to sense-contact, or not a bringer-into-proximity of the sense-organ—like moving a wall for cloths and so on. Neither is possible for sound, since being eternally inherent, there is neither obstruction-removal nor proximity-establishment. Nor [is it] from a modification of the hearing organ, because a modification of the sense-organ, such as opening the eyes or [providing] light, is observed to produce fitness for grasping all objects accessible to a single sense-contact at once; likewise, wind too would produce in the ear at once a modification conducive to the perception of all sounds, and thus all sounds would be perceived. As stated: 'The ear, modified once, would reveal all sounds; the eye, opened for a pot, does not fail to perceive a cloth.' Now, through positive and negative concomitance, just as effects have specific producers, so sounds too have specific manifestors; because when there is identity of locus under one delimiter, they are grasped by the same sense-organ—like the unity-dimension of a pot. Nor is there deviation through the composite-contact that is not manifested by the manifestor of the composite-whole, or through the blueness of the lotus that is not manifested by the lamp which manifests lotus-hood, or through the unity that is not manifested by the manifestor of the separateness residing in the pot—because composite-contact and composite-whole, and blueness and lotus-hood, are related as having non-co-extensive and co-extensive occurrence respectively, and lotus-hood has wider occurrence, so they do not occur under a single delimiter. The property of being manifested by a specific manifestor for plurality and separateness—hence in 'the blue cranes'

etena sāmānyavattve satyasmadādivahirindriyajapratyakṣatvāt ityapāstaṃ, pratyabhijñānabādhāt śabdatva-gatvāderasiddheśca, tasmācchabdo nityaḥ vyomaikaguṇatvāt tatparimāṇavat, śrotragrāhyatvāt śabdatvavat, viśeṣaguṇāntarāsamānādhikaraṇaikavṛttiguṇatvāt samayaparimāṇavat, pṛthivītaranityabhūtaviśeṣaguṇatvāt apākajatve sati nityaikasamavetatvāt jalaparamāṇurūpavat, avyāsajyavṛttitve sati anātmavibhuguṇatvāt kālaparimāṇavat, vipakṣe bādhakañca pratyabhijñānameveti /
children.translated_text: In reality, however, when non-difference is established by the force of recognition that cannot be otherwise explained, the argument establishing that [sounds] are manifested by specific manifestors has no greater force. And [the views that] sound produces sound, or sound destroys sound, or that production is postulated by the analogy of wave-crests—these are mere postulations, since sound does not produce sound nor destroy sound, like the last and first sounds [in a series]. By this, the argument that 'being possessed of a universal, [sound] is directly perceptible by an external sense-organ like ours' is also refuted—because of the defeat by recognition, and because the universal 'sound-hood' or 'cow-hood' and the like are not established [as proving impermanence]. Therefore, sound is eternal: because it is the sole quality of <s>ākāśa</s> (space), like its dimension; because it is grasped by the ear, like sound-hood; because it is a quality occurring in a single locus that is not co-located with any other particular quality, like the dimension of time; because being an unproduced particular quality of a substance other than earth, and being eternally inherent in a single [substance], like the color of a water-atom; because having non-pervading occurrence and being a quality of a non-self all-pervading [substance], like the dimension of time. And the defeater in the opposing case is recognition itself.

na /

na ca varṇābhivyañjakavāyubhireva dūre dhvanimātramabhivyajyate, kavyañjakasya gavyañjana iva varṇavyañjakasya dhvanivyañjane 'sāmarthyāt tatsamarthaśaṅkhāderabhāvācca /
na ca tatra śabdatvamevapratīyate na śabdaḥ, vyaktyagrahe jātyagrahāt /
na cābhivyañjako vāyureva kolāhalatvena pratīyate, śabdatvena pratyayāt sannidhāvapi tathā pratyayaprasaṅgācca /
gakārādigrahe 'pi teṣāṃ parasparabhedāgrahāt kolāhaladhīriti cet, na, teṣu vaidharmyābhāvāt tadabhāve 'nyonyābhāvasyābhāvāt svarūpagrahaṇāt samīpe bahugakāreṣu bhedābhāvena tadagrahe kolāhaladhīprasaṅgācca /
anekavarṇoccāraṇasya taddhetutve dūre 'pi tadapratyayāpatteḥ /

asti ca śabdasya ko 'pi ca jātiviśeṣaḥ śrotragrāhyaḥ yasmāt prācyādidigdeśaviśiṣṭaśaṅkhaprabhavatvamanumīyate, avyapadeśasyatve 'pi ikṣukṣīrādimādhuryāvāntaravattatsattvāt /
anyathā digdaśaviśiṣṭaśaṅkhādīnāṃ grahe śrotraśyāsāmarthyāt tatpratītirna syādeva /
tathāpi gatvādinā parāparabhāvānupapattyā śukādigakārādiṣu na jātiviśeṣā iti cet, śukakārādiṣu katvādivyāpyā nānājātirbhinnā tayā pratyekaṃ śukakārādiṣu ekā jātirasti śukaprabhavatvādyanumāpikā tadvyavahārakārikā vā, gatvādinā saṅkaraprasaṅgāt, gatvantu na nānā ananugatatvena tato 'nugatavyavahārānupapatteḥ /
ata eva tāratvamapi gatvādivyāpyaṃ nānā na tu gatvaṃ, tanniścaye 'pi gatvasandehaśca vyāpyatāvacchedakatvenānugatena nānātāratveṣṭhanugatavyavahārasambhavāt, tadajñāne vyavahārāsiddheḥ /
tāratva-mandatve na jātī sapratiyogikatvāt iti cet, na tāratva,tārataratvādayautkarṣādirūpā jātiviśeṣā eva te cāśraye gṛhyamāṇa eva gṛhyante na tūtkarṣāvadhyapekṣāḥ yathā madhurataratvādaya utkarṣavyavahāraṃ itarasāpekṣāḥ kurvanti tathā mandādyapekṣayā tāratvādivyavahāraṃ, utkarṣastu jātirūpādanyo 'sambhāvita eva gakāre tu naivaṃ, ananyathāsiddhabhedapratyayabalena vaktṛviśeṣānumānabalena ca tatsiddhergatva-katvavyāpyatannānātvasvīkārāt /
children.translated_text: Here it is said: The instances of the phoneme 'ga' and so forth are individually distinct. And there is a manifestation of difference in their own nature among the phonemes 'ga' and the like produced by parrots, <s>sārikā</s>-birds, and humans, and produced by women, men, and their respective subtypes, due to the more vivid distinctiveness [among them], like the sweetness of sugarcane-juice, milk, and the like. Nor is this cognition of difference adventitious (<s>aupādhika</s>); for just as one who knows saffron [recognizes] 'the young woman is saffron-red,' the property of being produced by a woman or man is not an experiential adventitious condition (<s>upādhi</s>), since even one who does not know the difference of woman, man, and so forth through sense-contact has the cognition of phoneme-difference, from which they infer 'this is a parrot's sound, this is a woman's sound,' and so forth—otherwise there would be mutual dependence: the cognition of difference when the source is known, and the inference of the source from the cognition of difference. Nor is the adventitious character established by reasoning, like the elongation of the face [reflected] in a sword following the presence and absence of the sword, because there is no such following of any other [condition]. Now if [it is objected that] the distinctiveness belongs only to the manifesting air, and appears as belonging to the parrot's 'ga' and so forth, since air is perceived in that very form—no. Because there is no defeater (<s>bādhaka</s>) for [the distinctiveness] belonging to the phoneme 'ga.' Nor is the recognition of non-difference a defeater, for there is no recognition 'this very parrot-sound is this very woman's sound'—otherwise, in the absence of the cognition of difference in those [sounds], there would be no inference of the particular speaker. Nor is the distinctiveness of the manifesting air alone what enables the inference of a parrot and so forth, because that [distinctiveness] does not inhere in the phoneme 'ga,' and because there would follow the consequence that the inference based on that superimposition would be erroneous. Therefore, just as when difference is manifest in 'a black cow, a white cow,' the cognition that follows the common element of the phoneme 'ga' grasps cow-ness (<s>gotva</s>), so too when difference is manifest in the phonemes 'ga' of parrots and so forth, the cognition 'this is a ga, this too is a ga' grasps ga-ness (<s>gatva</s>)—thus both recognition and the manifestation of difference are accounted for. Moreover, if ga-ness and the like are not universals (<s>jāti</s>), then there would be no cognition of cacophony (<s>kolāhala</s>). For indeed, in a city and so forth, when many persons simultaneously utter phonemes, one standing at a distance hears only cacophony, without distinguishing the individual phonemes 'ga' and so forth. Nor is it possible that in that case one hears a sound of a different nature, namely of the form of <s>dhvani</s> (resonance), other than the phonemes, because the instruments that manifest it—drums and the like—are absent. Nor are the very same [agents] that manifest the phonemes also the manifesters of <s>dhvani</s>, because even when the phonemes are heard in proximity, there would follow the consequence of hearing that [<s>dhvani</s>] as well. Nor is it the case that only the very air that manifests the phonemes manifests mere <s>dhvani</s> at a distance—because the manifester of one thing lacks the capacity to manifest another, like [the instrument used for] clarified butter [cannot be used for] cow's [milk], and because of the absence of conches and the like that have that capacity. Nor is it the case that only sound-ness (<s>śabdatva</s>) is cognized there, not sound [itself], because without grasping the instance, the universal cannot be grasped. Nor is it the case that the manifesting air itself is cognized as cacophony, because of the cognition as 'sound,' and because even in proximity, there would follow the same consequence. Even if the phonemes 'ga' and so forth are grasped, since the mutual difference among them is not grasped, there is the cognition of cacophony—if so objected, no, because there is no dissimilarity among those [identical] phonemes, and in the absence of that, the mutual absence [between them] is absent, since their own nature is grasped, and because when many phonemes 'ga' in proximity are not differentiated, there would follow the consequence of cacophony. And if the simultaneous utterance of multiple phonemes were the cause of that, even at a distance there would follow the consequence of the non-occurrence of that [cacophony cognition]. Therefore, there is necessarily a universal of the form of ga-ness and the like, in the absence of the grasping of which, even when the phonemes 'ga' and so forth are grasped, there is the cognition and designation of cacophony. And there is some specific universal of sound, apprehensible by the ear, from which the origin in a conch and the like characterized by specific directions is inferred; even if it is not designatable, its existence is established, like the sub-varieties of sweetness in sugarcane-juice, milk, and the like. Otherwise, since the ear lacks the capacity to grasp conches and the like characterized by specific directions, there would be absolutely no cognition of them. Even so, because the higher-and-lower relation is not accounted for by ga-ness and the like, in the phonemes 'ga' and so forth of parrots and the like, there are no specific universals—if so objected: in the phonemes 'ga' and the like of parrots, there are diverse universals (<s>jāti</s>) pervaded by 'ka-ness' and the like, and by those [diverse universals], in each case of parrot-'ga' phonemes and the like, there is one universal that enables the inference of origin from a parrot and the like, or that produces the corresponding verbal usage. Due to ga-ness and the like, there would follow the consequence of conflation. But ga-ness is not diverse, because in the absence of common element there would be the impossibility of common verbal usage from that. For this very reason, 'high-pitched-ness' (<s>tāratva</s>) too is diverse, pervaded by ga-ness and the like, but ga-ness is not. Even when ga-ness is ascertained, there is also doubt about ga-ness, since from the common element functioning as the delimitor of the pervasion-relation, when there is diversity among the various instances of high-pitched-ness, the possibility of common verbal usage [arises], while in the absence of knowledge of that, the verbal usage would not be established. High-pitched-ness and low-pitched-ness are not universals because they have a counterpositive—if so objected, no. High-pitched-ness, higher-pitched-ness, and so forth are specific universals of the form of degrees of excellence; and those, being grasped in the substrate, are grasped without reference to the benchmark of excellence, just as higher sweetness and the like produce the verbal usage of excellence in relation to another [degree of sweetness], so too high-pitched-ness and the like produce verbal usage in relation to low-pitched-ness and the like. But excellence, being different from the universal nature, is simply inconceivable. In the case of the phoneme 'ga,' however, it is not so, since the establishment of that [difference in phonemes] is through the force of the cognition of difference not otherwise explicable and through the force of inference of the particular speaker, and [therefore] the acceptance of the diversity of what is pervaded by ga-ness and ka-ness follows.

nanvevamutpatti /

na hi tāvadvarṇamātramānupūrvī, jarā-rāja-nadī-dīnādiṣu tannānātvāt, kintu taduccāraṇānantaramuccāraṇaṃ tajjñānānantaraṃ jñānaṃ vā tacca nāneti tadvatī gāthāpi nānaiva /
nacābhede bhāsamāne utpādādibuddhirevānyasyotpādādikamavagāhate, gākāragatatvapratīterbhrāntatva prasaṅgāt /
na ceṣṭāpattiḥ, abhede bhāsamāne tadviruddhadharmavattvabhramānudayāt vinigamakābhāvenobhayasyāpi yathārthatvāñca, kutastarhi
children.translated_text: Even for you who hold that [phonemes] are modifications of air, the distinctiveness (<s>vijātīyatva</s>) of the air that manifests the phonemes 'ka,' 'ga,' and so forth of parrots and the like must be stated. And thus, if the property of being air that manifests parrot-phonemes is pervaded by the property of being air that manifests the phoneme 'ka,' then it would not apply to the air manifesting the parrot's phoneme 'ga.' If it is instead pervading [i.e., wider], then all air that manifests 'ka' would be air that manifests parrot-phonemes. Therefore, even on the view that [phonemes] are modifications of air, the diversity of those [phoneme-types] is necessary. Now if [it is conceded that] let there be the difference of phonemes 'ga' produced by women, men, and so forth—nevertheless, corresponding to every difference of speaker, the eternally existing phonemes are innumerable, due to recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>)—if so objected: even when the cognition of origination and destruction is present, the recognition 'this is the very same phoneme ga' [occurs]; for indeed, even immediately after that [recognition], there is the manifestation of origination and destruction. Nor is there any defeater for either of the two—the cognition of origination and the recognition of non-difference—that would defeat the other while leaving it aside; nor is there a determining factor for the defeater-defeated relation between them, by which one would be erroneous and hence there would be no contradiction. How indeed, overriding the mutual obstructing capacity of the cognitions of difference and non-difference established elsewhere, could the first arising of one [cognition] even when both are present [lead to] the consequence of the other arising—and thus, being in an impasse, the recognition cannot be used as a <s>pramāṇa</s> for the eternality of phonemes. But if [it is objected that] in that case, how can non-eternality be established by 'having origination' and the like [either]?—[We reply] thus: between the cognition of origination and the recognition, there must be a difference of object; if they had the same object, there would follow the consequence that, due to contradiction, immediately after one, the other could not arise. And thus, when difference is manifest, the object of recognition is being of the same kind (<s>sajātīyatva</s>), not non-difference of the instance. Nor should it be said that [the recognition] would then be 'this is of the same kind,' not 'this is that very one.' Even the cognition of being of the same kind has the form 'this is that very one,' as in 'this is the very same verse, this is the very same medicine—made by many and also being made by me every day,' and so forth. For certainly it is not the case that the sequential arrangement alone constitutes the verse [or] melody. In 'old age' (<s>jarā</s>), 'king' (<s>rāja</s>), 'river' (<s>nadī</s>), 'poor' (<s>dīna</s>), and the like, the [phoneme arrangement] is diverse. Rather, it is the utterance immediately after that [prior] utterance, or the cognition immediately after that [prior] cognition—and that too is diverse. Hence the verse that possesses that is also diverse. Nor when non-difference is manifest, does the cognition of origination and the like apprehend the origination and the like of something else—because there would follow the consequence of the cognition of [origination] as belonging to the phoneme 'ga' being erroneous. Nor is this an accepted consequence, since when non-difference is manifest, there is no arising of the error of possessing a contradictory property. And due to the absence of a determining factor, both [cognitions] are veridical. Then whence

tasmāt utpatti-vināśa-tāratvādipratyayasya pratyabhijñānasya ca tulyatve dvayorapi nityatvamanityatvaṃ vā /
na cobhayorapi nityatvameva, uktanyāyena pratyabhijñāyāstajjātītvaviṣayatvāt /
kiñca yadi vyaṅyaḥ śabdaḥ syāt tadā bāhyālokābhāve ghaṭasyeva vyañjakābhāve śabdasyānupalambhāt tatsaṃśayaḥ syāt, na tvihedānīṃ śabdo nāstīti niścayaḥ tasmādvarṇo na nityo 'nityo vā sattve satyutpattimattvāt, asmadādibahirindriya-grāhyatve sati jātimattvāt, asmadādipratyakṣaguṇatvādvā, ātmaikatvapratyakṣapakṣe pratyakṣaviśeṣaguṇatvāt, vyāpakasamavetapratyakṣaviśeṣaguṇatvāt, anātmapratyakṣaguṇatvāt, avyāpyavṛttitvāt, īśvarajñānañca na tathā, tatprayokakāraṇābhāvāt, bahirindriyavyavasthāhetuguṇatvāt, bhūtapratyakṣaguṇatvāt, utkarṣāpakarṣarpaśabdapravṛttinimittajātimattvādvetyādi, rasatvādivyāpyajāternānātve 'pi tādṛśapravṛttinimittatvasya sādhāraṇyāt /
na cātra sādhanāvacchinnasya pakṣadharmāvavicchannasya vā sādhyasya vyāpakaḥ sparśavatsamavetatvaṃ upādhiḥ, sarvatra varṇātmakaśabdapakṣīkaraṇe vyomaguṇeṣṭhanityeṣu dhvaniṣu sādhyāvyāpakatvāt sparśavat padasya pakṣamātravyāvartakatvena pakṣetaratvācceti /
yadā ca varṇā eva na nityāstadā kaiva kathā puruṣavivakṣādhīnānupūrvyādiviśiṣṭavarṇasamuharūpāṇāṃ padānāṃ, kutastarāñca tatsamūharūpasya vākyasya kutastamāñca tatsamūhasya vedasyeti /
children.translated_text:
The object of that [recognition] is non-difference; where initially there is no manifestation of difference, precisely for that reason, even when difference exists, due to ignorance of it, [recognition] is sometimes erroneous. Therefore, where the cognition of difference is not sublated by any other sublating cognition, there recognition simply does not occur, or if it does occur, it takes as its object mere belonging-to-the-same-class (<s>tajjātīyatva</s>), but is not erroneous, because error does not arise when a specific difference is perceived.
Moreover, just as in the case of sounds of conch-shells and the like, when the impermanence [of those sounds] is established through cognitions of origination and destruction and through association with contradictory properties such as high pitch (<s>tāratva</s>) etc., the very same recognition 'this is that Gujari [melody]' and the like has as its object belonging-to-the-same-class — so too with the recognition of phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>).
Otherwise, even musical sounds (<s>dhvani</s>) would be eternal,
because the cognitions of origination, destruction, high pitch, etc. would be [dismissible as] merely adventitious (<s>aupādhika</s>) on the strength of recognition. Nor should it be said that in [the case of] phonemes, the musical sounds (<s>dhvani</s>) appearing as high-pitched alone are the adventitious factors, while phonemes are not [adventitious factors] in musical sounds, because of the absence of the contact with throat, palate, etc. that produces them —
because even at the time of uttering phonemes, the causes that produce the Gujari [melody] and the like are absent.
Therefore, when the cognition of origination, destruction, high pitch, etc. and recognition are on equal footing, either both [phonemes and musical sounds] are eternal or both are non-eternal.
And it is not the case that both are simply eternal, because, by the reasoning stated above, recognition has as its object belonging-to-the-same-class.
Furthermore, if sound (<s>śabda</s>) were [merely] manifested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>), then just as in the absence of external light a pot [is not perceived], so in the absence of a manifesting agent the sound would not be apprehended, and there would be doubt about it — but [we find] the certainty 'there is no sound here now,' not [mere] doubt. Therefore, the phoneme (<s>varṇa</s>) is not eternal — [it is] non-eternal; because, while existing, it possesses origination; because, while being graspable by external sense-organs of persons like us, it possesses a universal (<s>jāti</s>); or because it is a quality (<s>guṇa</s>) perceptible to persons like us; in the view that the self is perceived as one, because it is a quality that is a specific perceptible; because it is a quality that is a specific perceptible inhering in a pervasive [substance]; because it is a quality perceptible by [a sense-organ] other than the self; because it is a non-pervasive occurrence (<s>avyāpyavṛtti</s>). And the knowledge of <s>Īśvara</s> (God) is not like that, because of the absence of a cause prompting it. Because it is a quality that is the basis for the determination of external sense-organs; because it is a quality perceptible to material elements (<s>bhūta</s>); because it possesses a universal that is the ground for the application of words expressing degrees of intensity and diminution — and so forth. Because even though the pervaded universal such as taste-ness (<s>rasatva</s>) etc. does not establish non-eternality, the property of being a ground for such [verbal] application is common [to sound and taste etc.].
And here the co-inherence in something possessing touch (<s>sparśavatsamavetatva</s>) is not an adventitious condition (<s>upādhi</s>) for the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) as delimited by the <s>sādhana</s> (probans) or as undelimited by the property-of-being-in-the-subject (<s>pakṣadharma</s>) — because when all phoneme-constituted sound is made the subject (<s>pakṣa</s>), [this co-inherence] does not pervade the <s>sādhya</s> in the case of the qualities of ether (<s>vyoman</s>) which are accepted as eternal sounds (<s>dhvani</s>); and because the term 'possessing touch' (<s>sparśavat</s>), by excluding only the subject, belongs to the non-subject class.
And when phonemes themselves are not eternal, what need is there to speak of words (<s>pada</s>), which are aggregates of phonemes whose sequence depends on the speaker's intention (<s>puruṣavivakṣā</s>)? And even less of sentences (<s>vākya</s>), which are aggregates of those [words]? And least of all of the <s>Veda</s>, which is an aggregate of those [sentences]?
