children.text:
nanu sanodhātvarthagocarecchāvācitvāt lāghavāñca kṛtāvicchā cikīrṣā sā ca vṛṣṭāviveṣṭasādhanatājñānāditi cet, na, vahninā sādhayāmītivat kṛtyāsādhayāmītīcchāyāḥ kṛteḥ pūrvamanubhūyamānāyāḥ sanantāvācyatvena gauraveṇa ca pratyākhyātumaśakyatvāt /
kiñca pākaṃ cikīrṣatītyatra prādhānyena pākasyecchāviṣayatvamanubhūyate na tu kṛteḥ, dhātośca sanpratyayābhidheyecchāprakāravācitvaṃ, odanaṃ bubhukṣata ityatra bhojanaviśeṣyatayaudanasyecchāviṣayatvānubhavāt /
iṣṭasādhanatvena vṛṣṭāviva kṛtāvicchāsambhave 'pi kṛtīcchā na pravartikā kintu svakṛtisādhyecchaiva, ghaṭaṃ jānāti cikīrṣati karotījñāna-cikīrṣā-kṛtīnāmekaviṣayatvānubhavāt /
atha yadi kṛtyā sādhayitumicchā sā tadā cikīrṣitasya pākasyānyataḥ siddhau sā nāpagacchet, na hyupāyaviśeṣasādhyatvenecchopāyāntarādhīnaphalalābhena nivāryate, prītyā dhanalābhe 'pi pratigraheṇa tallipsāyā anivṛtteriti cet, na, svaviṣayasiddhatvasya phalecchāvicchedasya copāyecchāvirodhatvāt / asti ca tatra pākaudanayoḥ siddhatvaṃ, anyaudanecchāyāṃ pākacikīrṣā bhavatyeva, pratyutāsiddhatvāt kṛtāvevecchā na vicchidyeta yadi kṛtiviṣayasiddhatva-phalecchāvicchedau na virodhinau /
prītyā dhanalābhe ca tadadhikadhanecchā na vicchidyate tasyāsiddhatvāt tatphalecchāyāśca sattvāt dhanamātrārthinaśca prītyā dhanalābhe 'pi pratigraheṇa tallipsā nāstyeva dhanamātrasya siddhatvāt /
kiñcidviśeṣasiddhyaiva hi sāmānyecchāvicchedaḥ /
anyathā sakalasvaviṣayasiddherasambhavena tadvicchedo na syādeva /
vastutastu kriyānukūlā kṛtiriṣṭopāya iti jñāne kriyāyāḥ kṛtisādhyatvamiṣṭopāyatvañca bhātaṃ kriyādvāraiva kṛteriṣṭasādhanatvāditi tadbodhāt kṛtāviva kṛtisādhyatvena kriyāyāmapi saiveccheti cikīrṣāyāṃ kṛtisādhyatvaprakāranaiyatyamataḥ kṛtisamānaviṣayacikīrṣātvena cikīrṣāyāḥ kṛtikāraṇatvaṃ na tu kṛtīcchātvena bhinnaviṣayatayā gauravāt /
tathāpi yena rūpeṇa yasyeṣṭasādhanatvaṃ tena prakāreṇa tatrecchā yathā svakedāravṛṣṭitvena iṣṭasādhanatvāt tathaivaicchā tathā kṛtisādhyatvena pākasyeṣṭasādhanatvamataḥ kṛtisādhyatvena tatrecchā bhavatīti, kṛtau kṛtiviṣaye vā cikīrṣāyāṃ na vṛṣṭīcchā, vilakṣaṇasāmagrayantarakalpanamiti cet, bhavedevaṃ, yadi kṛtisādhyatvena pākasya odanasādhanatā syāt, na caivaṃ gauravāt kintu pākatvena, sa tu kṛtiṃ vinā netyanyadetat /
vahninā sādhayāmītivat kṛtyā sādhayāmītīcchā iṣṭasādhanatājñānādeveti cet, tarhi tatra vahnisādhyatājñānavadatrāpi kṛtisādhyatvajñānaṃ kāraṇamāvaśyakaṃ kṛtau cānubhavasiddhacikīrṣādhīnatatvaṃ viśeṣaḥ tena prāṇapañcakasañcāre jīvanayonikṛtisādhye na pravṛttiḥ, anyathā kṛtisādhyeṣṭasādhanatāpakṣe 'pi tatra pravarteta /
nanu cikīrṣādhīnatvasyopalakṣaṇatve upalakṣyamātragatānatiprasaktadharmābhāvāt kṛtimātrasya cātiprasaṅgāt tattatkṛtiviśeṣā upalakṣyāḥ tathāca tadananugamāt pravṛttyananugamaḥ, viśeṣaṇatve cikīrṣāyāṃ pravṛttau ca cikīrṣājñānakāraṇatve gauravaṃ pramāṇābhāvaśca /
kiñca cikīrṣāsādhyāvasthāyāḥ kṛteḥ siddhāvasthasādhanatvavirodhena kṛtisādhyatā pākādau na jñāyeteti cet, na, asti hi kṛtiviśeṣomānasapratyakṣasiddhojīvanayoniprayatnavyāvṛttaścikīrṣopalakṣyaḥ yatra cikīrṣākāraṇatvagrahaḥ sa ca tava jātirūpo mama tvanugatakāraṇopādhirūpaḥ, evañca cikīrṣādhīnatvenānugatena kṛtiviśeṣāṇāmupalakṣyāṇāṃ anugatatvamapi /
yathā gotveṇa taṭasthe nopalakṣitā mahiṣyādivyāvṛttadhānakarmavyaktiviśeṣāḥ
children.translated_text: Objection: Since the <s>san</s> suffix expresses desire directed toward the meaning of the verbal root, and due to parsimony, desire toward <s>kṛti</s> (effort) is <s>cikīrṣā</s> (desire to act), and that arises from the cognition that it is a means to the desired end, just as with rain — if so, no. Because just as there is the desire 'I shall accomplish by means of fire,' so the desire 'I shall accomplish by means of <s>kṛti</s>' — since <s>kṛti</s> is experienced prior [to the action], it cannot be rejected on account of the <s>san</s> suffix's denotation and the complexity [of the alternative]. Furthermore, in the expression '<s>pākaṃ cikīrṣati</s>' (he desires to cook), it is experienced that cooking is principally the object of desire, not <s>kṛti</s>; and the verbal root expresses the mode of desire denoted by the <s>san</s> suffix, as in '<s>odanaṃ bubhukṣate</s>' (he desires to eat rice), where rice is experienced as the object of desire as qualified by eating. Even though desire toward <s>kṛti</s> is possible in the manner of desiring rain as a means to the desired end, desire for <s>kṛti</s> is not the impeller; rather, it is only the desire for what is producible by one's own <s>kṛti</s>, because of the experience that cognition, <s>cikīrṣā</s>, and <s>kṛti</s> have the same object, as in 'he knows the pot, desires to make it, and makes it.' Now if the desire is to accomplish by means of <s>kṛti</s>, then when cooking that was desired to be done is accomplished by other means, that desire should not cease — for a desire directed toward producibility by a particular means is not blocked by obtaining the result through another means, just as the desire for wealth through gifts does not cease even when wealth is obtained through affection — if so, no, because the accomplishment of one's own object and the cessation of desire for the result are not incompatible with desire for the means. And there, cooking and rice are [both] accomplished; even when there is desire for different rice, the desire to cook persists. On the contrary, if the accomplishment of the object of <s>kṛti</s> and the cessation of desire for the result were not incompatible, then desire toward <s>kṛti</s> alone would never cease due to its non-accomplishment. When wealth is obtained through affection, the desire for more wealth does not cease because that [additional wealth] is not yet accomplished and because the desire for its result persists; but for one who desires only wealth in general, even when wealth is obtained through affection, there is no desire for it through gifts, because wealth in general is already accomplished. For the cessation of a general desire occurs through the accomplishment of any particular instance. Otherwise, since the accomplishment of the entirety of one's objects is impossible, that cessation would never occur at all. In reality, <s>kṛti</s> is favorable to action and is a desired means — in such cognition, the producibility of action by <s>kṛti</s> and its being a desired means are manifest; since <s>kṛti</s> is a means to the desired end only through action, from that cognition, the same desire that is directed toward <s>kṛti</s> is also directed toward the action as producible by <s>kṛti</s> — thus in <s>cikīrṣā</s> there is a fixed determination of the mode of producibility by <s>kṛti</s>; therefore the causality of <s>cikīrṣā</s> with respect to <s>kṛti</s> is by virtue of its being a <s>cikīrṣā</s> having the same object as <s>kṛti</s>, not by virtue of its being a desire for <s>kṛti</s>, since the latter would involve complexity due to different objects. Nevertheless, in whatever form something is a means to the desired end, in that very mode there is desire toward it — just as because rain on one's own field is a means to the desired end, desire is directed accordingly; so too, because cooking is a means to the desired end by virtue of being producible by <s>kṛti</s>, desire is directed toward it as producible by <s>kṛti</s> — thus in <s>cikīrṣā</s> directed toward <s>kṛti</s> or toward the object of <s>kṛti</s>, there is no desire for rain [separately], that being a postulation of a different causal complex — if so, this would be so if cooking's being a means to rice were by virtue of being producible by <s>kṛti</s>; but this is not so, due to complexity, rather it is by virtue of being cooking; and that [cooking] does not occur without <s>kṛti</s> — this is a separate matter. If one says that the desire 'I shall accomplish by means of <s>kṛti</s>' arises from the cognition that it is a means to the desired end, just as 'I shall accomplish by means of fire,' then just as cognition of producibility by fire is required there, here too cognition of producibility by <s>kṛti</s> is necessarily a cause; and the distinguishing feature is that <s>kṛti</s> depends on <s>cikīrṣā</s> as established by experience — therefore in the movement of the five vital breaths, which is producible by <s>kṛti</s> arising from the life-force, there is no volitional activity; otherwise, even on the view that it is a means to the desired end as producible by <s>kṛti</s>, there would be volitional activity there. Objection: If the dependence on <s>cikīrṣā</s> is merely an indicator (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>), then since the indicated instances lack a non-over-pervading property, and since <s>kṛti</s> in general would be over-pervaded, particular <s>kṛtis</s> would be what is indicated, and since those are not unified, there would be no unified account of volitional activity; if it is a qualifier (<s>viśeṣaṇa</s>), then complexity and lack of evidence would result from requiring cognition of <s>cikīrṣā</s> as a cause of <s>cikīrṣā</s> and of volitional activity. Furthermore, since <s>kṛti</s> in its state of being to-be-produced by <s>cikīrṣā</s> is incompatible with being a means in its accomplished state, the producibility by <s>kṛti</s> would not be cognized with respect to cooking and the like — if so, no. For there exists a particular <s>kṛti</s> established by mental perception (<s>mānasa-pratyakṣa</s>), distinct from the effort arising from the life-force, indicated by <s>cikīrṣā</s>, with respect to which the causality of <s>cikīrṣā</s> is grasped; and that is, according to you, of the nature of a universal, and according to me, of the nature of a pervading causal condition — and thus through the unified property of dependence on <s>cikīrṣā</s>, the indicated particular <s>kṛtis</s> are also unified. Just as, by means of the universal 'cowness' standing alongside, particular instances of milch-cows distinct from female buffaloes and the like are spoken of

children.text:
dhenupadenocyate na tu gotvamapi, tathā cikīrṣāpi, evaṃ jīvanayoniyatnavyāvṛttakṛtiviśeṣāṇāṃ kṛtitvena jñānaṃ kāraṇamiti nānanugamaḥ /
nanu kṛtisādhye na kṛtirviśeṣaṇamasattvāt sattve vā kṛtau satyāṃ jñānaṃ jñāne ca kṛtirityanyonyāśrayaḥ, nopalakṣaṇamatiprasaṅgāditi cet, na, kṛtirhi jñāne viṣayatayā viśeṣaṇameva sādhye ca paricāyakatayopalakṣaṇaṃ anyathā iṣṭasādhane 'pīṣṭaṃ na viśeṣaṇamasattvāt nopalakṣaṇamatiprasaṅgāt, liṅgajñānādau vā kā gatiḥ /
nanvevaṃ śrame 'pi cikīrṣā syāttasyāpi cikīrṣādhīnakṛtisādhyatvāt atra vadanti /
śramastu bhojanādikriyāsādhyo na tatkṛtisādhyaḥ acikīrṣitatvāt kṛteḥ svadhvaṃsasākṣātkārātirikte cikīrṣāviṣayamātre janakatvāt, na hi bhojanacikīrṣāviṣayamātre janakatvāt, na hi bhojanacikīrṣādhīnakṛtyā gamanaṃ sādhyate iti kecit, tanna, gurutarabhārottolane kṛtyasādhye bhramāt pravṛttasya nigaḍaniścaladehasya vā kṛtau satyāmuttolana-calanakriyānutpāde 'pi śramānubhavāt kṛtereva kāraṇatvāt /
na tu tajjanyakriyāyāḥ sukhe vyabhicārācca /
na hi sukhaṃ kṛtikāraṇacikīrṣāviṣayaḥ, upāyacikīrṣājanyā hi kṛtiḥ na tu sukhacikīrṣājanyā /
cikīrṣājanyakṛtisādhyatvaṃ na śrame dveṣayoniprayatnādapi tadutpatterityapare /
tanna /
śatrubadhasyeṣṭasādhatanatvena cikīrṣājanyakṛtisādhyatvāt dveṣasya yatnājanakatvāt, dveṣasiddhistu śatruṃ dveṣmītyanubhavabalāt /
children.translated_text: by the word '<s>dhenu</s>' (milch-cow), and not by 'cowness' as such — similarly with <s>cikīrṣā</s>. Thus, the cognition of particular <s>kṛtis</s> distinct from efforts arising from the life-force, under the universal '<s>kṛtitva</s>' (effort-ness), is the cause — hence there is no lack of unification. Objection: In what is producible by <s>kṛti</s>, <s>kṛti</s> is not a qualifier because it does not [yet] exist; or if it does exist, then when <s>kṛti</s> exists, cognition [is required], and for cognition, <s>kṛti</s> [is required] — this is mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśraya</s>); nor is it an indicator, due to over-extension — if so, no. For <s>kṛti</s> is indeed a qualifier of cognition by way of being its object, and with respect to what is to be produced, it is an indicator by way of making it familiar; otherwise, even in a means to the desired end, the desired end would not be a qualifier because it does not [yet] exist, nor would it be an indicator due to over-extension — or what would be the recourse in inferential cognition and the like? Objection: In that case, there would be <s>cikīrṣā</s> even with respect to fatigue, since that too is producible by <s>kṛti</s> dependent on <s>cikīrṣā</s> — here they respond: Fatigue is producible by actions such as eating, not by the <s>kṛti</s> of those actions, since it is not an object of <s>cikīrṣā</s>; for <s>kṛti</s> is productive only of what is the mere object of <s>cikīrṣā</s> — eating-<s>cikīrṣā</s>-dependent <s>kṛti</s> does not produce walking — thus say some. That is wrong. For when someone engages [in lifting] a very heavy load due to error, or when a person whose body is fixed in shackles — even when <s>kṛti</s> is present but the actions of lifting or moving do not occur — fatigue is still experienced, so <s>kṛti</s> alone is the cause. And not the action produced by it, due to deviation with respect to pleasure. For pleasure is not the object of the <s>cikīrṣā</s> that causes <s>kṛti</s>; <s>kṛti</s> is produced by desire for the means, not by desire for pleasure. Others say: Producibility by <s>cikīrṣā</s>-generated <s>kṛti</s> does not apply to fatigue, because fatigue arises also from effort born of aversion. That is wrong. Because the killing of an enemy, being a means to the desired end, is producible by <s>cikīrṣā</s>-generated <s>kṛti</s>; and aversion does not produce effort. The establishment of aversion is based on the force of the experience 'I hate the enemy.'

children.text:
yattu śramaḥ kṛtitvena kṛtisādhyo na cikīrṣādhīnakṛtitvena, yadyacikīrṣi'tepi śrame cikīrṣādhīna kṛtitvena kāraṇatā syāt tadā cikīrṣitameva bhojanaṃ kṛtyā sādhyate nācikīrṣitaṃ gamanādīti na syāt, śramavaṅgamane 'pi tajjanyatvaprasaṅgāt, bhojanādiśca cikīrṣādhīnakṛtiviśeṣāt, sa hi kṛtimātraṃ vyabhicārati jīvanayokṛtestadanutpādāt /
yadvā śramo na bhojanakṛtisādhyaḥ kintu tannirantarotpannajjīvanayoniprayatnādeveti /
tanna /
na hi /
kṛtitvena tacchramajanakatvaṃ, nāpi kṛtyantarādeva śramotpattiḥ, jīvanayoniprayatne satyapi bhārodvahanādikamakurvatastādṛśanamānanubhavena tasya śramājanakatvāt tasmāt bhojanādivat śramaviśeṣaṇāmapi bhojanādikṛtisādhyatvamananyagatikatvāt /
suptasya svedādyanumitaḥ śramaḥ tajjanya iti cet, na, svedādeḥ śramānyahetukatvāt anyathā jāgare 'pi tadanuvṛttau śramānuvṛttiprasaṅgāt iti maivaṃ svecchādhīnakṛtiśeṣaṇatvāt, śramaśca niyamato 'nyecchādhīnakṛtisādhyaḥ śrame duḥkhatvenecchāvirahād ata evānyecchājanyakṛtisādhyatvena śramo nāntarīyaka ityucyate /
svacikīrṣādhīnatvantu na kṛtau viśeṣaṇaṃ gauravāt /
children.translated_text: As for the [view] that fatigue is producible by <s>kṛti</s> under the universal '<s>kṛtitva</s>' (effort-ness), not under '<s>cikīrṣā</s>-dependent-<s>kṛtitva</s>' — if even in fatigue, which is not desired to be produced, causality were through <s>cikīrṣā</s>-dependent <s>kṛtitva</s>, then it could not be the case that only the desired eating is produced by <s>kṛti</s> and not the undesired walking and so forth, because there would be the undesired consequence that walking too, like fatigue, would be produced by it; and eating and the like are produced by a particular <s>kṛti</s> dependent on <s>cikīrṣā</s>, and that particular <s>kṛti</s> deviates from <s>kṛti</s> in general, since the <s>kṛti</s> arising from the life-force does not produce it. Alternatively, fatigue is not producible by the <s>kṛti</s> of eating, but rather by the effort arising from the life-force produced immediately after it. That is wrong. For it is not the case that its capacity to produce fatigue is by virtue of being <s>kṛti</s> [in general], nor does fatigue arise from another <s>kṛti</s> alone; even when the effort arising from the life-force is present, one who does not carry heavy loads and the like does not experience such fatigue, so that [life-force effort] does not produce fatigue. Therefore, like eating and the like, the particular forms of fatigue too are producible by the <s>kṛti</s> of eating and the like, there being no other recourse. If one says: The fatigue inferred from perspiration and the like in a sleeping person is produced by that [life-force effort] — no, because perspiration and the like have causes other than fatigue; otherwise, if those persisted even in waking, there would be the undesired consequence of fatigue persisting as well. [Reply:] Let it not be so, because [the relevant <s>kṛti</s>] is qualified by dependence on one's own volition (<s>svecchā</s>). And fatigue is invariably producible by <s>kṛti</s> dependent on another's desire, since with respect to fatigue, being painful, there is an absence of desire [for it]; for this very reason, fatigue is said to be a necessary concomitant by virtue of being producible by <s>kṛti</s> generated from another's desire. But dependence on one's own <s>cikīrṣā</s> is not a qualifier of <s>kṛti</s>, due to complexity.

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 60)
children.translated_text: (Bibliotheca Indica 98, IV,2, p. 60)

children.text:
anye tu kṛtigataṃ dharmāntarameva uddeśyatvaṃ tadviśiṣṭakṛtisādhyaśca na śramaḥ acikīrṣitatvāt kintu kṛtimātrasādhyaḥ /
ata eva kaṣṭaṃ karmetyanubhavolokānāṃ /
evaṃ cikīrṣāyāṃ mamaikaṃ kṛtisādhyatvaṃ prayojakaṃ tava tu kṛtisādhyatve satīṣṭasādhanatvaṃ sukhatvaṃ duḥkhābhāvatvañceti catuṣṭayaṃ, icchāprayojakantu mama sukhatvaṃ duḥkhābhāvatvañceti dvayaṃ, vṛṣṭisādhnatvena tatrecchā sādhanatvasyecchāvirodhitvāt /
tava tu cayaṃ, viṣabhakṣaṇe tu kṛtisādhyatve 'pi balavadaniṣṭasādhanatvena cikīrṣā nāstīti kṛtau cikīrṣājanyatvaṃ viśeṣaṇamiti kaścit, tattucchaṃ, evaṃ hi viṣabhakṣaṇaṃ kṛtisādhyameva na syāt jīvanayonikṛte stasyānutpatteriti vyarthaṃ viśeṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
Others, however, [hold that] being-the-object-of-intention (<s>uddeśyatva</s>) is simply a different property residing in effort (<s>kṛti</s>); and exertion (<s>śrama</s>), qualified by that [intention], is not achievable by effort because it is not desired to be done — rather, it is achievable by mere effort alone.
Precisely for this reason, [there is] the experience of ordinary people that 'the action is painful.'
Thus, for the desire-to-do (<s>cikīrṣā</s>), in my [view], the sole motivating factor is achievability-by-effort (<s>kṛtisādhyatva</s>); but for you, [the motivating factors] are a fourfold [set]: achievability-by-effort together with being-a-means-to-something-desired (<s>iṣṭasādhana</s>), pleasure-ness (<s>sukhatva</s>), and absence-of-pain-ness (<s>duḥkhābhāvatva</s>). As for the motivating factor of desire (<s>icchā</s>), in my [view] it is the twofold [set of] pleasure-ness and absence-of-pain-ness; [for example,] desire for rain [arises] through its being a means [to crops etc.], because the property of being a means is not incompatible with desire.
But for you it is [only desire]. In the case of eating poison, however, even though it is achievable by effort, the desire-to-do does not arise because it is a means to something overwhelmingly undesired — thus someone [argues that] being-produced-by-the-desire-to-do (<s>cikīrṣājanyatva</s>) is a qualifier of effort. That is empty — for in this case, eating poison would not be achievable by effort at all, since the effort produced for the purpose of sustaining life would not arise [toward it], making the qualifier useless.

children.text: syādetat iṣṭasādhanatābhramād viṣabhakṣaṇe caityavandane ca cikīrṣājanyakṛtisādhyatvamasti jñānaprayuktatvāt kāryatvasya tathāca sañjātabādho 'pi tatra kāryaṃ tvajñānāt pravarteta tathā tṛpto 'pi bhojane /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] It may be said that due to error regarding [something's] being a means to the desired, in eating poison and in worshipping a <s>caitya</s> (Buddhist shrine), the property of being achievable by effort produced from the desire-to-do does exist, because obligation (<s>kāryatva</s>) is prompted by knowledge. And thus, even after sublation has occurred, one would still engage in the obligatory action due to ignorance — just as a satiated person [might still engage] in eating.

children.text:
nanu svakṛtisādhyatānubhavastathā, anyatheṣṭasādhanatāsmaraṇe viṣabhakṣaṇe 'pi pravarteta, na ceṣṭasādhanatājñānaṃ vedovānubhāvakamastīti cet, na, vastutastatra kṛtisādhyatve liṅgāntareṇāptavākyena vā tadanubhavasambhavāt liṅgābhāsācchabdābhāsādvā apravṛttiprasaṅgācca, bhedāgrahavādinastacca tava tadanubhavābhāvāt, maivaṃ, svaviśeṣaṇavattāpratisandhānajanyaṃ hi kāryatājñānaṃ pravartakaṃ tathā hi kāmye puruṣaviśeṣaṇaṃ kāmanā tataḥ kāmyasādhanatājñānena yāga-pākādau kāryatājñānaṃ, nitye ca kāla-śaucādi svaviśeṣaṇaṃ, tathācaitatsandhyāyāmahaṃ kṛtisādhyasaṃdhyāvandanaḥ saṃdhyāsamaye śaucādisvaviśeṣaṇajñānajanyaṃ, taduktaṃ, sa ca kāryaviśeṣaḥ puruṣaviśeṣaṇāvagataḥ pravṛttiheturiti /
saṃjātabādhasya ca viṣabhakṣaṇe caityavandane ca bhramadaśāyāmiva neṣṭasādhanatājñānamasti yena tajjanyakāryatājñānāt pravarteta tṛptasya ca kāmanāviraheṇa iṣṭasādhanatājñānābhāva na tathā bodhaḥ /
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] But [in my view] the experience of achievability-by-one's-own-effort is sufficient [for action]; otherwise, through recollection of [something's] being a means to the desired, one would engage even in eating poison. And there is no knowledge of being-a-means-to-the-desired that the <s>Veda</s> or [anything else] can produce.
[Reply:] No — because in reality, the experience of achievability-by-effort in that case is possible through another inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) or through a reliable statement (<s>āptavākya</s>); and because of the undesirable consequence of non-engagement even from a pseudo-mark (<s>liṅgābhāsa</s>) or a pseudo-testimony (<s>śabdābhāsa</s>); and for you, the proponent of non-apprehension-of-difference, because of the absence of that experience.
[Reply:] It should not be so [objected], because the knowledge of obligation (<s>kāryatājñāna</s>) that motivates [action] is produced from the recollection of possessing one's own qualifications (<s>svaviśeṣaṇavattāpratisandhāna</s>). Thus, in the case of optional rites (<s>kāmya</s>), desire (<s>kāmanā</s>) is the person's qualification, and from that, through knowledge of [the rite's] being a means to [fulfilling] the desire, knowledge of obligation arises regarding sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>), cooking (<s>pāka</s>), etc. In obligatory rites (<s>nitya</s>), time, purity (<s>śauca</s>), etc. are the qualifications. Thus [the cognition] 'I, at the twilight hour, am one for whom the twilight prayer (<s>sandhyāvandana</s>) is achievable by effort' — [this] is produced from knowledge of one's own qualifications such as purity at the time of twilight. As it has been said: 'That specific obligation, apprehended from the person's qualification, is the cause of activity.'
And for one who has attained sublation [of error], there is no knowledge of being-a-means-to-the-desired regarding eating poison or worshipping a <s>caitya</s> — just as in the state of error — from which, through the resulting knowledge of obligation, one would engage. And for a satiated person, due to the absence of desire, there is no knowledge of being-a-means-to-the-desired, [so] there is no such cognition.

children.text:
anye tvātmano jīvitvapratisandhānajanyaṃ śrame kṛtisādhyatājñānaṃ sambhavatīti jīvanavyatiriktatvaṃ svaviśeṣaṇe viśeṣaṇamiti, tanna, śrame svecchādhīnakṛtisādhyatvābhāvāt /
iṣṭasādhanatāliṅgakaṃ kāryatājñānaṃ pravartakaṃ ityapare, tanna, nitye tadabhāvāt /
children.translated_text:
Others, however, [hold that] since the knowledge of achievability-by-effort regarding exertion can arise from the recollection of one's being alive, 'being-other-than-mere-living' is a qualifier within [the category of] one's own qualifications. That is wrong — because in exertion there is no achievability-by-effort dependent on one's own will.
[Yet] others [hold that] the knowledge of obligation based on the inferential mark of being-a-means-to-the-desired is the motivating factor. That too is wrong — because in obligatory rites (<s>nitya</s>) that [inferential mark] is absent.

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 79)
children.translated_text: [page 079]

children.text:
nanu viṣabhakṣaṇavyāvṛttamiṣṭasādhanatvameva kṛtisādhyatājñāne viṣayatayā viśeṣaṇamastu svaviśeṣaṇavattājñānajanyatvāpekṣayā laghutvāt /
kiñcopāyaviṣayā
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] Let being-a-means-to-the-desired, excluding [cases like] eating poison, be the qualifier in the content of the knowledge of achievability-by-effort — [this is preferable] because it is simpler than [requiring] the condition of being produced from knowledge of possessing one's own qualifications.
Furthermore, [the desire-to-do,] directed toward the means —

children.text: cikīrṣā iṣṭasādhanatājñānasādhyā upāyecchātvāt vṛṣṭīcchāvat /
children.translated_text: The desire-to-do (<s>cikīrṣā</s>) is achievable through the knowledge of being-a-means-to-the-desired, because it is a desire for means (<s>upāyecchā</s>), like the desire for rain.

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 81)
children.translated_text: [page 081]

children.text:
bhogacikīrṣāyāṃ tadabhāvāvaprayojakamiṣṭasādhanatvamiti cet, na, tavāpi svaviśeṣaṇadhījanyatvābhāvena tatra tasyāprayojakatvāt /
kṛtihetucikīrṣāyāṃ tat prayojakaṃ, na ca bhogacikīrṣā tathā, upāyacikīrṣāta eva kṛtisambhavāt, iti cet, tulyamiti, maivaṃ, sādhyatva-sādhanatvayorvirodhenaikatra jñātumaśakyatvāt /
asiddhāvasthasya hi sādhyatvaṃ siddhatādaśāyāṃ tadabhāvāt siddhatādaśāyāñca sādhanatvaṃ asiddhāvasthāvataḥ kāryānutpatteḥ tathāca pākāderasiddhatva-siddhatvajñāne sādhyatva-sādhanatvagrahaḥ /
na caikamekenaikadā siddhamamasiddhañca iti jñāyate /
na ca svarūpagatatāsādhyatva-sādhanatvayorato na virodha iti vācyam /
yadi hi svarūpanibandhanaṃ tadubhayaṃ tadā tatsvarūpaṃ sadaiva siddhamasiddhañca syāt, bhinnanirūpitatve 'pi tayoḥ siddhatvāsiddhatve anavagamyājñānāt, tasmāt samayabhedopādhika eva tadubhayasambandhaḥ pāke /
(Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 86)
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] In the desire-to-enjoy (<s>bhogacikīrṣā</s>), [the property of] being-a-means-to-the-desired is not a motivating factor even in its absence. [Reply:] No — because for you as well, due to the absence of being produced from knowledge of one's own qualifications, [that property] is not a motivating factor there.
[Objection:] In the desire-to-do that is the cause of effort, that [being-a-means-to-the-desired] is a motivating factor; but the desire-to-enjoy is not like that, because effort is possible from the desire-for-means (<s>upāyacikīrṣā</s>) alone. [Reply:] The same [objection applies to your view]. [Counter-reply:] It should not be so, because achievability (<s>sādhyatva</s>) and instrumentality (<s>sādhanatvā</s>) are contradictory and cannot be known simultaneously in one thing.
For the property of being-to-be-achieved belongs to what is in an unaccomplished state, and is absent in the accomplished state; while the property of being-a-means belongs to what is in the accomplished state, since the effect does not arise from what is unaccomplished. Thus, the apprehension of both achievability and instrumentality [arises from] the knowledge of cooking etc. as being in unaccomplished and accomplished states.
And it is not the case that one and the same thing is known simultaneously as both accomplished and unaccomplished.
Nor should it be said that both [properties] are grounded in the intrinsic nature [of the thing] and hence are not contradictory —
for if both were grounded in the intrinsic nature, then that very nature would always be simultaneously accomplished and unaccomplished. Even if [these properties] are determined with reference to different [factors], the accomplished-ness and unaccomplished-ness remain unascertained due to ignorance. Therefore the connection of both [properties] with cooking is contingent on a temporal distinction.
(Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 86)

children.text:
idānīṃ sādhyatvaṃ agre sādhanatvaṃ jñāyata iti cet, na, idānīmagrimapadārthayornānātvādananugamena vyāptyagrahāt śabdena tathā pratipādayitumaśakyatvāt gauravācca /
na ca kṛtitaḥ siddhamiṣṭasādhanamitijñānāt cikīrṣā, na hi siddhaṃ kaścit cikīrṣati, kṛteḥ pūrva kṛtitaḥ siddhamiti jñānābhavācca /
na ca kṛtisādhyatvena pākāderiṣṭasādhatvāt sādhanatvamapi sādhyam /
na hi kṛtisādhyatvena pākasyaudanasādhanatā, ityuktaṃ tasmāt kṛta -kriyamāṇavilakṣaṇaṃ kṛtyanantarabhaviṣyattārūpaṃ kṛtisādhyatvaṃ cikīrṣāprayojakaṃ tādṛśañca sādhanatvavirodhyeva /
kiñca sādhanatvasya siddhamātradharmatvāt sādhanatvajñānamicchāvirodhi, na hi kaścit siddhamicchatītyuktam /
etena vṛṣṭyādāviṣṭasādhanatājñānamupāyecchākāraṇatvena kḷptamiti nirastam /
kathaṃ tarhi svato 'sundare vṛṣṭyādivicchā, tatsādhyeṣṭajñānāditi gṛhāṇa /
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] 'Achievability is known now, and instrumentality later.' No — because since the referents of 'now' and 'later' are different, [the invariable concomitance] cannot be grasped due to lack of a common thread (<s>anugama</s>); and because it cannot be taught thus through language; and because of prolixity (<s>gaurava</s>).
Nor does the desire-to-do arise from the knowledge 'that which is desired as a means is accomplished through effort' — for no one desires to do what is already accomplished; and prior to effort, there is no knowledge 'it is accomplished through effort.'
Nor is instrumentality also something-to-be-achieved because cooking etc. is a desired means through its achievability-by-effort.
For the instrumentality of cooking in relation to cooked rice is not [itself] through achievability-by-effort — this has been stated. Therefore, achievability-by-effort (<s>kṛtisādhyatva</s>) as having the form of 'that which will come into being immediately after effort,' distinct from what has been done and what is being done, is the motivating factor of the desire-to-do; and such [achievability] is indeed contradictory to instrumentality.
Furthermore, since instrumentality is a property belonging only to what is accomplished, knowledge of instrumentality is incompatible with desire — for it has been stated that no one desires what is [already] accomplished.
By this, [the view] that in [cases like] rain etc., knowledge of being-a-means-to-the-desired is established as the cause of the desire for means — is also refuted.
How then [does] the desire for rain etc., which is not intrinsically pleasant, [arise]? Accept that it arises from knowledge of the desired [result] that is achievable through it.

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 90)
children.translated_text: [page 090]

children.text:
anye tu sukha-duḥkhābhāva-tatsādhaneṣṭicchāprayojakamanugatamuddeśyatvaṃ puruṣārthapadavedanīyaṃ dharmāntaramasti anugatakāryasyānugatakāraṇaniyamyatvāt /
tadeva duḥkha-tatsādhanādau cikīrṣāprayojakamiti /
na ca duḥkhavirodhitvameva tathāstīti vācyam /
sahānavasthānaniyamavirodhasyāsambhavāt, badhya-dhātaka bhāvasyaikasamaye samānādhikaraṇyābhāvasya ca yatnādi sādhāraṇyāditi /
tanna /
tadajñāne 'pi sukhatvajñānādicchotpatteḥ, na hi sukhatve jñāte dharmāntarajñānaṃ vinā necchati, tathātve svataḥ prayojanahānyāpatteḥ, tadeva hi svataḥ prayojanaṃ tadavagataṃ sat svavṛttitayeṣyate /
kiñcānugatadharmakalpanāpi kāraṇe /
children.translated_text:
Others, however, [maintain that] there exists a distinct property called 'being-the-object-of-intention' (<s>uddeśyatva</s>), which is a common thread [and] the motivating factor of desire for pleasure, absence of pain, and the means to those — expressible by the term <s>puruṣārtha</s> (human goal) — because a common effect is necessarily governed by a common cause.
That very [property] is the motivating factor of the desire-to-do regarding pain, its means, etc.
Nor should it be said that contrariety to pain alone serves as such [a motivating factor] —
because the impossibility of [defining] contrariety as the rule of non-co-existence, because [the relation of] being-what-is-to-be-overcome and being-what-overcomes cannot occur simultaneously in the same locus, and because [these relations] are common to effort and the like.
That is wrong —
because even without knowledge of that [distinct property], desire arises from knowledge of pleasure-ness etc.; for it is not the case that when pleasure-ness is known, one does not desire without knowledge of a further property. If it were so, there would be the undesirable consequence that [pleasure] would lose its character of being intrinsically a human goal (<s>svataḥ prayojana</s>); for that which is intrinsically a human goal, when apprehended, is desired by virtue of its own occurrence.
Furthermore, the postulation of a common property in the cause [is also problematic] —

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 93)
children.translated_text: [page 093]

children.text:
na ca sukhādi icchākaraṇaṃ anāgatatvāt, kintu tadavagamaḥ, tarhi sukhādijñāne tat svarūpasadevecchāprayojakamastviti cet, na, yathā hyuddeśyatvaṃ sukhajñānādiṣūtpadyate anyataratvāt tṛṇāraṇi-maṇinyāyādvā tathaivecchaiva jāyatāṃ, kṛtisādhyatvañca kṛtau satyāṃ agrimakṣaṇe svarūpaṃ na kṛtiṃ vinā, kṣemasādhāraṇañcaitat /
kṛtisādhyatvañca na kṛteḥ pūrvaṃ /
nanu kṛtau naṣṭāyāṃ sannapi dharmī na kāryaḥ tathāca kathaṃ kārye 'pūrve kāmino 'nvayaḥkṣaṇikatvena kriyātulyatvāditi cet, na, yadvṛttikāmyasādhanatvaṃ tatra kāryatā buddheḥ prayojakatvāt na tu kāryatāviśiṣṭasya kāmyasādhanateti vyāptiḥ /
nanu pākādau kṛtisādhyatājñānaṃ na pratyakṣeṇa kṛtyanantaraṃ pāke sati kṛtisādhyatājñānaṃ tasmin sati kṛtirityanyonyāśrayāt kṛtisādhyatotīrṇe cikīrṣā-kṛtyorasambhavācceti cet, na, pāko matkṛtisādhyaḥ matkṛtiṃ vinā asattve sati madiṣṭasādhanatvāt daivādyanadhīnatve sati madiṣṭasādhanatvādvā madbhojanavadityanumānāt svakṛtisādhyatājñānaṃ yasya yadiṣṭasādhanaṃ yatkṛtiṃ vinā yadā na sambhavati tat tadā tatkatisādhyaṃ iti vyāpteḥ /
asiddhasyeṣṭasādhanatvābhāvāt, balavadaniṣṭānanubandhitvañca liṅgaviśeṣaṇaṃ tena na madhu-viṣasaṃmpṛktānnabhojane vyabhicāraḥ sāmānyatastasyāpi kṛtisādhyatotīrṇe na vyabhicāraḥ sāmānyatastasyāpi kṛtisādhyatvāt, atītatādaśāyāñcātītaudanecchāviraheṇeṣṭasādhanatvābhāvāt /
ata eva nidāghadūnadehovarṣati vāride toyadātoyalābhasambhāvanāyāṃ vā saro 'vagāhane na pravartate iṣṭasantāpaśāntisādhanatoyasambandhasya svakṛtiṃ vināpi siddhipratisandhānena liṅgābhāvena svakṛtisādhyatvajñānābhāvāt /
yadā ca matkṛtiṃ vinā na sambhavatīti pratisandhatte tadā pravartate /
children.translated_text: And it is not the case that pleasure and the like are the instrumental cause of desire, since they are future [and thus non-existent]; rather, it is the cognition of them [that is the cause]. Then let the cognition of pleasure, together with its intrinsic form, be the cause of desire—no, because just as the property of being a purpose arises in the cognition of pleasure and so on, either from being one or the other, or by the analogy of the fire-stick and the jewel, so too let desire itself arise. And the property of being achievable through effort (<s>kṛtisādhyatva</s>)—when effort exists, the intrinsic form [arises] at the next moment, not without effort—and this is common with <s>Kṣema</s>'s [view]. And the achievability through effort does not [exist] before the effort. Objection: even when the effort has ceased, the property-bearer, though existing, is not the effect; so how is there co-occurrence of desire in a novel effect? Because [the effect], being momentary, is like an action. No—because the cognition that 'that in which desire-object-instrumentality resides, there is effect-hood' is the cause, not the pervasion that 'what is an instrument of the desired, qualified by effect-hood, is achievable through effort.' Objection: in cooking and the like, the knowledge of achievability through effort is not by perception; that knowledge arising when cooking occurs after effort, and effort arising when that knowledge exists—this is mutual dependence; and when achievability through effort has passed, desire and effort are impossible. No—because from the inference 'cooking is achievable through my effort, since without my effort, when it would not exist, it is an instrument of my desired [end]—or, since when not dependent on fate and the like, it is an instrument of my desired [end]—like my eating,' the knowledge of achievability through one's own effort [arises]. The pervasion is: whatever is an instrument of someone's desired [end] that would not exist at a time without that person's effort, that is at that time achievable through that person's effort. Because what is unestablished [future] lacks desired-instrument-hood, and the qualification that it is not accompanied by a stronger undesired [consequence] is a qualifier of the inferential mark—hence there is no deviation in the case of eating food mixed with honey and poison. In general, there is no deviation even when achievability through effort has passed, because that too is achievable through effort; and in the past state, due to the absence of desire for past rice, there is absence of desired-instrument-hood. For this very reason, one whose body is afflicted by summer heat does not engage in bathing in a lake when it is raining, or when there is a possibility of obtaining water from a water-giver—because there is no knowledge of achievability through one's own effort, due to the absence of the inferential mark, since one recognizes that the connection with water that is the instrument of cooling the desired heat-affliction is achievable even without one's own effort. And when one recognizes 'it is not possible without my effort,' then one engages in action.

children.text:
yasya santāpaśāntimamātramiṣṭaṃ sa sato 'vagāhanasyeṣṭasādhanatvameva na pratisandhatte upasthitavṛṣṭito 'pi tatsambhavāditi kaścit, tanna toyasambandhatvena santāpaśāntisādhanatvaṃ tasya ca saro 'vagāhane 'pi sattvāt anyathā vṛṣṭirapi tatsādhanaṃ na syāt saro 'vagāhanādapi tatsiddheḥ /
kāryasādhanatvañca kṛtisādhyatve na liṅgaṃ pākādivadodanāderapi pravṛtteḥ pūrvaṃ kṛtisādhyatvajñāne hetvabhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Someone [says]: one whose desired [end] is merely the cooling of heat-affliction does not recognize the desired-instrument-hood of bathing that already exists, because that [cooling] is possible even from imminent rain. That is not so—because the instrument-hood of cooling heat-affliction consists in being connected with water, and that exists also in lake-bathing; otherwise rain too would not be an instrument of that, since that [cooling] is accomplished even by lake-bathing. And being an instrument of the effect is not an inferential mark for achievability through effort—because, as with cooking, for rice and the like too, there is no cause for the knowledge of achievability through effort prior to [the first] action.

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 111)
children.translated_text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 111)

children.text:
nanvevaṃ liṅgajñānameva pravartakaṃ astu prāthamikatvāt āvaśyakatvāñca /
na ca lāghavāt kṛtisādhyatvajñānaṃ tathā, kṛtisādhyatānumitau tadā mānābhāvena yugapadupasthityabhāvāt pravṛttisāmagṣānumitipravibandhāñceti cet, na, liṅgajñāne kṛtisādhyatvāprakāśe tatprakārakacikīrṣāyāṃ tasyāhetutvāt /
ata eva liṅgāntarajñānamapi na pravartakam /
nanu pākādiḥ kṛtaḥ kriyamāṇovā na pakṣaḥ tasya kṛtisādhyatve bādhāt, nāpyanāgataḥ, bhāvipāke mānābhāvenāśrayāsiddheḥ, pākatvaṃ bhaviṣyadvṛtti sāmānyatvāt gotvavat iti mānamiti cet, na, mānābhāvena gotve 'pi tasyāprasiddheḥ /
pākamātraṃ pakṣa iti cet, na, mātrārtho yadi pākatvaṃ tadā bādholiṅgāsiddhiśca /
sarvapākaparatve ca tasya siddhabhāge bādho 'nāgatabhāge cāśrayāsiddhiḥ /
vartamānādyudāsīnaḥ pākaḥ pakṣaḥ pākasāmānye ca kṛtisādhyatvaṃ na bādhitamityapi na, siddhasya pakṣatvaṃ nāsiddhasyetyanumiteḥ siddhaviṣayatve bādhāt bhinnaviṣayatve vā siddhaviṣayecchāpravṛttyādyanutpādakatvācca /
kṛta-kriyamāṇasādhāraṇakṛti sādhyatvajñānādevāsiddhaviṣayā cikīrṣā kṛtiścotpadyate, ananyagatikatvena tathākāraṇasvabhāvakalpanāditi, cet, tarhi yādṛśaṃ kṛtisādhyatvaṃ cikīrṣāyāṃ prakāraḥ tādṛśaṃ jñāne nāstītyanyaprakārakajñānādeva cikīrṣā syāt /
tathā ca liṅgajñānameva pravṛttiheturastu prāthamikatvāt /
children.translated_text: Objection: let the knowledge of the inferential mark alone be the cause of action, since it is primary and necessary. And it is not the case that the knowledge of achievability through effort is so due to parsimony, because at the time of inferring achievability through effort, due to the absence of a means of valid knowledge, simultaneous presentation does not occur, and there is obstruction to the inference of the causal complex of action. No—because when the knowledge of the inferential mark does not reveal the achievability through effort, it cannot be a cause of the desire to act (<s>cikīrṣā</s>) which has that [achievability] as its qualifier. For this very reason, the knowledge of a different inferential mark also is not a cause of action. Objection: cooking that has been done or is being done is not the subject of inference (<s>pakṣa</s>), since its achievability through effort is defeated [by the fact it's already accomplished]; nor is future [cooking the subject], because of the fallacy of unestablished substratum—there being no means of valid knowledge for future cooking. If [one says] 'cooking-hood' will exist in the future, being a universal like cow-hood, that is a means of valid knowledge—no, because due to the absence of a means of valid knowledge, that [universal existence] is not established even for cow-hood. If [one says] mere cooking is the subject—no, because if 'mere' means cooking-hood, there is defeat and unestablished inferential mark. And if it refers to all cooking, there is defeat regarding the established portion and unestablished substratum regarding the future portion. [If one says] the subject is cooking indifferent to present and other [times], and achievability through effort in cooking-universal is not defeated—this too is incorrect, because inference has the rule that what is established is the subject, not what is unestablished; if its object is the established, there is defeat; if a different object, since it does not produce desire, action, and so on regarding the established [future cooking]. [If one says] from the knowledge of achievability through effort common to what has been done and what is being done, desire and effort regarding the unestablished [future] arise, because there is no other recourse and such a causal nature is postulated—then, whatever form of achievability through effort is the qualifier in desire, that form does not exist in the knowledge [of established cooking]; so desire would arise from knowledge with a different qualifier. And in that case, let the knowledge of the inferential mark alone be the cause of action, since it is primary.

children.text:
yattu smṛtapāke kṛtisādhyatvāsaṃsargāgrahātpravṛttiḥ sa cāsaṃsargāgrahaḥ iṣṭasādhanatāgrahāditi /
tanna, smṛtapākasya siddhatvena tatra kāryatvāsaṃsargagrahe 'numānabādhāt /
children.translated_text: As for [the view that] regarding remembered cooking, action arises from the non-grasping of the non-connection with achievability through effort, and that non-grasping of non-connection is from the grasping of desired-instrument-hood—that is not so, because since remembered cooking is established [already accomplished], when the non-connection with effect-hood there is grasped, there is defeat by inference.

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 117)
children.translated_text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 117)

children.text:
smṛtapākasya siddhatvaṃ tadā na gṛhyate iti cet, tarhi smṛtapākasya siddhatvagrahe odanārthī pāke na pravarteta, tatra pākādau siddhatvagrahāttadasaṃsargagraha iti cetulyam / api ca smṛtapāke kāryatvāsaṃsargādvidyamānāsaṃsargāgrahādvisaṃvādinī pravṛttiḥ syāt /
kiñcaivaṃ siddhapākajñānādajñāte 'siddhe pāke icchā-pravṛttī syātāmiti /
atra brūmaḥ /
pāke kṛtisādhyatvaṃ siddhat siddhe bādhāt anāgatapākamādāya sidhyati /
pakṣatāvacchedakadharmasāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ sādhyamānasya liṅgena sidhyatītyanumāne kḷtvāt yathā prasiddhavahnibādhe 'pi vahnimātraṃ na bādhitaṃ ityaprasiddho 'pi vahniḥ sidhyati tathā prasiddhapāke kṛtisādhyatvabādhe 'pi pākamātre na bādhitamityaprasiddhaṃ pākamādāya tatsidhyati, aprasiddhayoḥ pakṣasādhyayoḥ siddhāvaviśeṣāt, tasmāt asiddhasya kvacit siddhe siddhe siddhasya ca kvacit /
aprasiddhasya cāsiddhe siddhistenānumā tridhā /
anyathā kṛtisādhyeṣṭasādhanatāpakṣe 'pi pākādau kṛtisādhyatvaṃ kathamavagamyeta / kiñca tavāpīṣṭasādhanatājñānāt kathaṃ vṛṣṭyādāvicchā siddhatvasyecchāvirodhitvāt anāgatasya jñātumaśakyatvāt /
ata eva siddhāsiddhaviṣayatvanirāsena sukhādijñānāt phale 'pi neccheti na vṛṣṭyādāviṣṭasādhanatāpi /
na ca vṛṣṭyādisādhyeṣṭajñānāt vṛṣṭyādāvicchā, icchāyāḥ siddhāsiddhavṛṣṭyāditatphalaviṣayatvavikalpagrāsāt /
atha sāmānyalakṣaṇapratyāsattyā vṛṣṭyāditvena sukhāditvena ca siddhāsiddhavṛṣṭyādi-tatphalaviṣayakaṃ jñānamutpannaṃ tena siddhaṃ virodhinaṃ tyaktva asiddhaviṣayecchotpadyate, yadi ca sāmānyalakṣaṇā nāsti tadā yena rūpeṇeṣṭasādhanatvagrahaḥ tena rūpeṇa jñāte siddhe vecchotpadyate, anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ tādṛśajñānasya tādṛśecchājanakatvāvadhāraṇāt sukhecchāyāmapyekaṃ iti cet, tarhi mamāpi pākatvācchedena kṛtisādhyatājñānādanāgate cikīrṣā tacca jñānaṃ sakalapākaviṣayaṃ sannikṛṣṭapākaviṣayaṃ vetyanyadetat /
bālasya vyāptyādyagraheṇādyā pravṛttirjīvanādṛṣṭodbodhitajanmāntarasaṃskārajanyāt stanapānaṃ kāryamiti smaraṇāt tavāpīṣṭasādhanatāsmaraṇāt tatra pravṛttiḥ ananyagatikatvāt /
na ca janmāntare 'pi paryanuyogaḥ /
janmadhārāyā anāditvāt pratyakṣānumānamūlakatvācca nāndhaparamparā /
vastutastu śuṣkakaṇṭhatayā bālo duḥkhamanubhavan virodhitayā sukhaṃ smarati, tataḥ sukhatvajñānāt sukhavṛttikāryatvaṃ sukhavṛttitayā, antaraṅgatvāt na tu stanapānamiṣṭasādhanamiti smaraṇaṃ, sukhāvṛttitvena vahiraṅgatvāt sukhakāryatvañca stanapānamapi viṣayaḥ tena stanapāne kāryatvajñānādeva pravṛttiḥ, iṣṭasādhanatājñānasya tadānīṃ sāmāgṣabhāvāt evañcādyapravṛttau kāryatvajñānaṃ prayojakaṃ kḷptamityagre 'pi tadeva pravartakaṃ kḷptatvāt /
children.translated_text: If [one says] the established-ness of remembered cooking is not grasped at that time—then, when the established-ness of remembered cooking is grasped, one desiring rice would not engage in cooking; the same [objection applies] since from the grasping of established-ness in that cooking, there is grasping of non-connection [with effect-hood]. Moreover, regarding remembered cooking, since non-connection with effect-hood is a real non-connection, from non-grasping of a real non-connection, the resulting action would be unreliable. Furthermore, thus from the knowledge of established cooking, desire and action would arise regarding an unestablished [future] cooking that is unknown. Here we say: achievability through effort in cooking—since there is defeat regarding the established [case]—is established by taking future cooking [as the subject]. Since co-location of the subject-delimiting property with what is being proved is established by the inferential mark—this is settled in inference—just as even when there is defeat regarding well-known fire, fire in general is not defeated, and thus even unestablished fire is established; similarly, even when achievability through effort is defeated regarding established cooking, it is not defeated regarding cooking in general; thus, taking unestablished cooking, that [achievability through effort] is established. Because there is no distinction in the establishment of an unestablished subject and an unestablished predicate. Therefore: of the unestablished, sometimes the established is established; of the established, sometimes [something else]; and of the unestablished, [something] in the unestablished is established—thus inference is threefold. Otherwise, even in the subject of achievability-through-effort-desired-instrument-hood, how would achievability through effort in cooking and the like be cognized? Moreover, even for you, from the knowledge of desired-instrument-hood, how is there desire regarding rain and the like, since established-ness contradicts desire, and the future cannot be known? For this very reason, by removing the restriction to established and unestablished objects, it is not the case that from the knowledge of pleasure and so on there is no desire even regarding the result; nor is there desired-instrument-hood even regarding rain and the like. And it is not the case that from the knowledge of the desired achievable through rain and so on, there is desire regarding rain and so on—because desire is subject to the dilemma of having as its object either established or unestablished rain and the like, or their results. Now, if through <s>sāmānyalakṣaṇā</s> (generic extraordinary perception), a cognition arises having as its object established and unestablished rain and so on, and their results, under the form of rain-hood and pleasure-hood, then abandoning the established which is contradictory, desire arises regarding the unestablished object; and if <s>sāmānyalakṣaṇā</s> does not exist, then in whatever form desired-instrument-hood is grasped, in that very form desire arises regarding the known or established—because from positive and negative concomitance, such knowledge is ascertained to produce such desire; even in the desire for pleasure there is one [principle]. If so, then for me too, from the knowledge of achievability through effort delimited by cooking-hood, there is desire to act regarding the future [cooking]; and whether that knowledge has all cooking as its object or proximate cooking as its object is another matter. The first action of an infant, who does not grasp <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) and so on, arises from the memory 'sucking milk is an effect,' generated by impressions from a previous birth awakened by the <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit) governing life—for you too, from the memory of desired-instrument-hood, there is action there, since there is no other recourse. And there is no infinite regress into previous births, because the stream of births is beginningless, and because it is grounded in perception and inference, there is no blind succession. In reality, however, the infant, experiencing suffering due to a dry throat, remembers pleasure as its opposite; then from the knowledge of pleasure-hood, the effect-hood residing in pleasure [is cognized], because of being pleasure-residing, being the proximate [cause]—not the memory 'sucking milk is an instrument of the desired,' because of being external due to not residing in pleasure. And effect-hood in pleasure has sucking milk too as its object; hence action regarding sucking milk arises from the knowledge of effect-hood alone, since the knowledge of desired-instrument-hood does not at that time form part of the causal complex. And thus, since the knowledge of effect-hood is established as the cause of the first action, it is the cause of subsequent actions too, being already established.

children.text:
navīnāstu mamedaṃ kṛtisādhyamiti jñānaṃ na pravartakaṃ anāgataviṣaye pratyakṣānumānayorasambhavāt, kintu yādṛśasya puruṣasya kṛtisādhyaṃ yaddṛṣṭaṃ tādṛśatvamātmanaḥ pratisandhāya tatra pravartate, tathāhyodanakāmasya tatsādhanatājñānavataśca taṇḍulādyupakaraṇavataḥ pākaḥ kṛtisādhyaḥ ahamapi ca tādṛśa iti jñānāt pāke pravartate /
evañcānyakṛtapāke kṛtisādhyatājñānaṃ ātmanaḥ pāke kṛtisādhyatvaprayojakaviśeṣaṇavattvajñānañca prapartakaṃ /
anyatrāpi pravṛttirevamevetyanāditaiva /
ata eva sañcātabādhaścaityavandane viṣayabhakṣaṇe ca na pravartate iṣṭasādhanatā jñānavato hi tat kṛtisādhyaṃ /
na ca sañjātabādhastatra iṣṭasādhanatājñānavān /
evaṃ tṛptīcchāvato 'pi bhojanaṃ kṛtisādhyaṃ tṛptaśca na tṛptīcchāvattvamātmanyavetīti na bhojane pravartate /
children.translated_text:
The newer [logicians] (<s>navīna</s>), however, [hold that] the cognition 'this is achievable by my effort' is not the motivating factor, because perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) and inference (<s>anumāna</s>) are impossible regarding what is yet to come. Rather, [one acts] by recollecting one's own similarity to a person of the kind for whom something was seen to be achievable by effort, and then engages in that [action]. Thus, for one who desires cooked rice (<s>odana</s>), who possesses knowledge of its being a means [to satisfaction], and who has the materials such as uncooked rice (<s>taṇḍula</s>) etc. — cooking (<s>pāka</s>) is achievable by effort. [And the agent thinks] 'I too am of that kind' — from this knowledge, he engages in cooking.
Thus, in the case of cooking done by another, the knowledge of achievability-by-effort together with the knowledge of possessing the qualifications that motivate achievability-by-effort in one's own cooking — [these two together] are the motivating factors.
Activity in all other cases too is exactly like this, being beginningless [in this pattern].
Precisely for this reason, one who has attained sublation [of error] does not engage in worshipping a <s>caitya</s> (Buddhist shrine) or eating poison — for that is achievable by effort [only] for one who possesses knowledge of [its] being-a-means-to-the-desired.
And one who has attained sublation does not possess knowledge of being-a-means-to-the-desired regarding those [actions].
Likewise, eating is achievable by effort for one who desires satisfaction; and a satisfied person does not cognize the property of desiring satisfaction in himself — therefore he does not engage in eating.

children.text:
atinavīnāstu yādṛśasyetyādau avigītatvaṃ tatkṛtau viśeṣaṇamāhuḥ /
sañjātabādhastu viṣabhakṣaṇaṃ caityavandanañca vigītakṛtitādhyatvenaiva jānātīti tatra na pravartate /
children.translated_text:
The most recent [logicians] (<s>atinavīna</s>), however, state that 'being-undisputed' (<s>avigītatva</s>) is a qualifier in the effort regarding [the expression] 'of the kind for whom' etc.
One who has attained sublation knows eating poison and worshipping a <s>caitya</s> only as having disputed achievability-by-effort (<s>vigītakṛtisādhyatva</s>) — hence he does not engage in those [actions].

children.text: pravṛttiviṣayaśca sāmānyataḥ kālāsambhinnaḥ pākādirjñāyate, pravṛttimahimnā cānāgatapākasiddhiḥ , cikīrṣā ca kālāsambhinnaviṣayā na tu bhāvinaṃ kṛtyā sādhayāmītyākāraiveti /
children.translated_text: And the object of activity is known generally as temporally undifferentiated (<s>kālāsambhinna</s>) — cooking etc. [is cognized without temporal specificity]. And the accomplishment of future cooking is [effected] through the power of activity itself. And the desire-to-do (<s>cikīrṣā</s>) has a temporally undifferentiated object — it is not of the form 'I shall accomplish through effort what is yet to come.'

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 144)
children.translated_text: [page 144]

children.text: vidhivādasiddhāntaḥ
children.translated_text: The established conclusion of the doctrine of injunction (<s>vidhivādasiddhānta</s>)

children.text:
atrocyate /
viṣabhakṣaṇādivyāvṛttaṃ kṛtisādhyatvajñāne iṣṭasādhanatvaṃ viṣayatayāvacchedakaṃ lāghavāt, na tu svaviśeṣaṇavattāpratisandhānajanyatvaṃ gauravāt /
na ca siddhāsiddhāvasthayoḥ sādhyatva-sādhanatvayorvirodhaḥ, nirviśeṣitayostayoravirodhāt /
pāko 'siddhaḥ sādhyaḥ siddhaḥ sādhanañcetyunubhavāt /
tadā sādhyatvaṃ hi tadā sādhanatvasya virodhi niyamatastenaiva tasya pratikṣepeṇa sahānavasthānaniyamāt, na tu sādhanatvasyānyadā sādhanatvasya vā, tayorapratikṣepāt /
anyadā sādhanatve 'pi sādhanatvamastyeva sāmānyābhāve viśeṣābhāvaprasaṅgāt / evantadā asiddhatvasya tadā siddhatvaṃ virodhi niyamatastasyaiva pratikṣepāt, na tu siddhatvamātraṃ, anyadapi tatra siddhatvābhāvaprasaṅgāt, nirviśeṣitayorvirodhe ca siddhatvayoścānyataradeva pākādau syānna tu samayabhede 'pyubhayam /
na ca tadā kṛtisādhyatve sati tadeṣṭasādhanatvajñānaṃ pravartakaṃ, ata eva vājapeyena yajetetyatra yāgasya karaṇāvasthāyāṃ siddhatvena na vājapeyasya sādhyatā ekadā tayorvirodhāditi karmanāmadheyatvaṃ, na tu karaṇasya siddhatvena sādhyatvavirodhaḥ yogasvarūpe tayoḥ sattvāt /
children.translated_text:
Here it is stated:
Being-a-means-to-the-desired (<s>iṣṭasādhanatvā</s>), excluding [cases like] eating poison etc., is the delimiting factor (<s>avacchedaka</s>) as content within the knowledge of achievability-by-effort — [this is accepted] because of parsimony (<s>lāghava</s>); but not being-produced-from-the-recollection-of-possessing-one's-own-qualifications, because of prolixity (<s>gaurava</s>).
Nor is there a contradiction between achievability (<s>sādhyatva</s>) and instrumentality (<s>sādhanatva</s>) in the accomplished and unaccomplished states, because when taken without qualification (<s>nirviśeṣitā</s>) they are non-contradictory.
[This is established] from the experience: 'cooking, when unaccomplished, is something-to-be-achieved; when accomplished, [it is] a means.'
For achievability-at-that-time is contradictory to instrumentality-at-that-time specifically, because of the rule that [each] excludes only its own [temporal counterpart] through the rule of non-co-existence. But [achievability-at-that-time] is not [contradictory] to instrumentality-at-another-time, or to instrumentality [in general], because there is no mutual exclusion between them.
Even when [there is] instrumentality at another time, instrumentality [in general] still exists — because the absence of the universal would entail the absence of the particular. Similarly, unaccomplished-ness-at-that-time is contradictory to accomplished-ness-at-that-time specifically, through the exclusion of that very [temporal counterpart] alone — but not to accomplished-ness as such, because otherwise accomplished-ness at other times would also be precluded. And if the unqualified [properties] were contradictory, only one of the two accomplished-nesses could exist in cooking etc. — not both even at different times.
Nor [should it be said that] when achievability-by-effort exists at that time, the knowledge of being-a-means-to-the-desired at that time is the motivating factor. Precisely for this reason, in [the injunction] 'one should sacrifice with the <s>Vājapeya</s>,' the sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) in its state of being performed is [already] accomplished, and hence the <s>Vājapeya</s> does not have achievability [at that moment] — because at one and the same time there is contradiction between [the two]. Hence it is a designation of the rite (<s>karmanāmadheya</s>). But the achievability of the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) is not contradicted by its accomplished-ness, because both [properties] exist in the essential nature of the connection (<s>yogasvarūpa</s>).

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 150)
children.translated_text: [page 150]

children.text:
atha viruddhayoravacchebhedamādaya ekatra pratītiḥ syāt /
na ca kṛtisādhyatveṣṭasādhanatvayoḥ samayabhedamādayaikatra pratītirasti, tathā liṅgābhāvāditi cet, na, sādhyatva-sādhanatvayoravirodhasyoktatvāt, evaṃ siddhatvāsiddhatvayorbhāvābhāvarūpatve 'pi na virodhaḥ ekadharmigatvena mānasiddhatvāt /
tasmāt saṃyoga-tadabhāvayoriva yena prakāreṇa yayorvirodhaḥ tena tayorekadharmigatatvaṃ na pratīyate, na tu rūpāntareṇāpīti /
api ca yadi sādhyatva-sādhanatvayorvirodhastadā tavāpīṣṭasādhanatvena kāryasādhanatvena vā kāryatvaṃ nānumīyate hetu-sādhyayorvirodhena sāmānādhikaraṇyābhāvena vyāptyasiddheḥ pakṣe sādhya-sādhanayoranyatarasattve bādhāsidhyoranyataraprasaṅgācca /
na ca vācyamidānīṃ matkṛtisādhyatvaṃ sādhyamagre madiṣṭasādhanatvaṃ hetuḥ daivādyanadhīnatve sati yadagre madiṣṭāsādhanaṃ tadidānīṃ matkṛtisādhyamiti vyāptiḥ tathāca samayabhedamādāya sādhyatva-sādhanatvayoravagama iti, idānīmagrimapadārthayornānātvādanugatarūpābhāvena vyāpteragrahāt, pākanyāyenānyatrāpi tattatsamayāntarbhāvena sādhyatva-sādhanatvayorapratītiḥ, pratītau vā mamāpīdānīṃ kṛtisādhyatve satyagre iṣṭasādhanamiti jñānaṃ pravartakamastu /
na ca pāke sādhyeṣṭakatvena kṛtisādhyatvamanumeyaṃ, asiddhāvasthāvato hi pākādiṣṭānutpatteḥ pākasya siddhatvamavagamya tatsādhyatvamiṣṭasyāvagantavyamasiddhatvañcāvagamya kṛtisādhyatvamiti siddhatvāsiddhatvayorvirodho 'trāpi durvāraḥ /
api ca svaviśeṣaṇadhījanyakāryatājñānābhāvāt sukhe kathaṃ cikīrṣā, na hi kṛtisādhyatājñānamātrāt, sā, sañjātabādhasya viṣabhakṣaṇādau cikīrṣāprasaṅgāt /
athopāyacikīrṣāyāṃ tatkāraṇaṃ icchākaraṇasukhatvajñāne kṛtisādhyatvaṃ yadā viṣayastadā sukhe cikīrṣā no cedicchāmātramiti dvayameva cikīrṣāheturiti cet, tarhīcchāhetujñāne yadā kṛtisādhyatvaṃ bhāsate tāda cikīrṣā no cedicchāmātramityeva sukha-tadupāyacikīrṣākāraṇamastu lāghavāt, sukhatvajñānavadiṣṭasādhanatājñānasyāpīcchākāraṇatvāt /
ata eva pāke iṣṭasādhanatājñāne kṛtisādhyatvaṃ viṣaya iti tatra cikīrṣā na tu vṛṣṭyādijñāne tadviṣayatvamitīcchāmātraṃ, sukhacikīrṣāyāmicchākāraṇajñāne kṛtisādhyatāviṣayake cikīrṣājanakatvāvadhāraṇāt /
anyathā tatra cikīrṣānutpatteḥ /
vastutastūpāyacikīrṣā iṣṭasādhanatājñānasādhyā upāyecchātvāt vṛṣṭīcchāvat /
na ca bhogacikīrṣāvattena vināpi syādityaprayoñjakatvaṃ, upāyecchāyāstadanvaya-vyatirekānuvidhānāt vṛṣṭeśca svato 'sundaratvenecchānutpatteḥ anugatopāyecchāyāṃ anugatasya prayojakatve sambhavati bādhakaṃ vinā tyāgāyogācca /
na ca cikīrṣānyatve sati upāyecchātvaṃ icchātvaṃ vā /
tajjanyatve prayojakaṃ, gauravāt sukhecchāyāṃ tadabhāvācca /
evañcopāyacikīrṣāyāmiṣṭasādhanatvajñāne dhruve 'tiprasaṅgavāraṇārthaṃ kṛtisādhyatvanirvāhārthañca kṛtisādhyatvamapi viṣayatayāvacchedakamastu na tu tadvihāya tanmātraṃ, kḷptakāraṇaṃ vinā kāryānupapatteḥ /
ata eva stanapānapravṛttāvapyupāyecchākāraṇatvena gṛhītasyeṣṭasādhanatvajñānasyāpi kalpanaṃ dṛṣṭānurodhitvāt kalpanāyāḥ /
nanu sādhanatvamicchāvirodhi tasya siddhadharmatvāt vṛṣṭyādau tatsādhyeṣṭajñānādiccheti cet na, nirviśeṣitayoḥ siddhatvāsiddhatvayoravirodhenecchāsādhanatvayoravirodhāt /
tadāsiddhatvaṃ tadā siddhatvañca necchāsādhanatvayoḥ prayojakamiti tathā na jñāyata eva /
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] Then, taking a difference of delimiting conditions (<s>avacchedabheda</s>), there could be a cognition of contradictories in one [locus].
But there is no cognition of achievability-by-effort and being-a-means-to-the-desired together in one [locus] by taking a temporal distinction, because there is no inferential mark for that. [Reply:] No — because the non-contradiction of achievability and instrumentality has been stated. Similarly, even though accomplished-ness and unaccomplished-ness are of the nature of existence and absence, there is no contradiction, because their co-location in one property-bearer is established by a means of valid knowledge (<s>māna</s>).
Therefore, just as with conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) and its absence — the co-location of two [properties] in one property-bearer is not cognized in the mode in which they are contradictory, but [it is possible] in another mode.
Furthermore, if there is a contradiction between achievability and instrumentality, then for you as well, obligation (<s>kāryatva</s>) cannot be inferred from being-a-means-to-the-desired or from being-a-means-to-an-effect — because the invariable concomitance (<s>vyāpti</s>) is unestablished due to the absence of co-location (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) [arising] from the contradiction between the probans (<s>hetu</s>) and the probandum (<s>sādhya</s>); and because, if one of the two — the achievable and the instrument — exists in the subject (<s>pakṣa</s>), either sublation (<s>bādha</s>) or unestablishedness (<s>asiddhi</s>) would follow.
Nor should it be said: 'achievability-by-my-effort is the probandum now, and being-a-means-to-my-desired is the probans later; and the invariable concomitance is: whatever is later a means to my desired, that is now achievable by my effort; thus, taking a temporal distinction, achievability and instrumentality are apprehended' — [this is refuted] because, the referents of 'now' and 'later' being different, there is no common form (<s>anugata</s>) by which the invariable concomitance can be grasped; and by the same reasoning as in the cooking [example], in other cases too, achievability and instrumentality are not cognized through inclusion within their respective temporal moments; or if they are so cognized, let even my [view] be that the knowledge 'achievable by effort now and a means to the desired later' is the motivating factor.
Nor can achievability-by-effort be inferred for cooking through the property of being a desired means — for since the desired [result] does not arise from cooking in its unaccomplished state, one must apprehend the accomplished-ness of cooking, and [then] apprehend the achievability of the desired [result] from that; and [one must also] apprehend its unaccomplished-ness to [infer] achievability-by-effort — thus the contradiction between accomplished-ness and unaccomplished-ness is unavoidable here as well.
Furthermore, in the absence of knowledge of obligation produced from knowledge of one's own qualifications, how [can there be] the desire-to-do regarding pleasure? For it does not [arise] from mere knowledge of achievability-by-effort alone, since otherwise there would be the undesirable consequence of the desire-to-do arising in one who has attained sublation regarding eating poison etc.
[Objection:] In the desire-for-means (<s>upāyacikīrṣā</s>), the being-a-means-to-the-desired (<s>iṣṭasādhanatvā</s>) grasped as the cause of desire for means is also the cause of desire [in general], and when achievability-by-effort is the content in the knowledge causing desire, [there arises] the desire-to-do regarding pleasure; otherwise, [there is] mere desire (<s>icchā</s>) — thus only these two together constitute the cause of the desire-to-do. [Reply:] Then [it may equally be held that] when achievability-by-effort appears in the knowledge causing desire, [there arises] the desire-to-do; otherwise, mere desire — let this alone be the cause of the desire-to-do regarding pleasure and its means, because of parsimony (<s>lāghava</s>); since the knowledge of being-a-means-to-the-desired, just like the knowledge of pleasure-ness, is also a cause of desire.
Precisely for this reason, when achievability-by-effort is the content in the knowledge of being-a-means-to-the-desired in cooking, there is the desire-to-do there; but when that [achievability] is not the content in the cognition of rain etc., there is mere desire. [This is] because the knowledge causing desire in the desire-to-do regarding pleasure is ascertained as a generator of the desire-to-do only when it has achievability-by-effort as its content.
Otherwise, the desire-to-do would not arise there.
In truth, the desire-for-means (<s>upāyacikīrṣā</s>) is achievable through the knowledge of being-a-means-to-the-desired, because it is a desire-for-means, like the desire for rain.
Nor [is there] the non-motivation [of being-a-means-to-the-desired] on the grounds that [the desire for means] could exist even without it, like the desire-to-enjoy — because the desire for means conforms to the presence and absence of that [knowledge]; and because the desire for rain does not arise [by itself] since rain is not intrinsically attractive; and because, when there is a common factor motivating a common desire for means, it cannot be abandoned without a sublating cognition.
Nor is the motivating factor [merely] being-a-desire-for-means or being-a-desire, distinct from the desire-to-do.
When [it is] its being-a-product that motivates, [there is] prolixity — because in desire for pleasure, that [qualification] is absent.
Thus, in the desire-for-means, when being-a-means-to-the-desired is fixed in the knowledge [of the object], let achievability-by-effort also be a delimiting condition as content, for the purpose of blocking over-extension and for establishing achievability-by-effort — but not that [achievability] alone to the exclusion of [being-a-means-to-the-desired]; because an effect cannot be accounted for without its established cause.
Precisely for this reason, even in the activity of an infant suckling at the breast, the knowledge of being-a-means-to-the-desired, grasped as a cause of the desire for means, is also postulated — because postulation conforms to what is observed.
[Objection:] Instrumentality is incompatible with desire, because it is a property of what is [already] accomplished; and regarding rain etc., desire [arises] from the knowledge of [rain's] being achievable as something desired. [Reply:] No — because accomplished-ness and unaccomplished-ness taken without qualification are non-contradictory, [and therefore] desire and instrumentality are non-contradictory.
That accomplished-ness-at-that-time and unaccomplished-ness-at-that-time are not the motivating factors of desire and instrumentality — [this] is simply not cognized in that manner.

children.text: yattu tatsādhyeṣṭajñānād vṛṣṭyādāviccheti, tattucchaṃ, asiddhāvasthādvṛṣṭyāderiṣeṭānutpattestasyāvaśyaṃ siddhatvamavagantavyamicchānurodhitvāccāsiddhatvamiti,
children.translated_text: As for [the claim] that desire regarding rain etc. [arises] from the knowledge of the desired [result] achievable through it — that is empty. Because since the desired [result] does not arise from rain etc. in their unaccomplished state, their accomplished-ness must necessarily be apprehended; and their unaccomplished-ness [must also be apprehended] because it conforms to desire.

children.text:
tatrāpi virodha eva /
vṛṣṭau satyāmiṣṭaṃ tayā vinā netyanvaya-vyatirekagrahasya vṛṣṭisiddhatvamādāya vṛṣṭinirūpiteṣṭasādhyakatvagrāhakatvāt /
kiñca cikīrṣājanyakṛtisādhyaṃ maṇḍalīkaraṇamityarthapratipādakaṃ 'maṇḍalīṃ kuryāditi vākyaṃ pramāṇaṃ syātviṣayābādhāt /
etena navīnamatamapyapāstaṃ, parasya hi kṛtisādhyatvaudanakāmanāvattveṣṭasādhanatājñānānāṃ jñānaṃ tathā ātmana odanakāmānāvattevaṣṭasādhanatājñānasya jñānaṃ na pravṛttikāraṇaṃ gauravāt, kintu matkṛtisādhyatve sati madiṣṭasādhanatājñānameva lāghavāt, yathā ca sādhyatva-sādhanatvayoravirodhaḥ anāgatasya pākādeḥ kṛtisādhyatvajñānañca tathopapāditameva kiñca parakṛtisādhyatvamajñātvāpi svakṛtisādhyeṣṭasādhanatājñānāt svakalpitalipyādau yauvane kāmodrekāt sambhogādau pravṛtteśca tadeva pravartakam /
vastutastu siddhaviṣayakakṛtisādhyatājñānāt kathaṃ kṛtyā sādhayāmītīcchā siddhe icchāvirahāt asiddhasyājñānāt /
atha siddhaviṣayādeva kṛtisādhyatājñānāt asiddhaviṣayā kṛtisādhyatvenecchā jñāyate icchāyā asiddhaviṣayatvasvabhāvatvādekaprakārakatvena jñāna-cikīrṣayoḥ kārya-kāraṇabhāvo na tvekaviṣayatve sati gauravāt, icchāyā anāgataviṣayatvāt tasya cājñānāt tathātvadarśanāt sukhādīcchāyāmapyevamiti cet, na, asiddhaviṣayecchānurodhenānāgatajñānopāyasya darśitatvāt /
astu caivaṃ, tathāpi kṛtisādhyatājñāne iṣṭasādhanatvameva vyāvartakamastu sva-parakīyeṣṭasādhanatājñāna-phalakāmanājñānāpekṣayā laghutvāt iṣṭasādhanatājñānajñānasya phalakāmanājñānasya ca hetutve mānābhāvācca /
children.translated_text: Even there, there is indeed a contradiction. When rain exists, the grasping of the positive and negative concomitance — 'the desired end obtains with it and not without it' — takes rain as already accomplished and thereby grasps that it is a means to the desired end as delimited by rain. Furthermore, the sentence '<s>maṇḍalīṃ kuryāt</s>' (one should make a circle), which conveys the meaning that making a circle is producible by <s>cikīrṣā</s>-generated <s>kṛti</s>, would be a valid means of knowledge, there being no sublation of its object. By this, the new view is also refuted. For the opponent holds that the cognition of the other person's producibility by <s>kṛti</s>, of having a desire for rice, and of being a means to the desired end [are all required]; likewise, the cognition of oneself as having a desire for rice and as knowing it to be a means to the desired end is not the cause of volitional activity, due to complexity. Rather, by parsimony, it is simply the cognition of being a means to the desired end while being producible by one's own <s>kṛti</s>. And just as there is no incompatibility between being-to-be-produced and being-a-means, and the cognition of the producibility by <s>kṛti</s> of future cooking and the like has been established in that manner — furthermore, even without knowing the producibility by another's <s>kṛti</s>, from the cognition that something producible by one's own <s>kṛti</s> is a means to the desired end, one engages in self-devised writing and the like, and in sexual enjoyment during youth due to the surge of desire — that alone is the impeller. In reality, how can the desire 'I shall accomplish by means of <s>kṛti</s>' arise from the cognition of producibility by <s>kṛti</s> with respect to an already accomplished object, since there is no desire toward what is already accomplished, and what is not yet accomplished is unknown? If one says that from the very cognition of producibility by <s>kṛti</s> with respect to an accomplished object, a desire with an unaccomplished object arises as having the mode of producibility by <s>kṛti</s> — since desire by its very nature has an unaccomplished object, and cognition and <s>cikīrṣā</s> stand in a cause-effect relation through having one mode, not through having one object (that being overly complex), since desire has a future object, and that is unknown, and this is observed, and this applies also to desire for pleasure and the like — if so, no, because the means of cognition regarding the future has been shown through conformity with desire for unaccomplished objects. Even granting this, still in the cognition of producibility by <s>kṛti</s>, let being-a-means-to-the-desired-end alone be the differentiator, since it is simpler than requiring cognition of being a means to one's own or another's desired end and cognition of desire for the result; and because there is no evidence for the causal status of cognition of being-a-means-to-the-desired-end-cognition and cognition of desire for the result.
