children.translated_text: The prior objection (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>) regarding the <s>apūrva</s> doctrine (<s>apūrvavāda</s>)

children.text:
atha svargakāmo yajetetyādāviṣṭasādhanatvaṃ kāryatvaṃ vā yadvidhiḥ sa samabhivyāhṛtakriyānvayī tadanyānvayī vā atra guravaḥ nāhatya kriyākāryatayā liṅgā bodhayituṃ śakyate svargakāmaniyojyānvayayogyatājñānavirahāt , kāmanāviśiṣṭasya hi mamedaṃ kāryamiti boddhṛtvaṃ niyojyatvaṃ tat kāmanāyāstadbodhopayoge sati bhavati sa ca kāmanānantaraṃ kāmyasādhanatābodhanāt kāryatā bodhe sati syāt evañca svargasādhanatābodhe sati svargakāmaniyojyānvayayogyatā /
na ca kālāntarabhāvisvarge kriyā sākṣāt paramparayā vā sādhanamiti śabdo bodhayitumarhati āśuvināśitvāt paramparāghaṭakānupasthiteśca tṛtīyaprakārābhāvācca /
anyathā tamādāya sādhanatvasambhavāt kalpyamapyapūrvaṃ na syāt iṣṭasādhanatāvidhipakṣe sphuṭaivānupapattiḥ /
kāryatāvidhipakṣe anvayaprakāratayā sādhanatvaṃ śābdamiti phalato na kaścidviśeṣaḥ /
ataḥ kriyāto 'nyat svargasādhanatārhaṃ kriyākāryatānirvāhakaṃ liṅgādyarthaḥ / nanu svajātīye 'nvayadarśanaṃ yogyatā dṛṣṭañca ghṛtapānasyāśuvināśinaḥ kālāntare puṣṭihetutvamiti cet na yathākathañcit sājātyasyāyogye 'pi sattvena yogyatayā avyāvartakatvāpatteḥ padārthatāvacchedakena sājātyasyādyajātaḥ payaḥ pibatītyādau prakṛte cāsambhavāt tasmādanvayaprayojakarūpavattvaṃ sājātyam /
ata eva dravadravyatvaṃ sekakaraṇatve prayojakaṃ ityayogyovahniḥ tadihāśuvināśinaḥ kālāntarabhāviphalajanakatve phalasamayaparyantasthāyivyāpārajanakatvaṃ prayojakamato 'pūrvaṃ vinā sājātyameva na gṛhyate ghṛtapānasya tu vaidyakopasthitadhātusāmyamādāya puṣṭisādhanatvayogyatājñānaṃ vijñasya /
atha bādhakapramāṇābhāvo yogyatā /
na ca sādhanatvamātre bādhakaṃ sākṣātdbodhe 'pi paramparāsādhanatvamādāya tadviśrāntisambhavāt /
na ca yogyānupalabdhā dvārasya bādhāt paramparāsādhanatvamapi bādhitaṃ saṃskāsyeva tasya sambhavāt anyathā vācye 'pyapūrve kriyā kāmikāryā na syāt kāmyāsādhatvāt /
na hi yadevāyogyaṃ tatpaścāt yogyaṃ ayogyatve ca niṣphalaḥ prayāsaḥ /
na ca kāmikāryamapūrvaṃ tadarthikāryā ca kriyeti vācyam /
yāge rāgādityanena virodhāt /
tathāpi dvārānupasthityā paramparāsādhanamiti jñānaṃ na bhavediti cet satyaṃ kintu svargasādhanaṃ yāga iti jñānaṃ sākṣātparamparodāsīnaṃ vastugatyā paramparāsādhanatvaviṣayakamutpadyamānaṃ nāyogyatayā paribhavituṃ śakyam /
yadi ca sākṣātparamparāviśeṣadvayavyatiriktaṃ sāmānyaṃ nāstyeva tadā ananugamaḥ kiṃ vā viśeṣayasi sākṣātparamparayā veti /
na ca yāvadviśeṣabādhe tadbidhitaṃ paramparāsādhanatve 'bādhāditi /
maivaṃ /
yogyatā hi svabādhakapramāviraho vā sakalabādhakapramāviraho vā ādye vahninā siñcatītyādau svabādhakapramā-tadvirahau samayabhedena sta iti tadeva yogyamayogyañceti prāptaṃ dvitīye tu yogyānupalabdhā tanniścayo 'śakyaḥ parapramāyā ayogyatvāt /
na ca vācyaṃ sakalabādhakapramāvirahaḥ svarūpasanneva prayojaka iti ayogye yogyatāmramādanvaya bodhābhāvaprasaṅgāt anyasya tatra bādhakapramāsattvāt /
anvayaprayojakarūpavattvena bādhakapramāviraho niścīyate iti cet tarhi prāthamikatvāt saiva yogyatā /
na ca sā prakṛte sambhavatītyuktaṃ kiñcaikaviśeṣabādhe śābdasāmānyajñānaṃ taditaraviśeṣaprakāratāniyataṃ chidrabādhe chidretaraghaṭajñānavat /
na ca dvārānupasthityā prakṛte tathā ghaṭate /
etena yaduktaṃ praśastarūpavān caitra ityatra gaura-śyāmaviśeṣānavagame 'pi rūpamātramavagamyate tadvat viśeṣānavagame 'pi sādhanatvamātramiti tatpratyuktaṃ tatraikaviśeṣabādhābhāvenaudāsīnyasambhavāt /
children.translated_text:
Now, in [injunctions] like '<s>svargakāmo yajeta</s>' ('one who desires heaven should sacrifice'), what the injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) prescribes — whether being-a-means-to-the-desired (<s>iṣṭasādhanatva</s>) or obligation (<s>kāryatva</s>) — is [the question]: does [the injunction] connect with the co-uttered action (<s>samabhivyāhṛtakriyā</s>), or with something other than that? Here, [according to] the teachers (<s>guravaḥ</s>), it is not possible to convey [the meaning] through the optative suffix (<s>liṅ</s>) as [signifying] obligation-of-the-action (<s>kriyākāryatā</s>), because of the absence of knowledge of the fitness of connection with the person-to-be-enjoined who desires heaven. For the capacity to understand 'this is my obligation' — i.e. the status of being-enjoined (<s>niyojyatva</s>) — qualified by desire, arises only when the desire is useful for that understanding; and that [understanding] would be possible only when, after [the arising of] desire, there is cognition of obligation through the cognition of being-a-means-to-the-desired. Thus, the fitness of connection with the person-to-be-enjoined who desires heaven [arises only] when there is cognition of being-a-means-to-heaven.
Nor can language convey that the action (<s>kriyā</s>) is a means — directly or indirectly — to heaven which comes at a later time, because [the action] is quickly perishable, because the intermediary links [of the causal chain] are not presented, and because of the absence of a third alternative.
Otherwise, since instrumentality could be [established] by taking that [intermediary], even <s>apūrva</s> (unseen potency), which is postulated, would not exist. In the view that [the injunction] prescribes being-a-means-to-the-desired (<s>iṣṭasādhanatāvidhi</s>), the inconsistency is obvious.
In the view that [the injunction] prescribes obligation (<s>kāryatāvidhi</s>), since instrumentality is [already] conveyed verbally as a mode of connection, there is in result no difference.
Therefore, [there must be] something other than the action that is capable of being a means to heaven and that fulfills the obligation of the action — [this is] the meaning of the optative suffix (<s>liṅ</s>) etc. [Objection:] But fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>) consists in the observation of connection in something of the same class; and it is observed that drinking ghee, though quickly perishable, is a cause of nourishment at a later time. [Reply:] No — because since any kind of class-membership exists even in what is unfit, there would be the undesirable consequence of [class-membership] being non-differentiating. [True] class-membership is [defined as] possessing a form that motivates the connection, by the delimiting factor of the relevant category — as in 'the first-born drinks milk' and the like — but this is impossible in the case at hand. Therefore, class-membership is [defined as] possessing a form that motivates the connection.
Precisely for this reason, being-a-liquid-substance is the motivating factor for instrumentality-in-sprinkling — hence fire is unfit [for that]. Here, for something quickly perishable to produce a result coming at a later time, the motivating factor is the capacity to generate an operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>) that endures until the time of the result — therefore, without <s>apūrva</s>, class-membership itself cannot be grasped. In the case of drinking ghee, however, for the learned person, the knowledge of fitness as a means to nourishment is obtained by taking into account the equilibrium of bodily humors (<s>dhātusāmya</s>) established in medical science (<s>vaidyaka</s>).
[Objection:] Fitness is the absence of a sublating means of valid knowledge (<s>bādhakapramā</s>).
But [there is] no sublation of mere instrumentality, because even in direct cognition, [the cognition] can rest in indirect instrumentality (<s>paramparāsādhanatva</s>).
Nor [should it be said that] through the non-apprehension of the fit (<s>yogyānupalabdhi</s>), the sublation of the intermediary means sublates even indirect instrumentality — because that [indirect instrumentality] is possible just like a disposition (<s>saṃskāra</s>). Otherwise, even in the case of <s>apūrva</s> to be postulated, the action would not be an optional obligation (<s>kāmikārya</s>), because of its not being a means to the desired.
For it is not the case that what is initially unfit later becomes fit; and in the state of unfitness, the effort is fruitless.
Nor should it be said that <s>apūrva</s> is the optional obligation and the action is obligatory for the sake of that [<s>apūrva</s>] —
because of the contradiction with [the statement] 'in sacrifice, passion etc.' [is prohibited].
[Objection:] Even so, through the non-presentation of the intermediary, the cognition 'this is an indirect means' would not arise. [Reply:] True, but the cognition 'sacrifice is a means to heaven' — indifferent to whether [it is] direct or indirect — arising as having indirect instrumentality as its content by the force of reality, cannot be overridden by [alleged] unfitness.
And if there is no general [instrumentality] apart from the two particulars — direct and indirect — then there would be no common thread (<s>anugama</s>). Why then do you specify 'directly or indirectly?'
Nor [should it be argued that] 'as long as the particular [mode] is not sublated, the unsublated [instrumentality] rests in indirect instrumentality.'
Do not [argue] thus.
For fitness is either the absence of its own sublating cognition, or the absence of all sublating cognitions. In the first case, in [the expression] 'sprinkle with fire' and the like, [there would be] both a sublating cognition and its absence at different times — thus the same thing would be both fit and unfit. In the second case, the ascertainment [of fitness] through non-apprehension of the fit is impossible, because of the unfitness of another's cognition.
Nor should it be said that the absence of all sublating cognitions, being of the nature of the [thing] itself, is the motivating factor — because there would be the undesirable consequence of no connection-cognition even in what is unfit, since a sublating cognition of another [party] exists there.
[Objection:] The absence of a sublating cognition is ascertained through possessing the form that motivates the connection. [Reply:] Then, being primary, that very [possessing the motivating form] is [the definition of] fitness.
But that is not possible in the case at hand, as stated. Furthermore, when one particular [mode] is sublated, the verbal general cognition is necessarily restricted to the other particular mode — like the cognition of a pot without a hole when the hole is sublated.
But in the case at hand, this does not work due to the non-presentation of the intermediary.
By this, the [following objection] is also answered: 'In [the expression] "<s>Caitra</s> is of excellent form," even without apprehending the particular — fair or dark — mere form is apprehended; similarly, even without apprehending the particular [mode], mere instrumentality [is apprehended].' [This is refuted] because there, due to the absence of sublation of any one particular, indifference is possible.

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 314)
children.translated_text: [page 314]

children.text:
etena svargakāmānvayabalāt kriyāyāḥ phalasādhanatvaṃ tadbalācca paṭoḥ saṃskāsyeva sthāyitvaṃ kalpyatāṃ kimapūrveṇa saṅkalpaviśeṣasya yāgasyāgre pratyakṣānupalabdhi rātmaviśeṣaguṇānāṃ prathamakṣaṇa eva svaviṣayakapratyakṣajananasvabhāvāt astu na caivaṃ kriyāntaramapi tathā pramāṇābhāvāt evaṃ lokaprasiddhakriyākāryatvavyutpattirapi bhagnā na bhavatīti parāstam /
svargasādhanatāyogyatayā svargakāmānvayaḥ tadanvaye ca sthāyitvaṃ ityanyonyāśrayāt lāke dharmigrāhakamānena kriyāyāḥ kṣaṇikatvaniścayācca /
children.translated_text:
By this, [the following view is refuted:] 'Through the force of the connection with [the phrase] "one who desires heaven," let the action's capacity to produce the result be postulated, and through that force, let its durability — like that of a cloth or a disposition (<s>saṃskāra</s>) — be postulated. What need is there for <s>apūrva</s>?' [Reply:] Because a sacrifice, being a particular volition (<s>saṅkalpaviśeṣa</s>), is not perceived at a later time — since qualities specific to the self (<s>ātmaviśeṣaguṇa</s>) have the nature of generating a perception of their own content at the very first moment [of their existence]. Let it be so [that there is no later perception]. But [it is not the case that] another action too [is durable] in the same way, because of the absence of a means of valid knowledge [for that]. Thus, [the objection that] even the understanding of the obligation of commonly known actions would be destroyed — [this] is set aside.
[There is] mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśraya</s>), because the connection with 'one who desires heaven' [depends on] the fitness of being a means to heaven, and the durability [depends on] that connection.

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 317)
children.translated_text: [page 317]

children.text:
nanu devapūjārtho yajiḥ pūjā cārādhanā gauravitaprītihetuḥ kriyā ato devatāprītidvārā yāgasya svargasādhanatvaṃ prīteḥ kṣaṇikatve 'pi prītyanubhavajanitasaṃskāradvārā tatsambhavāt /
ata evāgneyādau prītibhāgitayā agnagaderuddheśyatvamiti cet na yaj devapūjāyāṃ iti hi śābdikasmṛtiḥ smṛtitvādeva na svataḥ pramāṇam /
na ca yāgasya devatāprītihetutve svargasya devatāprītisādhyatve vā mānāntaramasti /
vastutastu cetane deve mānameva nāsti yatra ca viṣṇuprītikāmādivādo 'sti tatra viṣṇureva prītiḥ na tu viṣṇoḥ ṣaṣṭhyarthalakṣaṇādoṣāt viṣṇuśabdasya prītiviśeṣavācakatvaṃ veda eva kalpyate /
na ca devatāpūjārthayajyanvayabalāttathā anyonyāśrayāt /
nanvevaṃ āgneyāndīnāṃ ṣaṇāṃ kṣaṇikatvāt yogyatānavagatau paramāpūrvakāraṇatvānavagame kathamapūrvakalpaneti cet na kāmye apūrvavācyatvasthitau āgneyādau tadvārā sādhanatvasya yogyatāsambhavāt na tu prathamam /
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] The root <s>yaj</s> ('to sacrifice') is for the purpose of worship of deities (<s>devapūjā</s>). And worship is adoration — an action that causes pleasure in the one revered. Therefore, the sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) is a means to heaven through the intermediary of the deity's pleasure (<s>devatāprīti</s>); even though pleasure is momentary, [the result] is possible through the intermediary of a disposition (<s>saṃskāra</s>) generated by the experience of pleasure.
Precisely for this reason, in the <s>Āgneya</s> sacrifice etc., <s>Agni</s> and the other [deities] are the intended recipients (<s>uddeśya</s>) by virtue of being partakers of pleasure. [Reply:] No — the tradition (<s>smṛti</s>) '<s>yaj</s> means worship of deities' is a textual tradition, and being a <s>smṛti</s>, it is not independently authoritative.
Nor is there any other means of valid knowledge for the sacrifice being a cause of the deity's pleasure, or for heaven being achievable through the deity's pleasure.
In truth, there is no means of valid knowledge whatsoever for a sentient deity. And where there is [an expression like] 'one who desires <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s pleasure,' there '<s>Viṣṇu</s>' itself is [the meaning of] 'pleasure' — not [that pleasure belongs] to <s>Viṣṇu</s> [in the genitive sense]. [This is] because of the fault of the sixth-case meaning [i.e. genitive]; [instead,] the capacity of the word <s>Viṣṇu</s> to denote a particular type of pleasure must be postulated in the <s>Veda</s> itself.
Nor [can it be argued that] this follows from the force of the connection of the root <s>yaj</s> with the purpose of deity-worship — because of mutual dependence.
[Objection:] But if so, since the six [sacrifices] like the <s>Āgneya</s> etc. are momentary and [their] fitness is not ascertained, and [their] being a cause of the supreme <s>apūrva</s> is not ascertained — how then is the postulation of <s>apūrva</s> [justified]? [Reply:] No — because when the expressibility of <s>apūrva</s> is established in optional rites (<s>kāmya</s>), the fitness of instrumentality through that [<s>apūrva</s>] is possible in the <s>Āgneya</s> etc. — but not [the other way] first.

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 331)
children.translated_text: [page 331]

children.text:
nanu yo brāhmaṇāyāvagurettaṃ śatena yātayedityatra brāhmaṇabadhodyamasya śatayātanāhetutvāvagame yathā duritāpūrvaṃ kalpyate tathehāpīti cet na avaguret yātayet ityatra hetu-hetumatorliṅityanuśāsanāt liṅgā avagoraṇa śatayātanayoṃrniyataṃ paurvāparyaṃ bodhyate pratyakṣeṇānubhava-smaraṇayoriva tacca sādhanatve sādhanasādhanatve vā ubhayamapi madhyavartighaṭitamiti dūritakalpanaṃ saṃskāravat iha tu vidhyanuśiṣṭā liṅg kāryatāmāha /
kiñca kāmī kāmyādanyat kāmyāvyavahitasādhanatayā jñātameva kartavyatayāvaitīti niyamāt na kriyāyāṃ kāminonvayo yogyaḥ /
na ca tṛptikāmasya pāke pravṛttervyabhicāraḥ odanakāmasya tatra pravṛtteḥ tṛptikāmanā tu tatkāmanopayogino na tu sākṣāt anyathā sādhanasādhane pravṛttirna syāt /
kāmyasādhanatvaṃ pravartakaṃ
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] In [the injunction] 'whoever insults a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, him one should punish with a hundred [lashes],' when the effort of killing a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is understood as a cause of punishment by a hundred [lashes], just as a demerit-<s>apūrva</s> (<s>duritāpūrva</s>) is postulated [there], so too here [in the case of sacrifice, an <s>apūrva</s> should be postulated]. [Reply:] No — because in 'he would insult' and 'he should punish,' the <s>Pāṇinian</s> rule that the optative suffix (<s>liṅ</s>) [applies] to cause and effect conveys a determinate sequence between the insulting and the punishing; [this sequence is understood] through perception, just as with experience and recollection. And that [sequence], whether in [the mode of] instrumentality or instrumentality-of-an-instrument, is constituted by both [terms] with an intermediary — thus the postulation of demerit is like [the postulation of] a disposition (<s>saṃskāra</s>). But here [in the case of sacrifice], the optative suffix conveys obligation as enjoined by the injunction (<s>vidhi</s>).
Furthermore, [there is] the rule that one who desires [something] should perform only what is known as an immediate means to the desired, and not [anything] other than the desired means — therefore the connection of the desirer with the action is not fit.
Nor is there deviation [from this rule] in the case of one who desires satisfaction engaging in cooking — because one who desires cooked rice (<s>odana</s>) engages in that [cooking]; one who desires satisfaction [engages] through [cooking's] usefulness to that desire, not directly. Otherwise, engagement in the means-of-a-means would be impossible.
Being-a-means-to-the-desired (<s>kāmyasādhanatva</s>) is the motivating factor.

children.text:
lāghavāditi cet na bhojanakāmasya siddhaudanasya pāke pravṛttiprasaṅgāt tasyaudanadvārā bhojanasādhanatvāviśeṣāt viśeṣaṇe tu yatrāvyavahitasādhanaṃ pākaḥ tat na kāmyaṃ yacca kāmyaṃ tatra nāvyavahitasādhanaṃ pākaiti na pravṛttiḥ /
nanu pākasya siddhaudanadvārā bhojanasādhanatvaṃ na sambhavati dvārasyāsādhyatvāt odanāntaradvārā ca tathā pratisandhāne avyavahitaviśeṣaṇe 'pi kuto na pāke pravartate odanāntare dvāre sākṣātsādhanatvāditi cet na pākasya bhojanasādhanatve viśeṣasyāprayojakatayā odanamātrasya dvāratvāt tasya ca sādhyatvāvivādāt /
odanaviśeṣe ca siddhe odanakāmanāvirahāt na tulyatvam /
nanvodane siddhatvāt yathā na kāmanā tata eva dvāratāpi na athaudanāntarasyāsiddhatvamādāya dvāratā tarhi kāmanāpi syāt tasyāsiddhatvamādāya dvāratā tarhi kāmanāpi syāt tasyāsiddhatvāditi cet na pākasyaikaviśeṣadvāratā bādho na
viśeṣāntaradvāratāvirodhī sakalaviśeṣasyaikatra dvāratvāsambhavāt ekaviśeṣasiddhau tu tanmātrakāmanā vicchidyate na hi sakalaviśeṣasiddhatvena sāmānyakāmanāvicchedaḥ sakalaviśeṣasiddherasambhavena tadanucchedaprasaṅgāt /
atha vā kāmyādanyat sākṣādasādhanatvena jñāyamānaṃ yatkartavyatayā kāmo budhyate tatkāmyāvyavahitasādhanamantarā kṛtvaiva /
yadvā kāmyādanyat kāmo prathamaṃ kāmyāvyavahitasādhanaṃ kartavyatayāvaiti paścāt tadvārā avyavahitasādhanamiti prathamaṃ yāge kāmikāryatābodho 'yogyatāparāhata eva /
children.translated_text: If one says 'by parsimony' — no, because there would be the undesired consequence that one who desires eating would engage in cooking when rice is already available, since cooking does not differ in being a means to eating through the medium of rice. But with the qualifier [that the means must be proximate]: Where cooking is the proximate means, that is not the object of desire; and where the object of desire is, cooking is not the proximate means — hence no engagement. Objection: Cooking's being a means to eating through the medium of already-available rice is not possible, because the medium is not something to be produced; and if we posit its being a means through the medium of different rice, then even with the proximate-means qualifier, why does one not engage in cooking, since it is a direct means when different rice is the medium? No, because in cooking's being a means to eating, since the particular specification is irrelevant, rice in general is the medium, and its being something to be produced is not disputed. And when a particular rice is already available, there is no desire for rice [in general], so there is no parity. Objection: Just as there is no desire for rice since it is already available, for that very reason there is no mediation either; or if mediation is taken by reference to the non-availability of different rice, then there should also be desire, since that is non-available — no, because cooking's mediation through one particular [rice] is blocked but its mediation through another particular [rice] is not incompatible, since all particulars cannot be mediated through a single [instance]; and upon the availability of one particular, the desire for that alone ceases — for the cessation of a general desire does not [require] the availability of all particulars, since the availability of all particulars being impossible, there would be the consequence of its never ceasing. Alternatively, what is other than the desired end, being cognized as not being a direct means, is understood as obligatory through desire [only] after performing something that is a proximate means to the desired end. Or, what is other than the desired end — desire first understands a proximate means to the desired end as obligatory, then [understands] a means through that medium as a proximate means — thus the initial cognition of enjoined obligatoriness in the sacrifice is itself defeated by unsuitability.

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 339)
children.translated_text: (Bibliotheca Indica 98, IV,2, p. 339)

children.text:
uttānāstu vivādaviṣayoliṅg samabhivyāhṛtakriyānvitakāryatābodhikā pramāṇaliṅgatvāt laukikaliṅgavat liṅgapasthāpyaṃ kāryatvaṃ samabhivyāhṛtakriyānvitaṃ liṅupasthāpyakāryatvatvāt pacetetikāryatvavat yāgo vā kāryatvānvitaḥ kriyākāryatvāvagamenāpūrvaṃ kalpyamiti tatra prathame yāgānvitakāryatvabodhikatvaṃ liṅgo bodhyate na tu kriyate /
na ca yogyatājñānaṃ vinā tatsambhavatītyuktameva /
na hi yogyatādikaṃ vinaiva tadanumānaprāmāṇyaprayojanamātrādanvitamabhidhīyate śabdena nāntyau kuryādityatra vyabhicārāt vedāsyānuvādakatāpātācca /
children.translated_text: The plain [view] is: The inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) in the matter under dispute is a means of valid cognition that produces awareness of obligatoriness connected with the action co-occurring [in the sentence], because it has the nature of a valid inferential mark, like a mundane inferential mark. What is presented by the <s>liṅga</s> is obligatoriness connected with the co-occurring action, because it has the nature of obligatoriness presented by the <s>liṅga</s>, like the obligatoriness [conveyed by] '<s>pacet</s>' (one should cook). Or: The sacrifice is connected with obligatoriness; through the understanding of the obligatoriness of the action, <s>apūrva</s> (unseen merit) is postulated. In the first [alternative], what is conveyed of the <s>liṅga</s> is its capacity to produce awareness of obligatoriness connected with the sacrifice, not that it produces [the sacrifice]. And it has already been said that this is not possible without cognition of suitability. For without suitability and the like, something is not denoted by a word merely because of the purpose of the validity of that inference with which it is connected — due to deviation in '<s>nāntyau kuryāt</s>' (one should not kill fish), and because it would lead to the <s>Veda</s>'s being merely reiterative.

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 342)
children.translated_text: (Bibliotheca Indica 98, IV,2, p. 342)

children.text:
nanvapūrve vyutpattivirahaḥ tathā hi prasiddhārthasvargakāmapadasamabhivyāhārānyathānupapattyā upasthite śaktirgrahītavyā /
na ca śābdānubhavāt pūrvaṃ apūrvamupasthitaṃ mānābhāvāt apūrvatvavyāghātāt avācyatvāpātācca /
na ca liṅgādinā tadupasthitiḥ vyutpattyanantaraṃ tatpravṛttāvanyonyāśrayāt /
na ca kāryatvenopalakṣite tatra śaktigrahaḥ upalakṣaṇaṃ hi smaraṇamanumānaṃ vā agṛhīte sambandhāgrahādaśakyamiti /
maivaṃ /
kārye dharmiṇi kāryatvena śaktigrahāt kāryatvaviśiṣṭañcopasthitameva tato 'nvitābhidhānadaśāyāṃ yāgaviṣayakaṃ kāryamityanubhavaḥ svargakāmānvayāyogyatayā ghaṭādikaṃ tiraskṛtya kriyāṃbhinne yogyatāvaśādyāgaviṣayakāpūrve paryavasyati na tvapūrvatvena śaktigrahaḥ /
na cāpūrvaṃ kāryamityanubhavaḥ bhavati ca sāmānyataḥ sambandhabuddhiḥ sahakārivaśāt viśeṣabuddhyāpayaḥ yathā tavaiva kartṛviśeṣasiddhiḥ /
nanu kāryatvenāpi kiṃ ghaṭādau śaktigrahaḥ utāpūrve ubhayatra vā nādyaḥ anyapratipattāvanyaśaktigrahānupayogāt /
nāntyau prāganupasthiteriti cet na yena hi rūpeṇa śabdenānubhavo janyate tena rūpeṇa śaktigrahaḥ padārthasmaraṇañca śābdānubhavahetuḥ na hi prameyatvena śaktigrahaḥ padārthasmaraṇañca ghaṭatvena śābdānubhavahetuḥ / evañca ghaṭādāveva kārye śaktā liṅgiti śaktigrahastataḥ kāryamiti smaraṇaṃ tato yogyatādivaśāt pracuradravya-guṇa-karmāṇi kāryāṇi vihāya yāgaviṣayakaṃ kāryamityunubhavo bhavannapūrvamālambate yogyatvācca tasya sthāyitvalābhaḥ /
ata eva vākyārthānubhavamātraviṣayatvāttadapūrvam /
na ca smṛtānāmākāṅkādivaśādanvayabodhaḥ padena kriyate na cāpūrvaṃ smṛtigocara iti vācyam /
śaktigraha-padārthasmṛtiśābdānubhavānāṃ samānaprakārakatāmātreṇa hetu-hetumadbhāvāvadhāraṇāt lāghavādāvaśyakatvācca na tu kvacit sahacāramātreṇa anvayapratiyogina evopasthitistathā gauravāt gopadādapūrvagavānanubhavaprasaṅgācca /
viśiṣṭa-vaiśiṣṭyabodhe sarvatra tathaiva anyathā parvatīyavahnirvyāpakatayā nāvagata iti kathaṃ tadanvayo 'numitau /
nanu sāmānyalakṣaṇā pratyāsattyā sarvā eva vyaktayo vyāptigrahe śaktigrahe ca viṣayībhavanti kathamanyathā parvatīyadhūmavyāptyagrahe tasmādanumitiriti cet na yena rūpeṇa vyāptigrahastena rūpeṇa vyāpyatvena vā pakṣadharmatāgraho 'numitau kāraṇamastu kiṃ tathā /
api ca sā yadyasti mamāpi nāsti cetāvāpi /
kiñca tava darśane sāstīti sutarāmapūrvavācyatā kāryatvena hi rūpeṇāpūrvasyāpi śaktigrahaviṣayatvaṃ padārthasmṛtiviṣayatvañca /
na caivamapūrvatvakṣatiḥ yāgaviṣayatvāderviśeṣasya kārye liṅgaṃ vinānupasthiteḥ yathā parvatīyatvabhānaṃ vahnau nānumitiṃ vinā /
nanu kārye yadi kriyāsādhāraṇena liṅgaśaktiḥ kriyā cāyogyeti yogyapūrvalābhaḥ tadā nityaniṣedhāpūrvayoralābhaḥ na hi tatrāyogyatayā kriyā tyaktuṃ śakyate phalāśravaṇāt kalpanāyāñca bījābhāvāt /
na ca ekatra nirṇītaḥ śāstrartho 'nyatra tathaiveti nyāyāt tatrāpyapūrvameva liṅgartha iti tyaktuṃ na hyapūrvatvena śaktigrahaḥ kintu kāryatvaviśiṣṭe dharmiṇi kriyā ca tathā bhavatyeva /
na ca kāryeṇa samaṃ kriyāyā anvayānupapattyā apūrve paryavasānaṃ
children.translated_text: Objection: There is absence of linguistic convention (<s>vyutpatti</s>) with respect to <s>apūrva</s> (unseen merit). To explain: The linguistic capacity must be grasped through the inexplicability-otherwise of the co-occurrence with the word '<s>svargakāma</s>' (desirer of heaven) whose meaning is well-known. But <s>apūrva</s> is not presented prior to verbal experience, due to the absence of a means of knowledge, because it would contradict its being unprecedented, and because it would lead to its being inexpressible. Nor is it presented through an inferential mark and the like, because of mutual dependence — its presentation depending on the convention, and the convention operating after its presentation. Nor is the linguistic capacity grasped with respect to what is indicated by obligatoriness as an indicator — for an indicator is either recollection or inference, and without the relation having been grasped, it is impossible due to the non-grasping of the relation. Let it not be so. Because the linguistic capacity is grasped with respect to the property-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>) that is the effect, under the aspect of being an effect, what is presented is qualified by effect-ness itself; then at the stage of connected denotation, the experience is 'an effect pertaining to the sacrifice.' Setting aside pots and the like due to unsuitability with respect to connection with the desirer of heaven, by the force of suitability it terminates in <s>apūrva</s> pertaining to the sacrifice, which is distinct from [ordinary] action — but the linguistic capacity is not grasped under the aspect of being <s>apūrva</s>. And the experience is not '<s>apūrva</s> is the effect' — rather there is a general relational cognition, which through cooperating conditions terminates in a specific cognition, just as on your own view, the specific agent is established. Objection: Under the aspect of effect-ness, is the linguistic capacity grasped with respect to pots and the like, or with respect to <s>apūrva</s>, or with respect to both? Not the first, because grasping the capacity with respect to one thing is useless for cognizing another. Nor the last, since it was not presented before — no, because the linguistic capacity is grasped under the very aspect in which the word produces experience, and recollection of word-meaning, which is a cause of verbal experience, [operates] under that same aspect. For the linguistic capacity is not grasped under the aspect of being knowable, and the recollection of word-meaning is not a cause of verbal experience under the aspect of pot-ness. Thus, the capacity of the <s>liṅga</s> is grasped with respect to pots and the like as effects; from that, the recollection 'effect'; from that, by the force of suitability and the like, setting aside effects that are abundant substances, qualities, and actions, the experience 'an effect pertaining to the sacrifice' arises and takes <s>apūrva</s> as its object, and through its suitability, that obtains permanence. For this very reason, since it is the object only of the experience of sentence-meaning, it is unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>). Nor should one say that the connection-cognition of recollected [meanings] through expectancy and the like is produced by the word, and <s>apūrva</s> is not within the scope of recollection — because it is determined that the causal relation among capacity-grasping, word-meaning-recollection, and verbal experience holds merely through having the same mode, by parsimony and necessity; it is not the case that merely through co-occurrence somewhere, only the co-present entity is presented as the correlate of connection — that being more complex, and because there would be the consequence of not experiencing an unprecedented cow from the word 'cow.' In the cognition of the qualified and the qualification, [the same principle applies] everywhere; otherwise, how could the connection of fire on the mountain be inferred, since it is not known as pervading? Objection: Through the general-characteristic-based (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇā</s>) extraordinary perception, all individuals become objects in the grasping of universal concomitance and in the grasping of linguistic capacity — otherwise how could there be inference from the non-grasping of the concomitance of smoke on the mountain? — no, because let the grasping of the subject-property under the aspect of being the pervaded, or under the very aspect in which the concomitance is grasped, be the cause in inference — what of it? Moreover, if that [extraordinary perception] exists [for you], it exists for me too; if not, not for you either. Furthermore, on your view it exists all the more, and hence the expressibility of <s>apūrva</s> [follows] even more readily — for under the aspect of effect-ness, <s>apūrva</s> too is an object of capacity-grasping and word-meaning-recollection. Nor does this damage the unprecedented nature [of <s>apūrva</s>], because the specific features such as pertaining-to-the-sacrifice are not presented in the effect without the <s>liṅga</s>, just as the feature of being-on-the-mountain does not appear in fire without inference. Objection: If the capacity of the <s>liṅga</s> pertains to the effect through what is common to [all] actions, and action is unsuitable, and [only through that] the unprecedented [<s>apūrva</s>] is obtained — then <s>apūrva</s> connected with obligatory [rites] and prohibitions would not be obtained, for there, action cannot be set aside as unsuitable, since no result is heard [for them], and there is no seed for postulation. Nor can one say that the meaning of scripture determined in one place applies equally elsewhere — for even there, <s>apūrva</s> alone is the meaning of the <s>liṅga</s>, and it cannot be set aside. For the linguistic capacity is not grasped under the aspect of being <s>apūrva</s>; rather, action is indeed such [i.e., an effect] in the property-possessor qualified by effect-ness. Nor does <s>apūrva</s> result from the impossibility of action's connection together with the effect —

children.text:
abhedasyāpyanvayāditi / maivaṃ /
na hi loke pacetetyādau kārye dharmiṇi śaktiḥ kalpitā kintvananyalabhye kṛtirūpe kāryatvamātre dharmiṇaḥ pākāderdhātorevopasthitisambhavāt kriyākāryatvasyānvitābhidhānalabhyatvātathāca dharmiṇi vede śaktiḥ kalpanīyā sā ca kriyānirāsenaiva /
na hi kriyāyāḥ kāryatvānvayayogyatve dharmiṇi śaktiḥ kalpayituṃ śakyate tasmādayogyatayā kriyānirāsānantaraṃ tadatirikta eva śaktiḥ kalpanīyā / na ca kriyātiriktakāryāt kāryamātraṃ laghuḥ tataḥ kriyāpi śakyaiveti vācyam /
yato na brūmaḥ kriyātiriktakāryatvena śaktiḥ kintvayogyatayā kriyāyāṃ nirastāyāṃ dharmiṇi śaktikalpanasamaye yat kriyātiriktaṃ tatra śaktiḥ na tu śaktigrahe kriyāpraveśaḥ na hi yatprayuktānupapattyā yatkalpanaṃ tadeva tasya viṣayaḥ evañca kāryatvenāpi tadatiriktakārye eva śaktikalpanānnitya niṣedhayorapi tadevopāsanādyanvayayogyaṃ liṅgābhidhīyate na tu kāryatvamātraṃ dharmiṇi bādhakābhāvāt lakṣaṇāprasaṅgācca /
ghaṭādistu liṅgaśaktigrahe na tiraskriyate na puraskriyate uyayathāpi gauravāt / anvitābhidhānadaśāyānvayogyatayā tasyāpraveśaḥ vidhipratyayasya ca tatrāprayogaḥ kevalasya tasyāsādhutvāt /
dhātusamabhivyāhārasthale ca tadarthenānvayabodhajanananiyamena ghaṭādyapratipādakatvāt /
ata evāprayogādevāprayogo 'pūrvatvaṃ vā prayogopādhiriti vadanti / athāpratipādyadhaṭādivṛttitayā na kāryatvaṃ pravṛttinimittaṃ pratipādyaghaṭādivṛttitayā na kāryatvaṃ pravṛttinimittaṃ pratipādyamātravṛttereva tathātvāt anyathā prameyatvameva tathāstviti cet na yatprakārikā hi pratipattiḥ padajanyā tadeva tatra pravṛttinimittaṃ phalakalpyatvāt śakteḥ na tu pratipādyamātravṛtti sāsnādau vyabhicārāt /
na ca prameyatvaṃ tathā tadbodhasyāpravartakatvāt /
ata eva lāke liṅg lākṣaṇiko kriyābhinne dharmiṇi vede śaktikalpanāt /
na ca laukikānāmapūrve tātparyaṃ sambhavati pūrvaṃ pramāṇāntareṇāpratīte kriyāsādhāraṇaśaktāvapi loke lakṣaṇaiva pacetetyatra hi pākakāryatāvagamyate tatra kāryatve liṅgastātparyaṃ lāghavāt /
na dharmiṇi kriyāyā dhātulabhyatvāt /
tadāhuḥ tātparyāddhi vṛttirna tu vṛttestātparyamiti tṛtīyāyāḥ karaṇatvaikatvāt kāryaṃ kāryatvañca na svatantraṃ śakyaṃ kintu viśiṣṭaṃ viśiṣṭācca viśeṣaṇamanyadeveti kāryatve lakṣaṇā /
na ca kāryatvaviśiṣṭadharmyupasthitāvapi dharmyaṃśamapahāya kriyāyāṃ kāryatvānvayo 'stu kiṃ lakṣaṇayeti vācyam /
na hītaradharmigatatvenopasthitasya dharmyantarākāṅkāsti ataḥ svatantrakāryatvopasthitaye dharmyantarākāṅkṣāsti ataḥ svatantrakāryatvopasthitaye lakṣaṇā yathā puroḍāśakapālena tuṣānupapacatītyatra puroḍāśarthitayā tadanvitatvenopasthitasya kapālasya nopavāpākāṅkṣeti svatantrakapālopasthitaye 'dhiṣṭhānalakṣaṇā /
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] 'Because even non-difference has connection (<s>anvaya</s>).' Do not [say] so.
For in ordinary usage, in [expressions like] 'he should cook' (<s>paceta</s>) and the like, the denotative power (<s>śakti</s>) is not postulated in the effect as the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>), but rather in being-an-effect (<s>kāryatva</s>) alone, which has the form of effort (<s>kṛti</s>) and is obtainable by no other means — since the property-bearer, cooking and the like, can be presented by the verbal root itself, and because the being-an-effect of the action is obtainable through <s>anvitābhidhāna</s> (connected denotation). Thus, the denotative power must be postulated in the property-bearer in the <s>Veda</s>, and that [is achieved] only by excluding the action.
For when the action is fit for connection with being-an-effect, the denotative power cannot be postulated in the [separate] property-bearer; therefore, after excluding the action due to unfitness, the denotative power must be postulated in something other than the action. Nor should it be said that mere being-an-effect is simpler than the being-an-effect-other-than-action, and therefore the action too falls within the scope of the denotative power.
Because we do not say that the denotative power is in being-an-effect-other-than-action; rather, when the action has been excluded due to unfitness, at the time of postulating the denotative power in the property-bearer, it is in whatever is other than the action that the denotative power [resides] — but the action does not enter the scope of the denotative power. For it is not the case that whatever is postulated due to the impossibility [of an explanation] occasioned by something, that very thing is its object. Thus, even through being-an-effect, the postulation of denotative power is in the effect other than [the action] alone; and in the case of obligatory and prohibitory [injunctions] too, what is denoted by the injunctive suffix (<s>liṅ</s>) is that which is fit for connection with worship (<s>upāsanā</s>) and the like — not mere being-an-effect, since there is no invalidating cognition regarding the property-bearer, and [otherwise] there would be an unwanted recourse to figurative usage (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>).
As for [entities like] a pot and the like, they are neither excluded nor included in the grasping of the denotative power of <s>liṅ</s>, [they are] irrelevant (<s>ubhayathā</s>) due to cumbersomeness. At the stage of connected denotation (<s>anvitābhidhāna</s>), they do not enter due to unfitness for connection; and the injunctive suffix is not used with respect to them, since it would be ungrammatical (<s>asādhu</s>) in isolation.
And in the context of co-occurrence with a verbal root, since [the suffix] invariably generates the cognition of connection with the root-meaning, it does not convey a pot and the like.
For this very reason, they say: either the non-usage itself [of the suffix with pots] is the reason for non-usage, or <s>apūrvatva</s> (unprecedented-ness) is a condition for usage. Now, if [it is objected that] being-an-effect is not the basis of application (<s>pravṛttinimitta</s>) insofar as it resides in non-denotable [entities like] pots and the like, and that it is not the basis of application insofar as it resides in denotable [entities like] pots and the like — since it [would be the basis of application] only insofar as it resides in what is denotable as such, [and] otherwise <s>prameyatva</s> (knowability) itself would serve [equally well] — [we reply:] no, for whatever qualifier characterizes the cognition generated by the word, that alone is the basis of application there, since the denotative power is postulated from the result (<s>phala</s>); not [something] that merely resides in the denotable, since there is deviation in [cases like] the dewlap and the like.
Nor is <s>prameyatva</s> (knowability) [the basis of application], since the cognition of it does not impel [action].
For this very reason, [they say] that in ordinary usage <s>liṅ</s> is figurative (<s>lākṣaṇika</s>), since the denotative power is postulated in the <s>Veda</s> with respect to the property-bearer, which is different from the action.
Nor can ordinary speakers have <s>apūrva</s> as the intended meaning, since [<s>apūrva</s>] has not been previously cognized through another means of valid knowledge. Even if [<s>liṅ</s>] has a denotative power exclusive to the action in ordinary usage, [what operates there] is only figurative usage. For in 'he should cook' (<s>paceta</s>), the being-an-effect of cooking is understood; therein, the intended meaning of <s>liṅ</s> is in being-an-effect, due to simplicity,
not in the property-bearer [separately], since the action is obtainable from the verbal root.
They say: 'it is from the intended meaning (<s>tātparya</s>) that the semantic function [proceeds], not from the semantic function that the intended meaning [proceeds]'; and since the third case-ending (<s>tṛtīyā</s>) has only instrumentality (<s>karaṇatva</s>) [as its meaning], the effect and being-an-effect are not independently denotable, but rather the qualified [whole is denotable], and from the qualified, the qualifier is something else — hence there is figurative usage with respect to being-an-effect.
Nor should it be said: 'even when the property-bearer qualified by being-an-effect is presented, setting aside the property-bearer aspect, let being-an-effect connect with the action; what need is there for figurative usage?'
For when something is presented as residing in a certain property-bearer, there is no expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>) for another property-bearer. Therefore, figurative usage is [needed] for the presentation of independent being-an-effect [connected with] another property-bearer — just as in 'he cooks the husks on the <s>puroḍāśa</s> potsherds' (<s>puroḍāśakapālena tuṣānupapacati</s>), the potsherd, being presented as connected with the <s>puroḍāśa</s>, does not have expectancy for [the action of] placing [rice grains], and therefore figurative usage based on substratum (<s>adhiṣṭhānalakṣaṇā</s>) is [needed] for the presentation of the potsherd independently.

children.text:
na ca vyutpattivirodhaḥ na hi loke kriyākāryatve śaktiravadhāritā yena virodho bhavet kintu kāryatvamātre kriyāyā dhātulabhyatvāt /
na ca dharmyantare śaktāvapi tadbhaṅgaḥ tasmāt prakṛtyarthānvitasvārthabodhakatvaṃ pratyayānāṃ gṛhītaṃ pratyayārthaścāpūrvamapīti na virodhaḥ /
astu vā loke liṅgaḥ kriyākāryatve śaktiḥ tathāpi tadbhaṅgaṃ vinaiva nānārthanyāyena vede dharmyantare śaktistāṃ vinā svargakāmānvayāsambhavāt /
children.translated_text:
Nor is there a contradiction with conventional usage (<s>vyutpatti</s>). For in ordinary usage, the denotative power is not ascertained to reside in the being-an-effect of the action [specifically], such that there would be a contradiction; rather, [it is ascertained] in mere being-an-effect, since the action is obtainable from the verbal root.
Nor is there a breaking [of the denotative power] even when the power resides in another property-bearer. Therefore, what is grasped for suffixes is the capacity to generate cognition of their own meaning connected with the root-meaning, and the meaning of the suffix can be <s>apūrva</s> too — hence no contradiction.
Alternatively, even if in ordinary usage <s>liṅ</s> has the denotative power in the being-an-effect of the action, even so, without breaking that [power], by the principle of multiple meanings (<s>nānārthanyāya</s>), there is a denotative power in another property-bearer in the <s>Veda</s>, since without it the connection with 'one who desires heaven' (<s>svargakāma</s>) would be impossible.

children.text:
anye tu pacetetyādau dhātunaiva pākaḥ kāryo 'bhidhīyate liṅg tatra tātparyagrāhikā na tu śaktā niyamatastādṛśyeva tatprayogāt sāmānyaśabdasya viśeṣaparatvañca na vṛttyantaranirvāhyaṃ ata eva vartamānatvādau na laṅgādiśaktiriti loke śakyagrahāt na vyutpattivirodha iti tadasat liṅaḥ kāryatve 'śaktau pacipadāt kāryatvajñānānupapatteḥ yugapadvṛttidvayavirodhāt /
na cājahatsvārthā ubhayasādhāraṇasyānupasthiteriti dik /
children.translated_text:
Others, however, [hold that] in 'he should cook' (<s>paceta</s>) and the like, it is by the verbal root itself that cooking as an effect is denoted; <s>liṅ</s> there functions as the determiner of the intended meaning (<s>tātparyagrāhikā</s>), not as having its own denotative power — [and this is] invariably so, since [<s>liṅ</s>] is used only in such [contexts]; and the reference of a general term to a particular [meaning] is not to be accounted for by a different semantic function. For this very reason, [they hold that <s>liṅ</s>] does not have denotative power in the present tense and the like — thus, from the grasping of what is denotable in ordinary usage, there is no contradiction with conventional usage. That is wrong, because if <s>liṅ</s> does not have denotative power in being-an-effect, the knowledge of being-an-effect from the word <s>paci</s> (cook) would be untenable, due to the impossibility of two co-occurring semantic functions.
Nor [can one resort to] <s>ajahatsvārthā</s> [lakṣaṇā] (figurative usage that does not abandon its own meaning), since what is common to both [meanings] cannot be presented — thus [is] the direction [of the argument].

children.text:
yadvā jñāne padānāṃ śaktiḥ śakyatvāt evañca liṅgapadaṃ ekatroccāraṇe yogyatādivaśāt yāgaviṣayakaṃ stāyisvargajanakaṃ kāryamityekaṃ jñānamanubhavarūpaṃ pracuradravya-guṇa-karmavilakṣaṇaviṣayaṃ kriyate /
na caivaṃ nānārthavadekaikajñāne śaktigrahādekaikaviṣayo 'nubhavo bhavet na samuditaviṣaya iti vācyam /
śaktigrahakāle ekatroccāraṇa iti viśeṣaṇamahimnā tatsambhavāt nānārthe tu pramāṇābhāvena gauravena ca śaktigrahe tasyāpraveśanāt /
tathāpyamīṣāṃ samūhālambanaṃ syānna tu parasparaṃ vaiśiṣṭyajñānamiti cet na sākāṅkṣadharma-dharmigocaraikajñānasyaiva viśiṣṭajñānatvāt cana ca samūhālambanasambhedaḥ /
tasya nirākāṅkṣaviṣayatvāt /
astu vopasthiteṣṭhagṛhītāsaṃsargeṣu sthāyitvasvargajanakatva-kāryatveṣu śaktiḥ agṛhītāsaṃsargakasyāpi viśiṣṭajñānasamānaśīlatvāt ata uktanyāyena tāvadviṣayakamekaṃ jñānaṃ liṅgpadena janyate /
evamevālaukikārtheṣu svargādipadeṣu śaktigrahaḥ /
nanu bhavatūktaprakāreṇa śaktigrahastathāpi liṅpadāt yāgaviṣayakakāryānubhave satyapūrvalābhāt svargakāmānvayaḥ sambhavatītyupapādakapratisandhāne prasiddhārthasvargakāmapadasamabhivyāhārānyathānupapattyā liṅgaḥ kārye śaktikalpanaṃ /
na hi prathamamupapādakapratisandhānaṃ vinārthāpattiḥ sambhavati /
na ca śaktikalpanāt pūrvaṃ upapādakaśarīraniviṣṭamapūrvaṃ jñātamiti cet tat kiṃ ya eva viśeṣa upapādakaḥ pakṣadharmatābalāt siddhyati tatpratisandhānamarthāpattau kāraṇaṃ tathātve pūrvaṃ gṛhītamātrasya kalpyate
children.translated_text:
Alternatively, the denotative power of words resides in cognition, because [words] are capable of producing cognition. Thus, the <s>liṅ</s> suffix, in a single utterance, by the force of fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>) and the like, produces one cognition in the form of experience, having as its object an effect that is directed toward sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>), that generates lasting heaven (<s>sthāyisvarga</s>), [a cognition] whose content is distinguished by abundant substance, quality, and action.
Nor should it be said that, as with words having multiple meanings (<s>nānārtha</s>), since the denotative power is grasped with respect to each individual cognition, the experience would have only individual objects, not a combined object —
because at the time of grasping the denotative power, due to the force of the qualifier 'in a single utterance,' that [combined cognition] is possible; whereas in [cases of] multiple meanings, [the combined cognition] does not enter the scope of the denotative power grasping due to the absence of a means of valid knowledge and due to cumbersomeness.
If [it is objected that] there would be a collective apprehension (<s>samūhālambana</s>) of these, but not a cognition of mutual qualification (<s>vaiśiṣṭyajñāna</s>) — no, because a single cognition whose content is a property and a property-bearer with mutual expectancy (<s>sākāṅkṣa</s>) is itself a qualified cognition (<s>viśiṣṭajñāna</s>), and there is no confusion with collective apprehension,
since [collective apprehension] has content without expectancy (<s>nirākāṅkṣa</s>).
Alternatively, let the denotative power reside in the [properties of] permanence (<s>sthāyitva</s>), heaven-producing-ness (<s>svargajanakatva</s>), and being-an-effect (<s>kāryatva</s>), which are presented but whose mutual connection has not been grasped — since even [a cognition] whose connection [of parts] has not been grasped has the same character as a qualified cognition. Thus, by the principle stated above, one cognition with that many objects is produced by the <s>liṅ</s> suffix.
In just this way, the grasping of denotative power occurs for non-worldly terms like 'heaven' (<s>svarga</s>) and the like.
[Objection:] Granted that the denotative power is grasped in the manner stated; nevertheless, when the cognition of being-an-effect directed toward sacrifice is produced from the <s>liṅ</s> suffix, the connection with 'one who desires heaven' (<s>svargakāma</s>) is possible through the obtaining of <s>apūrva</s>; thus, through the reflective reasoning (<s>upapādakapratisandhāna</s>) that [proceeds from] the impossibility of explaining otherwise the co-occurrence of the [<s>liṅ</s> suffix] with the well-known-meaning words 'one who desires heaven,' the denotative power of <s>liṅ</s> is postulated in being-an-effect.
For without the reflective reasoning of the justification, presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>) is not possible first.
If [it is said that] <s>apūrva</s>, which is contained in the body of the justification, is known before the postulation of the denotative power — [we ask:] is it that the very particular [entity] that is the justification is established by the force of <s>pakṣadharmatā</s> (being a property of the subject), [and] the reflective consideration of that is the cause in presumption? In that case, what has merely been previously grasped is [all that is] postulated.

children.text:
kalpanocchedāpattiḥ /
tasmāt yathā sāmānyatobhojanasya pīnatvasambandhāvagamāt upapādakatarke sati kalpanāto viśeṣāvagamaḥ yathā vā sāmānyaśaktavyaktivācakapadena samabhivyāhāravaśādviśeṣābhidhānamevamatrāpi kāryamātravācakatve kāryaviśeṣalābhaḥ sambhavatīti tarkitopapādakapratisandhānād bhavatyarthāpattyā śaktikalpanaṃ yāgaviṣayakañca kāryaṃ na ghaṭādi tasya saviṣayakatvābhāvāt viṣayatvañca jñānaghaṭayoriva svabhāvasambandho vā tannirūpaṇādhīnanirūpaṇatvaṃ vā tatsānasaṃvitasaṃvedyatvaṃ vā vyāvṛttasādhanatvaṃ veti /
asti hi yāga-dāna-homajanyāpūrvāṇāṃ tulyarūpasādhanāntaravyavacchedena pratyekamātrajanyatvam /
taduktaṃ viśabdo hi viśeṣārthaḥ sinotirbandha ucyate /
viśeṣeṇa sinotīti viṣayo 'to niyāmakaḥ iti /
nanu yena rūpeṇa śaktigrahaḥ tena rūpeṇa kāryatvaśaktāliṅg padāllakṣaṇayā kāryopasthitau yogyatādivaśādapūrvalābho 'stu kāryasmaraṇaṃ hi anvitābhidhānopayogi na tvapūrvasmaraṇaṃ tacca padena padārthena veti na kaścidviśeṣaḥ kāryañca śakyakāryatvasambandhitayāvagatameveti cet na liṅgo lākṣaṇikatvenāpūrvānanubhāvakatvāt /
na cetarānvitasvārthaśaktasya yajyādipadasyetaradapūrvamādāyānubhāvakatvamiti vācyam /
itaropalakṣitasvārthānvayamātre hi padānāṃ śaktirna tvitaratra gauravāt padāntaralabhyatvācca /
lakṣaṇāyāñca tīropalakṣitānvayaśālisvārthānubhāvakatvīmitarapadasya tīrasya tu saṃskārādupasthitirasannihitenānvitābhidhānābhāvāt /
na cāpūrvaṃ saṃskāraviṣayaḥ /
kiñca yajipadena svargakāmakāryaviṣayo yāga ityunubhavobhavet lakṣaṇāyāmitarapadasya lakṣaṇīyaviśeṣaṇasvārthaviśeṣyakānubhavajanakatvāt /
na caitādṛśo bodha ākāṅkṣitaḥ /
na ca yāgāviśeṣitakāryamātreṇa svargakāmānvayaḥ pratīyate kintu yāgaviṣayakakāryaviśeṣe tathāca tathāvidhabodhārthaṃ liṅgaḥ kārye śaktireveti /
children.translated_text:
[There would be] the undesirable consequence of the destruction of [all] postulation.
Therefore, just as the specific [type of food that causes corpulence] is ascertained through postulation (<s>arthāpatti</s>) — from the general understanding that eating is connected with corpulence, when there is a supporting reasoning (<s>upapādakatarka</s>) — or just as a word denoting a universal-possessing individual conveys a particular [meaning] through the force of co-utterance (<s>samabhivyāhāra</s>) — so here too, even when [the optative suffix] expresses mere obligation (<s>kāryamātra</s>), the acquisition of a specific obligation is possible. Thus, through the recollection of a supporting reasoning that has been arrived at, the postulation of the [optative's] capacity [to denote a specific obligation] occurs through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption). And the obligation pertains to sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>), not to a pot etc., because the latter lacks the property of having a content (<s>saviṣayakatva</s>). And 'being-a-content' (<s>viṣayatva</s>) [means] either an intrinsic relation, like that between a cognition and a pot; or having one's determination depend on the determination of that [other thing]; or being cognizable through cognition accompanied by that [other thing]; or being distinguished instrumentality (<s>vyāvṛttasādhanatva</s>).
For the <s>apūrvas</s> produced by sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>), gift (<s>dāna</s>), and oblation (<s>homa</s>) each have the property of being produced from that [particular rite] alone, to the exclusion of other means of similar form.
As it has been said: 'The [prefix] <s>vi</s> means "particular," <s>sinoti</s> means "binds." [<s>Viṣaya</s>] means "that which binds particularly" — hence it is a determiner.'
[Objection:] Let the capacity [of the suffix] be grasped in the form in which [it is grasped], and through secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) from the word having the capacity to [denote] obligation, let <s>apūrva</s> be obtained through fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>) etc. when obligation is presented. For the recollection of obligation is useful for the theory of connected denotation (<s>anvitābhidhāna</s>), not the recollection of <s>apūrva</s>; and that [recollection] is through the word or the word-meaning — there is no difference. And obligation is already understood as related by the relation of potency-and-its-effect (<s>śakyakāryatvasambandhi</s>). [Reply:] No — because the optative suffix, being employed through secondary signification (<s>lākṣaṇikatva</s>), is not capable of producing [the cognition of] <s>apūrva</s>.
Nor should it be said that the word <s>yaj</s> etc., having the capacity to [denote] its own meaning connected with another [meaning], is capable of producing [the cognition of] another [thing, namely] <s>apūrva</s> —
for words have the capacity [to denote] only the connection of their own meaning as indicated by the other [co-uttered words], not [to denote] the other [meaning] itself — because of prolixity, and because it is obtainable from another word.
And in secondary signification, the other word [like <s>tīra</s> 'bank'] has the capacity to produce the cognition of its own meaning that possesses the connection indicated [by the primary meaning]; but the presentation of the [secondary referent like] the bank (<s>tīra</s>) is through a disposition (<s>saṃskāra</s>), and since it is not [syntactically] present, there is no connected denotation (<s>anvitābhidhāna</s>).
Nor is <s>apūrva</s> an object of [mere] disposition.
Furthermore, through the word <s>yaj</s>, the cognition produced would be: 'sacrifice is an obligation whose content is [the desire of] one who desires heaven' — because in secondary signification, the other word generates a cognition whose qualificand is the primary meaning [of the other word] and whose qualifier is the secondarily signified [meaning].
But such a cognition is not what is desired.
Nor is the connection with 'one who desires heaven' cognized through mere unspecified obligation without reference to sacrifice — rather, [it is cognized] through a specific obligation whose content is sacrifice. And for such cognition, the optative suffix (<s>liṅ</s>) must have a capacity [to signify] obligation itself.

children.text: apūrvavādasiddhāntaḥ
children.translated_text: The established conclusion of the doctrine of <s>apūrva</s> (<s>apūrvavādasiddhānta</s>)

children.text:
atrocyate /
anvayaprayojakarūpavattvaṃ na yogyatā anāptokte payasā siñcatītyatra satyapyanvayaprayojakadravadravyatve bādhakapramāyāmanvayābodhāt /
atha yogyatve 'pi svabādhakapramāyāmanvayābodhāt /
atha yogyatve 'pi svabādhakapramāvirahaḥ kāraṇaṃ tarhi so 'pyavaśyāpekṣaṇīyaiti lāghavāt saiva yogyatā evañca tadeva yogyamayogyañca syāditi cet satyaṃ yathā daśāviśeṣe tadeva sākāṅkṣamanākāṅkṣamāsannañca tathā svabādhakapramā-tadvirahadaśāyāṃ tadevānvayabodhe yogyamayogyañcābhidhīyate svabādhakapramāyāṃ tadvirahe vā yogyāyogyatāvyavahāradarśanāt svabādhakapramāvirahadaśāyāṃ yogyatādisattve 'pi vahninā siñcatītyatrānvayabodhaḥ apramādoṣavatpuruṣaṇītatvāt /
sāmānyabhānasya kiñcidviśeṣabhānaniyatatvāt viśeṣābhāne kathaṃ tadbhāsata iti na vastugatyā paramparāsādhanaṃ viśeṣo bhāsata evaya paramparāsādhanatvantu prakāro na bhāsate tatprakārabhāne hi paramparāghaṭakajñānasya hetutvāt yathā ghaṭena jalamāharetyatra yogyatayā chidretaraghaṭe ghaṭatvena bhāsate na tu chidretaratvena tathā sati lakṣaṇāyāṃ yugapad vṛttidvayavirodhena ghaṭānanvayaprasaṅgāt ubhayasādhāraṇarūpeṇānupasthiteśca nājahatsvārthā /
atha saṃskārāttadusthitiḥ /
na ca subvibhaktīnāṃ prakṛtyarthagatasvārthānvayabodhakatvavyutpattestatra vibhaktyartho nāvyīyeteti vācyam /
prakṛtyartho hi prakṛtipratipādyāḥ lakṣaṇīyānvayānurodhāt /
sa ca saṃskārasahakārāt prakṛte 'pi /
na ca tasyāniyatodbodhakānna niyatā tadupasthitiḥ /
phalabalena tathā kalpanāditi cet na śabdopasthāpi tanaiva śabdasyānvayabodhakatvāt / na caivamākāśapadāśakyasya saṃskāropasthitasya śabdāśrayatvasya kathaṃ śābdānubhavaviṣayatvamiti vācyam /
niyamato yaddharmavattvenopasthite yatra śaktigrahaḥ tatsmaraṇajanakasaṃskārasya taddharmaviṣayatāniyamena tadudbodhakādeva tadaṃśe 'pi udbodhaniyamenākāśapadādaśakyasyāpi tasya bhānāt /
astu vā tadapi śakyaṃ yadi niyamata upasthitiḥ sahaprayogasya vācyādiparatvenāpyupapatteḥ /
vastutastu niyatopasthitireva nāsti / astu vā padādapi nirvikalpakaṃ tarhyanvayabodhadaśāyāmitarānvayānupapattyabhāvādagrre 'pi kalpanā na syāditi cet tarhi tavāpi kāryatābodhānantaraṃ aupādānikamādhanatābodho na syāt aupādānikamādhanatābodho na syāt aupādānikabodhe 'nupapattibodhasya hetutvāt klapanāmātrocchedaścaivaṃ syāt pratītānupapattimūlatvāt kalpanāyāḥ / vastutastu bādhakapramāvirahasya yogyatātve saṃśayapasādhāraṇaṃ jñānamātrameva tasyāḥ prayojakaṃ tena yatra bādhakapramāniścayastatraivānvayabodhābhāvo 'nyatra tu taddhīmātrācchabdabodha iti yāge 'pi yogyatāsaṃśayenānvayabodhāpratibandhaḥ bādhasaṃśayasyāpratibandhakatvāt anyathā anumānādyucchedaprasaṅgāt /
apūrvavācyatve 'pyapūrve svargasādhanatāsaṃśayādyogyatāyāḥ saṃśaya eva apūrvasya prathamaṃ svargasādhanatvāniścayādupādānasyānvitābhidhānottarakālīnatvāt sādhaka-bādhakapramāṇābhāvena dvārasambhavanayā sādhanatvasambhāvanātaḥ svargakāmānvaya iti tulyam /
api ca yathā na kriyā sthiretyayoṅgyā tathā
children.translated_text:
Here it is stated:
Possessing a form that motivates the connection (<s>anvayaprayojakarūpavattva</s>) is not [the definition of] fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>) — because in [the untrue statement] 'sprinkle with milk' uttered by an unreliable person, even though the liquid-substance-ness that motivates the connection [of milk with sprinkling] is present, there is no cognition of connection when there is a sublating cognition (<s>bādhakapramā</s>).
[Objection:] Even when there is fitness, there is no cognition of connection when there is a sublating cognition of one's own [i.e., when the fitness itself is sublated]. [Reply:] Then, since [the absence of one's own sublating cognition] must necessarily be taken into account, by parsimony, that alone is fitness. [Objection:] And thus, the very same thing would be both fit and unfit. [Reply:] True — just as in [different] states, the very same thing is both expectant (<s>sākāṅkṣa</s>) and non-expectant, proximate and [not proximate] — so, in the state of [the presence of] one's own sublating cognition and [the state of] its absence, the very same thing is called fit and unfit with respect to producing the cognition of connection — because the usage of fitness and unfitness is observed in [the states of] one's own sublating cognition and its absence. In the state of absence of one's own sublating cognition, even when fitness etc. are present, in 'sprinkle with fire' there is no cognition of connection — because [the statement was made by] a person who is non-erroneous and reliable (<s>apramādoṣavatpuruṣa</s>).
Since the appearance of a universal is necessarily accompanied by the appearance of some particular, [the question is:] how does that [universal] appear without the appearance of a particular? [Reply:] In truth, the particular — [namely] indirect instrumentality (<s>paramparāsādhana</s>) — does appear, but indirect instrumentality as a mode (<s>prakāra</s>) does not appear; for the appearance in that mode requires knowledge of the intermediary links. Just as in 'bring water with a pot,' through fitness, pot-ness appears in a pot-without-a-hole, but not as 'without-a-hole' — for if [it appeared] so, then in secondary signification, the contradiction of two simultaneous functions would lead to the non-connection of the pot [with the action]; and because [the meaning] is not presented through a form common to both, [the secondary signification] does not abandon its own meaning (<s>nājahatsvārthā</s>).
[Objection:] The presentation [of the specified pot] is through a disposition (<s>saṃskāra</s>).
Nor should it be said that since the convention (<s>vyutpatti</s>) of <s>sup</s> case-endings is [to denote] the connection of their own meaning with the meaning of the stem, the meaning of the case-ending would not be re-presented there —
because the meaning of the stem is what is conveyed by the stem; [and this meaning] accords with the connection to the secondarily signified [meaning].
And that [stem-meaning] applies in the case at hand also, with the assistance of a disposition.
Nor [is it the case] that because [the disposition] is aroused by non-determinate [factors], the presentation from it is non-determinate.
[Objection:] Such [determinate presentation] is postulated by the force of the result. [Reply:] No — because it is precisely through the presentation evoked by the word that the word has the capacity to produce the cognition of connection. Nor should it be said: 'How can the property of being a substratum of sound — which is not the denotative capacity of the word <s>ākāśa</s> (ether) but is presented through a disposition — be the content of a verbal cognition?' —
because, when [something] is grasped as possessing a certain property through a capacity-comprehension that is necessarily presented in a determinate way, the disposition generating the recollection of that [thing] is necessarily specific to that property — and therefore, through arousal from the very [word] that arouses [the property], that aspect too appears, even though it is not the denotative capacity of the word <s>ākāśa</s>.
Or let that too be the denotative capacity, since the determinate presentation [is accounted for]; because the co-usage (<s>sahaprayoga</s>) is compatible with the view that [the word] primarily denotes [this property] as well.
In truth, however, there is no determinate presentation [through disposition]. Or if there is [indeterminate] presentation even from the word, then [one gets only] an indeterminate cognition (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>); and in that case, at the stage of producing the cognition of connection, since there is no impossibility of connection with the other [meaning], there would be no postulation even later. [Objection:] Then, for you too, after the cognition of obligation, the cognition of instrumentality-through-a-subsidiary (<s>aupādānikasādhanatā</s>) would not arise — because the cognition of impossibility is the cause of the cognition of subsidiary instrumentality; and thus all postulation whatsoever would be destroyed, since postulation is rooted in cognized impossibility. [Reply:] In truth, when the absence of a sublating cognition is [taken as] fitness, mere cognition that is common to [both] doubt and [absence of sublation] is the motivating factor of that [fitness]. Therefore, only where there is the ascertainment of a sublating cognition is there the absence of cognition of connection — but elsewhere, from mere cognition [without ascertainment of sublation], there is verbal cognition. Thus, even in sacrifice, the doubt about fitness does not obstruct the cognition of connection — because doubt about sublation is not an obstructing factor; otherwise, there would be the undesirable consequence of the destruction of inference and other [means of valid knowledge].
Even in the view that [the optative suffix] expresses <s>apūrva</s>, since there is doubt about the fitness of <s>apūrva</s> [being a means] to heaven — [there is] indeed doubt about fitness — because <s>apūrva</s> is initially not ascertained to be a means to heaven, and the subsidiary [cognition] comes only after connected denotation. Through the absence of both establishing and sublating cognitions, and through the possibility of an intermediary — [there is] the plausibility of instrumentality. [Hence] the connection with 'one who desires heaven' is the same [in both views].
Furthermore, just as the action is unfit because it is not durable, so too —

children.text:
kāryamapūrvamapi viśiṣṭaṃ na sthiraṃ kṛtervinaṣṭatvāt /
na cādhiṣeṭhāne apūrvamātre sādhanatvaṃ tasya padāryaikadeśatvenānvayāpratiyogitvāt /
children.translated_text:
The obligation — even qualified <s>apūrva</s> — is not durable, because [the effort producing it] has perished.
Nor does mere <s>apūrva</s> in its overseeing [function] have instrumentality, because being only a part of the word-meaning, it is not a correlate of connection.

children.text:
anye tvanvayavirodhirūpaviraho yogyatā ata eva vahninā siñcatītyatra tad bhrame bhavatyanvayabhramaḥ /
yāge cānvayavirodhirūpaviraho yogyānupalabdhyā sugama eva /
na ca yāge āśuvināśitvaṃ kālāntarabhāviphalajanakatvavirodhīti vācyam /
anubhave kvāthapāne cāśuvinaśini kālāntarabhāviphalajanakatvād yāge 'pyantatastatsattvāt anyathāpūrvavaiphalyāt /
asmādanvayaprayojakarūpavattvaṃ laghviti cet na tatsattvepyanāptokte vyabhicārādanvayavirodhitvena yatkiñcit pratisandhānaṃ tatrāstyeva antato bādhakapramāviṣayatvasyaiva virodhinojñānāditi /
children.translated_text:
Others, however, [hold that] fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>) is the absence of a form that contradicts the connection (<s>anvayavirodhi</s>). Precisely for this reason, in 'sprinkle with fire,' when there is an error [about that], there is an erroneous cognition of connection.
And in sacrifice, the absence of a form contradicting the connection is easily [ascertained] through non-apprehension of the fit (<s>yogyānupalabdhi</s>).
Nor should it be said that in sacrifice, the quick-perishability contradicts the capacity to produce a result coming at a later time —
because in experience, [things like] drinking a decoction (<s>kvāthapāna</s>), though quickly perishable, have the capacity to produce results at a later time; and sacrifice too ultimately possesses that [capacity] — otherwise <s>apūrva</s> would be purposeless.
[Objection:] Therefore, possessing a form that motivates the connection is simpler [as a definition of fitness]. [Reply:] No — because even when that [form] is present, there is deviation in [statements] by unreliable persons. And [in those cases,] some recollection functioning as a contradicting factor of the connection does exist — at least the cognition that [the statement] is the content of a sublating cognition serves as the contradicting [factor].

children.text:
kāmyasādhanatvajñānameva pravartakaṃ lāghavāt /
siddhaudanastṛptikāmo laghūpāye bhojane pravartate na tu pāke gurarūpāyatvāt jalādyarthī ca sannihite /
ata eva jyotiṣṭomādau śrutasvargaphalakatve 'pi gurūpāyatvenānanuṣṭhānalakṣaṇāpramāṇyāpattyā phalabhūmā kalpyate iṣṭotpattyanāntarīyakaśramajanakatvaṃ vā pratibandhakaṃ /
api ca kāmyavyavahitasādhanatayā jñātameva yadi kāmī kartavyatayāvaitīti niyamaḥ tadā pūrvamapi kāryatayā nāvagamyeta anvitābhidhānāt pūrvaṃ kāmyasādhanatābodhakābhāvādupadānasasyānvitābhidhānottarakālīnatvāt / ata eva kāmyādanyadityādi prakāradvayaṃ nirastaṃ kāryatābuddhau pravṛttau vā kāmyasādhanatvasyaiva hetutvāt /
na ca kārye ghaṭādau liṅaśaktigrahakāle svargakāmānvayāyogyatvāt kriyānirāsastathā yāgānvayānupapattyā ghaṭādinirāso 'pi syāt /
na hi yāgaviṣayako ghaṭādiḥ sambhavati anyathā anvitābhidhānadaśāyāmapi tanniraso na syāt /
syādetat svargakāmānvayānupapattyā tadanvayayogye liṅaśaktigrahaḥ sthāyikāryañca tathā ataḥ śaktigrahakāle kriyānirāso yujyate na ghaṭādeḥ /
yajipadamantarbhāvya svargakāmapada-liṅapadābhyāṃ anvitābhidhānadaśāyāṃ ghaṭādinirāso yāgānvayayogyatvāditi tat kiṃ śaktigrahakāle yāgānvayanupapattirhastapihitā yena ghaṭādinirāsikā sā na pratisandhīyeta /
pratyuta pratyayasyāntaraṅgaprakṛtyarthānvayaṃ bodhayata evetarānvayabodhakatvamiti tadanvayānupapattipratisandhīyate /
pratyuta pratyayasyāntaraṅgaprakṛtyarthānvayaṃ bodhayata evetarānvayabodhakatvamiti tadanvayānupapattipratisandhānameva prāthamikaṃ puruṣadoṣādapratisandhāne śaktigraho bhrama eva ghaṭāderaśakyatvāt puruṣaviśeṣaṃ prati apūrvavācyatāpatteśca /
ghaṭādīnāmanantatvena yadi tannirāso na śakyaḥ tadā anvitābhidhānadaśāyāmapi na syāt pākādīnāṃ kriyātveneva pṛthivītvādinā nirāsasambhavācca /
evañca pracuradravya guṇa-karmasu nirasteṣu kva kārye dharmiṇi śaktigrahaḥ /
na ca viśeṣe niraste 'pi kāryasāmānyaṃ na nirastamiti vācyam /
na hi viśeṣāviṣayaṃ sāmānyajñānaṃ sambhavati /
etenāpūrvasādhāraṇakāryatvena ghaṭādau śaktigraha iti parāstam /
agṛhītāsaṃsargeṣu sthāyitvakāryatva-svargajanakatveṣu tajjñaneṣu vā śaktigraha ityapi parāstaṃ sthāyināṃ ghaṭādīnāṃ nirāsāt dharmamātre ca śaktigrahasya prakṛte 'nupayogāt /
kiñca teṣu śaktigrahaḥ samuditeṣu pratyekaṃ vā nādyaḥ prathamaṃ samudāyasyaikajñānāviṣayatvāt viṣayatve vā pūrvameva viśiṣṭasya sattve 'pūrvatvavyāghātaḥ ekajñānaviṣayasākāṅkṣadharma-dharmiṇoreva viśiṣṭatvāt /
na dvitīyaḥ evaṃ hi liṅapadāt smaraṇatrayaṃ yajipadācca yāgasmaraṇa /
na ca caturṇāṃ teṣāṃ yaugapadyamasti /
na ca pratyekaṃ śaktigrahe 'pi samuditaviṣayakamekameva smaraṇaṃ liṅapadāditi yuktaṃ samudāyasya pūrvamananubhavāt /
smaraṇañca yadi sākāṅkṣadharma-dharmiviṣayakamekaṃ tadā apūrvatvakṣatiḥ ekajñānārūḍhayoḥ sākāṅkṣadharma-dharmiṇoreva viśiṣṭatvāt tanniyatatvādvā /
etena svargādipadeṣu agṛhītāsaṃsargadharma-dharmiṣu śaktigraha iti vyudastam /
pratyeka-samudāyaviṣayakasmaraṇavikalpagrāsāt /
astu vā liṅgaḥ kārye lakṣaṇā yathā hi mañcāḥ krośantītyādau puruṣaviśeṣaḥ prāgananubhūto 'pyanubhūyate itarapadāllākṣaṇikasyānubhāvakatvāt tathāpūrvamapi astu ca svargakāmakāryaviṣayo yāga iti śābdānubhavānantaramarthādyāgaviṣayakaṃ kāryamiti jñānaṃ anupapattiprabhavaṃ /
ata eva śābdabodhānantaramaupādānikabodhātpradhātpravṛttiḥ /
kiñcāpūrvavācyatve 'pi na kalañjaṃ bhakṣayedityāditaḥ kalañjabhakṣaṇābhāvaviṣayakamapūrvamavagamyāpi na pravarteta tadabhāve tathāhi bhakṣaṇe rāgādasya kartavyatābuddhirjātā śabdācca bhakṣaṇābhāve niṣphalāt kāryāt saphalaṃ garīya iti nyāyena sukhahetau bhakṣaṇa eva pravarteta na tadabhāve niṣedhāpūrvameva phalamiti cet na tasya sukha-duḥkhābhāvānyatayā phaṇḍatvenatadajanakatayāca gauṇa-mukhyaprayojanatvābhāvāt /
sukhavadapūrvamapi prayojanamiti cet na loke tathānavagamāt /
alaukikayoḥ svargapavargayoḥ lokāvagataprayojanasukha duḥkhābhāvajātīyatayā prayojanatvaṃ vede 'pi kāmyasthale kāmyasādhanasyaivāpūrvasya gauṇaprayojanasya liṅgābhidhānaṃ kāmyasādhanatājñānaṃ vinā kāmikāryatvasya bodhayitumaśakyatvāt na tu svataḥ prayojanatvena tatrāsāmārthyādanupayogācca pravṛtterbhojanādāvivalokakḷptakāmyasādhanatājñānāt kāryatājñānādvā gauṇaprayojanatvenaivopapatteḥ /

children.translated_text: The cognition of being a means to the desired end alone is the impeller, by parsimony. One who has rice already available and desires satisfaction engages in eating, which is the easier means, but not in cooking, since it is a more laborious means; and one who desires water [engages with] what is at hand. For this very reason, even though the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and similar [rituals] are heard to have heaven as their result, since they are laborious means, abundance of result (<s>phalabhūmā</s>) must be postulated to avoid the invalidity characterized by non-performance; or alternatively, the production of fatigue as a necessary concomitant of the arising of the desired result is the obstructor. Furthermore, if the rule is that what the desirer knows merely as a mediate means to the desired end, he understands as obligatory — then even prior to that, it would not be cognized as an effect, because prior to connected denotation (<s>anvitābhidhāna</s>) there is no conveyer of being-a-means-to-the-desired-end, and the complementary sentences operate only after connected denotation. For this very reason, the two alternatives beginning with 'what is other than the desired end' are refuted, since being-a-means-to-the-desired-end alone is the cause both of the cognition of obligatoriness and of volitional activity. Nor is there rejection of action at the time of grasping the capacity of the <s>liṅga</s> (injunctive suffix) with respect to effects such as pots, due to unsuitability of connection with the desirer of heaven — for in that case, there should equally be rejection of pots and the like due to the impossibility of connection with the sacrifice. For a pot and the like pertaining to the sacrifice are not possible; otherwise, even at the stage of connected denotation, their rejection would not occur. One might say: The capacity of the <s>liṅga</s> is grasped with respect to what is suitable for connection with the desirer of heaven, through the impossibility of connection with the latter; and the effect is permanent and likewise — therefore rejection of action at the time of capacity-grasping is justified, but not of pots and the like. Having incorporated the word '<s>yaji</s>' (sacrifice), at the stage of connected denotation through the words '<s>svargakāma</s>' (desirer of heaven) and the <s>liṅga</s> suffix, pots and the like are rejected due to suitability of connection with the sacrifice — so what? Is the impossibility of connection with the sacrifice at the time of capacity-grasping concealed, such that the rejection of pots and the like is not connected? On the contrary, since the suffix, conveying the connection of its inner (proximate) stem-meaning, thereby conveys connection with the other [meaning] too — the very connection of the impossibility of that connection is primary; non-connection due to human deficiency makes the capacity-grasping itself erroneous, since pots and the like are not possible [as meanings], and there would be the consequence of expressibility of <s>apūrva</s> for particular persons [only]. If the rejection of pots and the like is not possible due to their infinity, then it would not be possible even at the stage of connected denotation; and the rejection of cooking and the like is possible through [the property of] earth-ness and the like, just as through action-ness. And thus, when abundant substances, qualities, and actions have been rejected, with respect to what effect-possessing property is the capacity grasped? Nor should one say that even when the particulars are rejected, the universal 'effect-ness' is not rejected — for cognition of the universal without [any] particular is not possible. By this, [the view] that the capacity is grasped with respect to pots and the like under the effect-ness common to <s>apūrva</s> is refuted. [The view] that the capacity is grasped with respect to permanence, effect-ness, and heaven-producing-ness — whose relations have not been grasped — or with respect to cognitions of those, is also refuted, since permanent things like pots are rejected, and capacity-grasping with respect to the mere property is useless in the present context. Furthermore, is the capacity grasped with respect to those [properties] collectively or individually? Not the first, because initially the collection is not the object of a single cognition; or if it were, there would be a contradiction of unprecedented-ness, since the qualified [entity] would already exist, the expectant property and property-possessor being qualified only as objects of a single cognition. Not the second, because then there would be three recollections from the <s>liṅga</s> suffix and a recollection of sacrifice from the word '<s>yaji</s>' — and there is no simultaneity of those four. Nor is it proper that even when capacity is grasped individually, there is a single recollection with a collective object from the <s>liṅga</s> suffix, because the collection has not been previously experienced. And if the recollection is a single one having the expectant property and property-possessor as its object, then the unprecedented nature is damaged, since the qualified [entity] is precisely the expectant property and property-possessor that have ascended to a single cognition, or because it is determined by that. By this, [the view] that capacity is grasped with respect to the property and property-possessor in words like '<s>svarga</s>' (heaven), whose relations have not been grasped, is refuted — consumed by the dilemma of recollection with individual or collective objects. Alternatively, let the <s>liṅga</s> have secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) with respect to the effect: just as in '<s>mañcāḥ krośanti</s>' (the platforms cry out), a particular person not previously experienced is experienced, because the other word has the capacity to produce experience of the secondary meaning — similarly with <s>apūrva</s>. And let the verbal experience be 'the sacrifice, whose effect is the object of the desirer of heaven,' after which through implication (<s>arthāpatti</s>) the cognition 'an effect pertaining to the sacrifice' arises. For this very reason, volitional activity arises from the cognition through implication (<s>aupādānika bodha</s>) that follows the verbal cognition, being stronger [than the verbal cognition alone]. Furthermore, even on the view that <s>apūrva</s> is expressible, from '<s>na kalañjaṃ bhakṣayet</s>' (one should not eat <s>kalañja</s>), even though <s>apūrva</s> having as its content the absence of eating <s>kalañja</s> is understood, one would not [thereby] be impelled [to abstain] — in the absence of that [abstention], for thus: since through passion one has formed the conviction of obligatoriness regarding eating, and from the word [conveying] that in the absence of eating, by the maxim 'what has a result is weightier than what is fruitless,' one would engage in eating itself as a cause of pleasure, not in its absence — if one says that the <s>apūrva</s> of the prohibition is itself the result — no, because being different from pleasure and absence of suffering, and being a <s>phaṇḍa</s> (barren entity) that does not produce them, it lacks both primary and secondary purpose-hood. If one says that <s>apūrva</s> too, like pleasure, is a purpose — no, because it is not so understood in the world. The supramundane heaven (<s>svarga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) have purpose-hood by being of the same kind as the worldly-known purposes of pleasure and absence of suffering. Even in the <s>Veda</s>, in the context of desired [rites], the <s>liṅga</s> denotes <s>apūrva</s> as a secondary purpose that is a means to the desired end, since the obligatoriness pertaining to desire cannot be conveyed without the cognition of being-a-means-to-the-desired-end — but not as an intrinsic purpose, due to incapacity and uselessness there, since volitional activity even in eating and the like is explicable either from the worldly-established cognition of being-a-means-to-the-desired-end or from the cognition of obligatoriness, as a secondary purpose alone.
