nitya-niṣedhayorapūrvaṃ svataḥ prayojanaṃ liṅgābhidhīyate /
kāmyasthale hi dharmigrāhakaliṅgādinā pravartakakāryatvenāpūrvamabhihitamatonityādāvapi kāryatvenāpūrvabodhanaṃ na tu svataḥ prayojanatvena /
nanu nitye loka-vedāvagatagauṇa-mukhyaprayojanābhāve sati liṅgevāpūrvasya svataḥ prayojanatvaṃ bodhayati tena vinā pravṛttiparatvānirvāhāditi cet na nirupadhīcchāviṣayatvaṃ hi svataḥ prayojanatvaṃ apūrvasya siddhaṃ liṅgā bodhanīyam /
na ca tādṛśecchāviṣayo 'pūrvaṃ kvacidapi siddham /
na ca liṅgevāpūrvecchāṃ janayitvā tāṃ bodhayati tasyāstatrāsāmarthyādicchāyāḥ sāmagṣantarajanyatvācca /
ato 'pi kāmye nitye cecchāviṣayatvaṃ prayojanatvamapūrvasya liṅgādinā na bodhyate apūrvecchāyāḥ śābdajñānāt pūrvaṃ asattvāt kintu śābdakāryatājñānāt seti /
atha nitye kāryatvenaivāpūrvasyābhidhānaṃ na tu svataḥ prayojanatvena kintu liṅgā apūrve bodhite tasya svataḥ prayojanatvamicchāviṣayatvaṃ sambhavati sukhajñānavadapūrvajñānasyāpi svata evecchājanakatvāt tataḥ kāmyāpūrvasādhanatājñānānnitye kāryatābodhāt pravṛttiriti cet na apūrvajñānasyecchāhetutvenākḷptvāt /
kāmyāpūrve hi lokakḷpteṣṭasādhanatājñānādevecchā na tvapūrvatvajñānāt /
śāstrasthasya śāstrajakartavyatājñānaṃ balavaditi cet saphalaviṣayaṃ tathā idañca niṣphalaviṣayam /
atha pravṛttimato nivṛttiniyoge 'dhikāra iti yadā bhakṣaṇapravṛttastadā tanniṣedhe śābdakāryatādhīriti tayā viparītaprayatne janite rāgāt kriyotpattiḥ tenaiva pratibandhāt rāgakāritapravṛttimupajīvya hi nivṛttikāryatā śāstreṇa bodhitā atastena bodhane svaphalaṃ viparītakṛtiravaśyaṃ utpadyeti śāstrasya balavattvamiti cet na nivṛttikāryatābodhe 'pi nivṛttau prayatna eva notpadyate yasya pratibandhakatā syāt syācca nivṛttikāryatābodhakamapramāṇaṃ niṣphalatvena tatra kṛterabhāvāt /
atha kalañjabhakṣaṇasya nindārthavādena balavadaniṣṭasādhanatvāvagamāt tadbhakṣaṇe na pravartata iti cet evamapi kalañjabhakṣaṇe nivartatāṃ tadabhāve niṣprayojanakatayā pravṛttau kimāyātamiti /
etena nityāpūrvasādhane sandhyāvandanādāvapi pravṛttirapāstā kriyāyāḥ kaṣṭatvāt loke pacetetyādau kāryatveṣṭasādhanatvarūpadharmaśaktatvena jñātā liṅga svargakāmo yajetetyādau tadanvayaṃ yāge yogyatādivaśād bodhayatīti na vede dharmiṇi śaktikalpanā pratītā ca svargasādhanatā sākṣādasādhanasya yāgasya vyāpāramantareṇānupapadyamānā tannirvāhakaṃ vyāpāramapūrvaṃ kalpayati /
nanu nirupadhipūrvavartitā kāraṇatā sā vyāpāreṇa nirvāhyata ityatra kor'thaḥ kiṃ kriyate uta jñāpyate nādyaḥ uttaravarttitvena vyāpārasya tatrāsāmārthyāt netaraḥ liṅgaiva tadbodhanāt ciradhvastaṃ kāraṇaṃ vyāpāreṇa vyāptamiti cet na vipakṣe bādhakābhāvenāprayojakatvādanyathā aindriyakaṃ kāraṇamatīndriyavyāpārakamiti yāgānubhavayodarśanāt tathā kalpyate /
children.translated_text:
In the case of obligatory (<s>nitya</s>) and prohibitory (<s>niṣedha</s>) [injunctions], <s>apūrva</s> (unprecedented transcendent result) is denoted by the injunctive suffix (<s>liṅ</s>) as an intrinsic purpose (<s>svataḥ prayojana</s>).
For in the case of desire-motivated (<s>kāmya</s>) [rites], <s>apūrva</s> is expressed by the <s>liṅ</s> suffix and other [elements] that apprehend the property-bearer, as being-an-effect that impels; therefore, in obligatory [rites] too, the cognition of <s>apūrva</s> is through being-an-effect, not through its being an intrinsic purpose.
[Objection:] In obligatory [rites], when there is an absence of both secondary and primary purposes known from ordinary experience and the <s>Veda</s>, the <s>liṅ</s> suffix itself conveys the intrinsic purpose-hood of <s>apūrva</s>, since without it the orientation toward activity cannot be sustained. [Reply:] No, for being the object of unconditional desire (<s>nirupadhīcchāviṣayatva</s>) — which is the intrinsic purpose-hood of <s>apūrva</s> — is already established [and therefore] needs to be conveyed by the <s>liṅ</s> suffix.
But <s>apūrva</s> as the object of such [unconditional] desire is not established anywhere.
Nor does the <s>liṅ</s> suffix first generate the desire for <s>apūrva</s> and then convey it, since [the <s>liṅ</s> suffix] lacks the capacity for that, and because desire is produced by another causal aggregate (<s>sāmagrī</s>).
Moreover, the purpose-hood of <s>apūrva</s> — being the object of desire — is not conveyed by the <s>liṅ</s> suffix and the like, either in desire-motivated or obligatory [rites], since the desire for <s>apūrva</s> does not exist prior to the verbal cognition; rather, [the desire] arises from the knowledge of being-an-effect generated by verbal testimony.
If [it is said:] in obligatory [rites], <s>apūrva</s> is expressed merely through being-an-effect, not through intrinsic purpose-hood, but once <s>apūrva</s> is cognized through the <s>liṅ</s> suffix, its intrinsic purpose-hood — being the object of desire — is possible, since the knowledge of <s>apūrva</s>, like the knowledge of pleasure, is itself a generator of desire, and therefore activity in obligatory [rites follows] from the knowledge of being-an-effect, as [it does] from the knowledge of being-a-means-to-the-<s>apūrva</s> in desire-motivated [rites] — [we reply:] no, because the knowledge of <s>apūrva</s> has not been postulated as a cause of desire.
For in the case of desire-motivated <s>apūrva</s>, desire arises only from the knowledge of being-a-means-to-the-desired, which is established in ordinary experience, not from the knowledge of <s>apūrva</s>-hood [as such].
If [it is said that] for one engaged in scriptural [study], the knowledge of obligatoriness generated by scripture is powerful — [we reply:] that is so when it concerns a fruitful object, but this [obligatory rite] concerns a fruitless object.
If [it is said:] when one who is [already] engaged [in eating] is enjoined to desist, the eligibility (<s>adhikāra</s>) [for the prohibition applies]; that is, when one is engaged in eating, the verbal cognition of the being-an-effect of desisting [arises] from the prohibition, and when the contrary effort is generated by that [cognition], the action [of eating] arises from passion (<s>rāga</s>), [and continues] due to obstruction by that very [passion]; for the being-an-effect of desisting, conveyed by scripture, presupposes the passion-caused activity, and therefore when [scripture] conveys [the prohibition], its own result — the contrary effort — necessarily arises, hence the authority of scripture — [we reply:] no, because even when the being-an-effect of desisting is cognized, the effort toward desisting itself does not arise, [and so] there is nothing whose obstruction [by passion] could [be claimed]; and the means of valid knowledge that conveys the being-an-effect of desisting would be invalid, being fruitless, since no effort [toward desisting] occurs there.
If [it is said:] since the being-a-means-to-preponderant-undesirable-[consequences] of eating <s>kalañja</s> is understood from the censuring <s>arthavāda</s>, one does not engage in eating it — [we reply:] even so, let one desist from eating <s>kalañja</s>; but in the absence of that [particular situation], what purpose does activity [toward the prohibition] serve, being purposeless?
By this, activity even toward obligatory [rites] like <s>sandhyāvandana</s> and the like, which are means to the <s>apūrva</s> of obligatory [rites], is refuted, due to the effortfulness of the action. [On this alternative view:] the <s>liṅ</s> suffix, known in ordinary usage like 'he should cook' as having denotative power in being-an-effect having the form of being-a-means-to-the-desired as a property, conveys [in Vedic usage like] 'one who desires heaven should sacrifice' the connection of that [property] with the sacrifice by the force of fitness and the like. Thus, there is no postulation of denotative power in the property-bearer in the <s>Veda</s>. And the being-a-means-to-heaven, which is cognized, is untenable for the sacrifice, which is not a direct means [to heaven], without an intermediary operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>); [hence] it postulates <s>apūrva</s> as the intermediary operation that fulfills [the causal connection].
[Objection:] The unconditional antecedent condition is causality; it is fulfilled by the intermediary operation — but what is the meaning here? Is [the <s>apūrva</s>] produced or [merely] made known? Not the first, since the intermediary, being subsequent [to the sacrifice], lacks the capacity for that. Not the second, since the <s>liṅ</s> suffix itself conveys it. [Reply:] If [it is said that] the cause, long since destroyed, is pervaded by [its] intermediary operation — no, because the absence of an invalidating cognition in the counter-instance renders it non-conclusive. Otherwise, just as it is observed in the case of sacrifice and experience that a perceptible cause has a supersensible intermediary operation, [similarly] it is postulated [for the Vedic case].

prāyaścittādīnāñca phalapratibandhakatvameva prāyaścittasya tasmādenasaḥ pūto bhavatīti yat phalaṃ śrutamasti tasya niṣiddhakriyātaḥ phalabhāk na bhavatītyarthaḥ ``dharmaḥ kṣarati kīrtanādityarthaḥ /
kṣaratītyatra bādhakaṃ vinā na lakṣaṇeti cet na upasthitatvena vihitakriyāyāmeva dharmapadaśaktigrahasya bādhakatvāt /
na caitasya mukhyatvārthaṃ padārthāntare śaktiḥ lakṣaṇocchedāpatteḥ vihitakriyākartṛtvajñānena dhārmikapadaprayogācca /
etena devadattādyaśarīraṃ devadattaviśeṣaguṇapreritabhūtapūrvakaṃ janyatve sati tadbhogasādhanatvāt tannirṃmitasragvadityanumānāt tatsiddhiriti parāstam /
janmāntarīyajñānādibhireva tajjanakatvābhimataiḥ siddhasādhanāditi maivaṃ ciradhvastasya vyāpārasattve kāraṇatvamiti nirupādhyanvaya-vyatirekābhyāṃ vyāptyavadharaṇāt yāgasya ciradhvastakāraṇatvena vyāpārakalpanāt /
kārye vyāpārasya pṛthaganvaya-vyatirekagrahastadvyāpārakatve upādhiriti cet na saṃskāre tadabhāve 'pyanubhavasya tadvyāpārakatvāt /
na cāprayojakatvaṃ yāgo yadi ciradhvastatve sati savyāpāro na syāt svargasādhanaṃ ghaṭavaditi vipakṣe bādhāt /
na cātra kāraṇatāgrāhakābhāva upādhiḥ tenāpi samaṃ vyāptyavadhāraṇe tasyāpyāpādanāt /
na caindriyakasyātīndriyavyāpāravattvaniyamaḥ savyāpāratve kāryāvyavahitapūrvasamaye asattvasyopādhitvenāprayojakatvāt /
nanvevaṃ sandhyāvandanākaraṇasya duḥkhasādhanatvaśruteḥ tatkaraṇaprāgabhāvo duḥkhahetustathāca tasya sthiratvena duḥkhajananasambhavāt na pāpe pramāṇam /
na ca prāyaścittavaiphalyaṃ prāgabhāvanāśa eva tena kriyata iti tanna dhvaṃsa-prāgabhāvānavacchinnakālasya pratiyogikālatvena tadā karaṇāpatteriti cet na sandhyākālīnākaraṇasya duḥkhajanakatvena viśiṣṭasya sandhyākālāpagame 'nupagamāt /
na ca sandhyākālīnākaraṇe viśeṣaṇaṃ kintu pratiyoṅgini karaṇe tathāca viśiṣṭābhāvaḥ sthira eveti vācyam /
sandhyāyā dvyakaraṇe 'nvayastasya padārthatvāt na tu karaṇe tasya padārthekadeśatvenāpradhānatvāt tathāpi dhvaṃsa eva vyāpāro 'stu tava sahabhāvānirūpakasyāpi kāraṇatvāt tasyānantatve 'pi svabhāvāt sāvadhiphalajanakatvam /
yatra yad dhvaṃsohetustatra tatprāgabhāvo 'pīti cet na duḥkhadhvaṃsajanyadadhni mithyādhīdhvaṃsasādhyamuktau ca vyabhicārāt
children.translated_text:
And expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) and the like function as obstructors of the result (<s>phala</s>). The meaning of '[by performing] expiation, one is purified from that sin' — what result is heard as existing [from the enjoined rite], from that result of the prohibited action one does not become a recipient — that is the meaning. [Similarly,] the meaning of '<s>dharma</s> diminishes from [mere] recitation.'
If [it is said:] in the word 'diminishes' (<s>kṣarati</s>), without an invalidating cognition there is no figurative usage (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) — no, because the grasping of the denotative power of the word <s>dharma</s> in the enjoined action alone, which [is the meaning already] presented, serves as the invalidating cognition.
Nor is there a denotative power in another word-meaning for the purpose of making this primary (<s>mukhya</s>), since that would lead to the destruction of figurative usage; and because the word <s>dhārmika</s> (righteous person) is used with reference to knowledge of being the agent of an enjoined action.
By this, the [argument] that <s>Devadatta</s>'s body and the like, being produced and being means to the enjoyment of [the results of <s>Devadatta</s>'s actions], are preceded by elements impelled by the particular qualities of <s>Devadatta</s>, and therefore, through the inference 'this is created by him, like a garland,' [the existence of <s>apūrva</s>] is established — this is refuted,
since there is the fallacy of establishing what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>) through the very things — knowledge from previous births and the like — that are accepted as its causes. [Objection:] Do not [say] so, for the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) is ascertained through unconditional positive and negative concomitance: 'causality consists in having an intermediary operation when [the cause is] long since destroyed'; and the intermediary operation is postulated for the sacrifice as a cause that was long since destroyed.
If [it is said that] the separate apprehension of positive and negative concomitance of the intermediary operation with the effect is a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>) for [establishing] its intermediary-operation-hood — no, because even in the case of an impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>), experience functions as its intermediary operation even in the absence of [the original cause].
Nor is there non-conclusiveness: if the sacrifice, though long since destroyed, were not to have an intermediary operation, it would not be a means to heaven, like a pot — [thus] there is an invalidating cognition in the counter-instance.
Nor is the absence of [an independent] apprehender of causality a limiting condition here, since even with that [supposed condition], the pervasion would be equally ascertainable, as the same [objection] could be raised [against it].
Nor is there a rule that a perceptible [cause] must have a supersensible intermediary operation; the being-accompanied-by-an-intermediary-operation [is not universal, since] the non-existence [of the cause] at the time immediately prior to the effect, serving as a limiting condition, renders [the argument] non-conclusive.
[Objection:] Then, since the non-performance of <s>sandhyāvandana</s> is heard as a means to suffering, the prior absence of its performance would be a cause of suffering; and since that [prior absence] is permanent, the possibility of generating suffering [would persist indefinitely], and therefore there would be no valid means [of knowing sin].
Nor is the expiation fruitless, since it effects precisely the destruction of the prior absence [of the rite]. [Reply:] That is wrong, because since the time not delimited by either the destruction or the prior absence [of the rite] has the character of being the time of the counterpositive, performance [of the rite] would be absurdly possible at that time. [Reply:] No, because the non-performance qualified by [occurring at] the <s>sandhyā</s> time, being a specific [entity], is not accepted [as continuing] after the passing of the <s>sandhyā</s> time.
Nor should it be said that the qualifier is not in the non-performance at the <s>sandhyā</s> time but rather in the performance as counterpositive, and thus the qualified absence is indeed permanent —
for the connection [of the word 'non-performance'] is with the non-performance at <s>sandhyā</s> time, since that is the word-meaning, not with the performance [as counterpositive], since that is a subordinate part of the word-meaning. Even so, let the destruction alone be the intermediary operation, since on your view even [something] that does not determine co-existence can be a cause; and though [the destruction] is eternal, by its very nature it produces a result with a limit.
If [it is said:] wherever a destruction is a cause, there the prior absence too [should be a cause] — no, because there is deviation in [the case of] curds produced from the destruction of suffering, in the destruction of false cognition, and in liberation which is to be accomplished by destruction.

children.text:
pratibandhakābhāvatvena hetutve tathābhāvācca /
dhvaṃsenānupapattiḥ kathaṃ tenaiva samādhātavyeti cet na dhvaṃse sati tadvyāpāratvajñānaṃ vinānupapattestadvyāpāratvakalpanayā śānteriti /
maivaṃ /
pratiyāgi-dhvaṃsayorekatrājanakatvāt /
na hi niyamato yaddhvaṃse sati yadabhavati tat tatra kāraṇam /
children.translated_text:
If the causality [of prior absence] is through being the absence of an obstructor, and there is no such absence [in the relevant cases] —
If [it is objected:] since the impossibility is with the destruction, it must be resolved by the destruction alone — no, because the impossibility [is resolved] by the postulation that the destruction functions as its intermediary operation, when there is knowledge that [the effect occurs] in the presence of the destruction — thus cessation [of the sin is explained].
Do not [say] so.
Because the counterpositive and its destruction do not [both] produce the same [effect] in a single [locus].
For it is not the case that invariably whatever occurs in the presence of the destruction of something is the cause of that [occurrence].

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 431)
children.translated_text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 431)

children.text:
na ca saṃsargābhāvatvena hetutve tatheti vācyam /
vyabhicārābhāvena tasyāpi prayojakatvāt /
atha śabdād yāgakāraṇatā vyāpāraṃ vinā tadanupapatteḥ tajjanyadhvaṃsasya kāraṇatvakalpanamityubhayamapi janakaṃ anyatra tu mānābhāvānna tatheti cet na yāgadhvaṃsasya yāgajanyasvargaṃ prati janakatvasya pramāṇāntaravirodhenārthāpattyāpyakalpanāt /
astu tarhi devatāprītireva vyāpāra iti cet yāgasya devatāprītihetutve mānābhāvāt gaṅgāsnānādau devatāprītihetutve mānābhāvāt gaṅgāsnānādau devatāviraheṇa tadasambhavāt /
na ca tatrāpi tatprītiḥ tasya tatprītihetutve mānābhāvāt lāghavena kartu-bhoktṛgatavyāpārakalpanācca /
nanu nāyaṃ niyamaḥ putrakṛtagayāśrāddhādinā pitari pitṛkṛtajāteṣṭyā putre cādṛṣṭotpatteḥ /
atha tatrāpi kartaryevādṛṣṭaṃ vihitakriyāyāḥ yāgasyeva kartṛgatādṛṣṭajanakatvāt /
na ca mukte putre tadadṛṣṭanāśāt pitari na svargaḥ syāditi vācyam /
adṛṣṭasya phalanāśyatayā pitari svargābhāvenādṛṣṭānāśāt svavṛttibhogajanakādṛṣṭasya muktivirodhitvāt na tu pitṛgatamadṛṣṭaṃ janyate mukte pitari doṣābhāvena yogināmiva vihitakriyāyāḥ pitradṛṣṭājanakatvāt tathātve ca sāṅgamapi śrāddhādikaṃ niṣphalaṃ syāditi taddhidheraprāmāṇyāpattiḥ putragatādṛṣṭena ca mukte pitari sukhotpattau na virodhaḥ yogināmiva sukhotpattau doṣasyāhetutvāt /
children.translated_text: Nor should one say that when [absence of connection] as absence of the relation is the cause, it is so — because that too has impelling force through the absence of deviation. If one says: From the word [of scripture], the causality of the sacrifice — since that is inexplicable without an operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>) — and the postulation of the causality of the destruction produced by it — both are generative, but elsewhere, due to the absence of a means of knowledge, it is not so — no, because the causality of the destruction of the sacrifice with respect to the heaven produced by the sacrifice is not postulated even through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), due to conflict with other means of valid knowledge. If one says: Let the gratification of the deity be the operation — [reply:] because there is no means of knowledge for the sacrifice's being a cause of divine gratification; and in bathing in the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the like, since there is no means of knowledge for that being a cause of divine gratification, and since in the absence of the deity there, that is impossible. Nor is there divine gratification in those cases either, because there is no means of knowledge for its being a cause of that gratification, and because by parsimony, an operation located in the agent and the enjoyer is postulated. Objection: This is not a rule, because <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit) arises in the father through the <s>Gayā</s> <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rite at <s>Gayā</s>) performed by the son, and in the son through the <s>Jāteṣṭi</s> (birth-rite) performed by the father. [Reply:] Even there, the <s>adṛṣṭa</s> is in the agent alone, because the enjoined action, like the sacrifice, generates <s>adṛṣṭa</s> located in the agent. Nor should one say that when the son is liberated, since his <s>adṛṣṭa</s> is destroyed, the father would not attain heaven — because <s>adṛṣṭa</s> is destroyed [only] by the destruction of its result, and since in the father there is no absence of heaven, the <s>adṛṣṭa</s> is not destroyed; and the <s>adṛṣṭa</s> that generates enjoyment in the father's existence is incompatible with liberation, but the <s>adṛṣṭa</s> located in the father is not generated when the father is liberated, due to the absence of defects, just as for <s>yogins</s> — the enjoined action does not generate <s>adṛṣṭa</s> in the father. And if so, even the <s>śrāddha</s> with all its limbs would be fruitless, leading to the invalidity of its injunction. And there is no contradiction in the arising of pleasure in the liberated father through <s>adṛṣṭa</s> located in the son, just as for <s>yogins</s>, defects are not the cause of the arising of pleasure.

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 440 )
children.translated_text: (Bibliotheca Indica 98, IV,2, p. 440)

children.text:
atha pitṛsukhaṃ pitṛpuṇyajanyamiti pitari puṇyaṃ tena vinā tadasambhavāt na putre tatra phalaprasaṅgāditi pitṛsvargakāmānājanyakriyā pitṛpuṇyaheturiti putrakriyāpi tajjaniketi cet evaṃ pitṛkriyāpi pitṛpuṇyajaniketi na tāṃ vinā pitari puṇyaṃ putrakriyā ca putrapuṇyajaniketi putre puṇyaṃ pitṛsvargakāmanājanyapuṇyatvena pitṛsvargaheturastu tatpuṇyaṃ pitṛvṛtti tatsukhahetupuṇyatvāt na putravṛtti tatsukhahetupuṇyatvāditi cet na tatpuṇyaṃ na pitṛvṛtti tatkṛtyajanyapuṇyatvāt putravṛtti vā tatkṛtapuṇyatvāt tasmāt pitṛsvargakāmanājanyapuṇyatvena pitṛsvargahetuteti putra eva tatpuṇyamiti /
maivaṃ /
svargopapādakaṃ hyapūrvaṃ svargāśraye kalpyate prathamopasthitatvāt lāghavāt kalpanāyāḥ sākṣādupapādakaviṣayatvācca /
na ca svargahetukāmanāśraye svargakāmanājanyakriyākartari vā vilambopasthitikatvāt gauravāt paramparayā svargopapādakatvācca /
yadi ca putrakṛtapuṇyena muktasya pituḥ śarīrādyutpattiḥ sukhañca syāt tadā sākṣividhayā asatyābhidhānādiputrakriyājanyapāpena ``sa viṣṭhāyāṃ kṛmirbhūtvā pitṛbhiḥ saha pacyate'' ityādibodhitanarakabhāgitāpi muktasya pituḥ syāt /
tathā ca putrakṛtatatathāvidhaśaṅkayā na kaścinmokṣārthaṃ brahmacaryādiduḥkhenātmānamavasādayet ``duḥkhenātyantaṃ vimuktaścarati na sa punarāvartate'' iti śrutivirodhaśca tathāca muktasya sukha-duḥkhe śarīrañca bhavatītpadarśanaṃ mukte pitari śrāddhādinā doṣābhāvādeva nādṛṣṭamutpadyate /
children.translated_text: If one says: The father's pleasure is produced by the father's merit; therefore merit must be in the father, since without it that [pleasure] is impossible; and not in the son, since that would lead to the consequence of results there — and the action not generated by the desire for the father's heaven is the cause of the father's merit, and so the son's action too generates that — [reply:] In that case, the father's action too generates the father's merit, so merit in the father is not impossible without [the son's action]; and the son's action generates the son's merit, so there is merit in the son. If one says that the merit has the character of being the cause of the father's heaven because of being merit not generated by the desire for the father's heaven — let that merit be located in the father, since it is merit whose cause is the father's pleasure; and not located in the son, since it is merit whose cause is the son's pleasure — no, that merit is not located in the father, since it is merit generated by the son's <s>kṛti</s> (effort); or it is located in the son, since it is merit made by the son. Therefore, since it is the cause of the father's heaven by virtue of being merit not generated by the desire for the father's heaven, that merit is in the son alone. Let it not be so. For the <s>apūrva</s> (unseen merit) that brings about heaven is postulated in the locus of heaven, since it is primarily presented, by parsimony of postulation, and because the postulation is concerned with what directly brings about [the result]. And not in the locus of the desire for the cause of heaven, or in the agent of the action generated by the desire for the heaven of the desirer of heaven — due to delayed presentation, complexity, and indirect bringing-about of heaven. And if by the merit produced by the son, the liberated father were to obtain a body and pleasure, then by the sin generated by the son's actions such as false statements — 'Having become a worm in excrement, he is cooked together with his ancestors' — the liberated father too would become a denizen of hell as taught by such [passages]. And thus, out of fear of the son's such [sinful] conduct, no one would afflict himself with the suffering of <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) and the like for the sake of liberation — and there would be contradiction with the <s>śruti</s> (scripture): 'Having been completely freed from suffering, he moves about and does not return again.' And thus the [absurd] demonstration that the liberated [father] has pleasure and suffering and a body [follows] — when the father is liberated, due to the very absence of defects, no <s>adṛṣṭa</s> arises through <s>śrāddha</s> and the like.

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 445)
children.translated_text: (Bibliotheca Indica 98, IV,2, p. 445)

children.text:
na caivaṃ sāṅgaśrāddhasyāpi niṣphalatvaṃ adṛṣṭotpattau svarūpasatodoṣasyāṅgasya vaiguṇyāt yathā vighnahetuduritaśūnyena kṛtaṃ maṅgalaṃ na pāpadhvaṃsaṃ janayati svarūpasataḥ pāpasyāṅgasyābhāvādevañca yāgasyāpi vyadhikaraṇo vyāpāro bhaviṣyatīti /
ucyate /
vihitakriyāyā kartṛgatavyāpāradvārā kālāntarabhāviphalaṃ janyata ityutsargaḥ sa ca balavatā bādhakenāpodyate prakṛte ca bādhakaṃ nāsti yathā śāstradeśitaṃ phalamanuṣṭhātarītyutsvargaḥ sa ca balavatā bādhakenāpodyate prakṛte ca bādhakaṃ nāsti yathā śāstradeśitaṃ phalamanuṣṭhātarīyatyutsvargaḥ /
putrakṛtagayāśrāddhāsya pitṛsvargaṃ prati pitṛkṛtajāteṣṭeḥ putrapūtatvādikaṃ prati hetutvasya śāstreṇa bodhanāt /
nanvayaṃ niyama eva pitṛyajña-jāteṣṭyādau paramparāsambandhena kartṛgatameva phalam /
na hi yasya kasyāpi pitari putre vā phalaṃ kintu svapitṛ-putrayostathāca svapitṛgatatvaṃ svargabhāgipitṛkatvaṃ vā paramparāsambandhaḥ phalena putrasya evaṃ pūtaputrakatvādikamapi pitṛgatameva /
na ca palasya kartṛgatvaṃ sākṣāt sambandhenaiveti vācyam /
grāma-paśu-putra-hiraṇyādīnāṃ paramparayā kartṛgatvamiti vyabhicārāt /
na hi grāmādayaḥ sākṣāt kartṛ-sambaddhāḥ /
evaṃ phalasya sākṣāt kartṛgāmitvabodhane śāstrasyotsargo na tu phalasya kartṛgāmitābodhane /
children.translated_text: Nor does the <s>śrāddha</s> with all its limbs become fruitless in this way — because in the generation of <s>adṛṣṭa</s>, there is deficiency of the limb that consists of the defect existing in its own nature, just as an auspicious rite performed by one free from the sin that causes obstacles does not produce the destruction of sin, due to the very absence of the sin that constitutes the limb. And thus, the operation of the sacrifice too will be in a different locus. It is said: The general rule (<s>utsarga</s>) is that the enjoined action produces a result that comes into being at a later time through an operation located in the agent — and that is overridden by a stronger sublating cognition. In the present case, there is no sublating cognition: just as the result taught by scripture belongs to the performer — that heaven — and that general rule is overridden by a stronger sublating cognition, and there is no sublating cognition in the present case. [This is] because scripture teaches the causality of the <s>Gayā</s> <s>śrāddha</s> performed by the son with respect to the father's heaven, and of the <s>Jāteṣṭi</s> performed by the father with respect to the son's purification and the like. Objection: This is precisely the rule — in the <s>Pitṛyajña</s> (ancestral sacrifice), <s>Jāteṣṭi</s>, and the like, the result belongs to the agent alone through an indirect relation. For the result goes not to just anyone's father or son, but to one's own father and son — and thus the indirect relation is either being-the-father-who-is-a-partaker-of-heaven or being-related-to-one's-own-father with respect to the result and the son. Similarly, being-the-father-of-a-purified-son and the like also belong to the agent alone. Nor should one say that the result's belonging to the agent is through a direct relation alone — due to deviation, since villages, cattle, sons, gold, and the like belong to the agent indirectly. For villages and the like are not directly related to the agent. Thus, the general rule of scripture is that the result directly goes to the agent, not that the result [always] goes to the agent.

children.text: yattu svargabhāgipitṛkatvaṃ na phalaṃ tatkāmanāyā adhikāriviśeṣaṇatvābhāvāt pitṛgatasvargakāma ityādiśruteḥ /
children.translated_text: As for [the claim] that being-the-father-who-is-a-partaker-of-heaven is not the result, because there is no mention of the desire for that as a qualifier of the eligible person, [considering] the <s>śruti</s> 'one who desires heaven for the father' and the like —

children.text: svataśca tathā kāmanayā pravṛttau śrutakāmanāviraheṇa prayoge 'ṅgavaiguṇyāt phalābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: And if, acting from such a desire intrinsically, in the performance with the absence of the scripturally stated desire, there would be the consequence of absence of result due to the deficiency of the limb.

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 449)
children.translated_text: (Bibliotheca Indica 98, IV,2, p. 449)

children.text:
kiñca svargabhāgipitṛkatvaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ tatra viśeṣyaṃ tatpitṛkatvaṃ na kāmyaṃ na vā phalaṃ siddhatvātadasādhyatvācca kintu viśeṣaṇaṃ pitṛgatasvarga iti sa eva phalamiti /
tanna /
na hi svargabhāgipitṛkatvaṃ phalaṃ api tu svargeṇa samaṃ putrasya paramparāsambandharūpaṃ taduktamiti /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, being-the-father-who-is-a-partaker-of-heaven is a qualified [entity]; therein, the qualificand — being the father of that [person] — is neither desired nor a result, since it is already accomplished and not producible. Rather, the qualifier is heaven located in the father, and that alone is the result. That is wrong. For being-the-father-who-is-a-partaker-of-heaven is not the result; rather, what has an indirect relational form with the son, together with heaven — that has been stated.

children.text:
ucyate yadi paramparāsambandhena putragatatvaṃ pitṛsvargasya tadā saṃyuktasamavāyādinā putretarasyāpi phalaṃ syāt /
sa sambandho na śāstreṇa bodhita iti cet tarhi svargabhāgipitṛkatvamapi na tathā śāstreṇabādhitatvāt grāma-paśu-hiraṇyādīnāñca siddhatvena na kāmyatvaṃ kintu tadviṣayakaṃ svatvaṃ kāmyaṃ phalamapi tadeva tacca sākṣādeva kartṛgatamiti kartṛgatatvena phalakāmanā tadgatameva śāstradeśitaṃ phalam /
ata eva kāmanāviṣayaḥ stagata eva svargaḥ phalaṃ yāgādeḥ svarga-pūtatvādeśca pitṛ-putragatatvena kāmyatvamiti śrāddha-jāteṣṭyādeḥ pitṛ-putragatameva phalam /
evañca mātāpitrādigatasvargakāmanayā putrādinā kṛtaṃ puṣkariṇīmahādānādikaṃ mātāpitrādisvargajanakameva kāmanāviṣayasvargasādhanatvena teṣāṃ śrutatvāt na hi svagatasvargakāmasya kartavyatāṃ puṣkariṇyādervidhirbodhayati tathā śruteḥ kintu svargakāmasya svargaśca svagataḥ paragato veti svargakāmatvamaviśiṣṭaṃ yajetetyātmanepadamapi kartabhipretakriyāphalamātrajanakatve na ca svargakāmo dadyādityādau svagatasvargakāmanāyā antaraṅgatvādautsargikatvācca svargakāmatvena svagatasvargakāma evocyate sāmānye bādhakaṃ vinā viśeṣaparatve mānābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: It is said: If the father's heaven belongs to the son through an indirect relation, then through the relation of contact-inherence (<s>saṃyukta-samavāya</s>) and the like, it would be the result of someone other than the son as well. If one says that relation is not taught by scripture — then being-the-father-who-is-a-partaker-of-heaven is also not taught by scripture, since it is sublated by it. And villages, cattle, gold, and the like, being already accomplished, are not desired [as such]; rather, ownership with respect to them is desired and is also the result, and that directly belongs to the agent — thus the desire for the result as belonging to the agent, and the result taught by scripture as going to the agent [is established]. For this very reason, the heaven that is the object of desire goes to the agent alone and is the result of the sacrifice and the like. And heaven, purification, and the like, being desired as located in the father and son, the result of <s>śrāddha</s>, <s>Jāteṣṭi</s>, and the like belongs to the father and son alone. And thus the great donations such as the <s>Puṣkariṇī</s> performed by the son and others with the desire for heaven going to the mother, father, and the like, are causes of heaven for the mother, father, and the like alone, because they are heard as means to heaven that is the object of desire. For the injunction does not convey to one who desires heaven for oneself the obligatoriness of the <s>Puṣkariṇī</s> and the like, given the scriptural statement. Rather, 'one who desires heaven' — and heaven may be for oneself or for another — the desire for heaven is unspecified. The <s>ātmanepada</s> (middle voice) in '<s>yajeta</s>' also indicates merely the result of the action intended by the agent. And in '<s>svargakāmo dadyāt</s>' (one who desires heaven should give) and the like, since the desire for heaven going to oneself is more proximate and is the default, by the term 'desirer of heaven,' only the desirer of heaven for oneself is meant, since in the absence of a sublating cognition for the general, there is no means of knowledge for a specific reference.

children.text:
kecittu samyag gṛhasthāśramaparipālanasya brahmalokāvāptiḥ phalaṃ śrūyata iti jāteṣṭi-pitṛyajñayorapi gṛhasthakarmatvena tadeva phalamiti phalasya kartṛgāmitve niyama eva prātisvikaphalābhiprāyeṇotsarga ityāhuḥ /
nanu yāvannityaparipālanasya tat phalaṃ na tu kāmyaśrāddhādeḥ kāmyāntarbhāve mānābhāvāt yāvat kāmyānuṣṭānāśakteśca /
yāvacchakyānuṣṭhānasyāpi nātrāntarbhāvaḥ kāmanāvirahādināpyakaraṇāt yāvannityānuṣṭhāne tatphalābhāvaprasaṅgāt nityasyaivāvaśyakatvenopasthityānvayācca /
api ca taiḥ karmabhiḥ pratyekamutpattyapūrvaṃ taiśca paramāpūrvaṃ janyate iti na gauravān mānābhāvācca /
kintvantimakriyā paripālanarūpakriyāntareṇa veti na sarvaṃ karma brahmalokāvāptiphalakamiti /
maivaṃ /
bhagavaduddeśena kṛtasya kāmyasya nityasya vā yasya kasyāpi karmaṇaḥ paripālanād brahmalokāvāptiḥ phalaṃ śrūyata iti jāteṣṭi-pitṛyajñayorapi tathā kṛtayostadeva phalam /
tathā ca bhagavadgītā ``yajñāyācarataḥ karma karmagranthirvilīyate /
children.translated_text:
Some, however, say that since it is heard [in scripture] that the result of properly maintaining the householder's stage of life (<s>gṛhasthāśrama</s>) is the attainment of <s>Brahmaloka</s> (the world of <s>Brahmā</s>), the same result applies to the birth-sacrifice (<s>jāteṣṭi</s>) and the ancestral offering (<s>pitṛyajña</s>) as well, since they are householder's duties. And since there is a rule that the result goes to the performer (<s>kartṛ</s>), [the statement about] the individual result is to be understood as a general principle (<s>utsarga</s>).
[Objection:] But that result belongs to the maintenance of all obligatory duties throughout life (<s>yāvannityaparipālana</s>), not to optional rites (<s>kāmya</s>) like <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rites) etc. — because there is no means of valid knowledge for including the optional within [the obligatory]; and because of the impossibility of performing all optional rites throughout life.
Nor is the performance of everything that is possible included here — because even through the absence of desire etc. [one may] not perform [some rites]; and because there would be the undesirable consequence that performing obligatory rites throughout life would not yield that result; and because the obligatory [rites] alone, being necessarily [to be performed], are presented in connection [with that result].
Furthermore, [the view that] those rites individually produce a proximate <s>apūrva</s> and collectively produce a supreme <s>apūrva</s> — [this is rejected] because of prolixity and because of the absence of a means of valid knowledge.
Rather, [the result comes from] the last action or from another action in the form of maintenance [of the āśrama] — hence not every rite has the attainment of <s>Brahmaloka</s> as its result.
Do not [object] thus.
Since it is heard [in scripture] that the attainment of <s>Brahmaloka</s> is the result of maintaining any rite — whether optional or obligatory — performed with dedication to the Lord (<s>Bhagavān</s>), the same result applies to the birth-sacrifice and the ancestral offering when performed in that manner.
Thus the <s>Bhagavadgītā</s> [states]: 'For one who performs action for the sake of sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>), the knot of action is dissolved.'

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 456)
children.translated_text: [page 456]

children.text:
yajñārthātkarmaṇo 'yatra lāko 'yaṃ karmabandhanaḥ'' /
iti tacca karma yajñārthatayā pratyekameva tatphalasamarthaṃ sambalanantu maṅgalavadupayujyate anyathā ekaprayogasya vyavadhānādasambhavaḥ paripālanantu kartavyamityeva kāraṇam /
taduktaṃ ``dadāmi deyamityeva yajñe yaṣṭavyamityahamiti /
children.translated_text:
'Other than action performed for the purpose of sacrifice, this world is bound by action.'
And that action, by virtue of being for the purpose of sacrifice, is individually capable of producing its result. The aggregation [of rites] is employed like an auspicious act (<s>maṅgala</s>); otherwise, the single performance [of all rites together] would be impossible due to interruption. And the maintenance [of the āśrama] is [performed] simply because it is obligatory — that is the reason.
As it has been said: 'I give because it is to be given; in sacrifice, [I sacrifice] because it is to be sacrificed — this is my [attitude].'

children.text:
yattu niṣiddhāsambandha eva samyaktvaṃ na tu vihitamātrānuṣṭhānamiti /
tanna /
yatkiñcinniṣiddhāsambandhasyābhāvāt sarvaniṣiddhāsambandhasya sarvatra sulabhatvāditi sampradāyaḥ /
children.translated_text:
As for [the view that] correctness (<s>samyaktva</s>) consists solely in the absence of connection with what is prohibited, and not in the mere performance of what is enjoined —
that is wrong.
Because the absence of connection with any particular prohibited [act] is [trivially present everywhere]; and the absence of connection with all prohibited [acts] is easily obtainable everywhere — this is the tradition (<s>sampradāya</s>).

children.text:
atra brūmaḥ /
bhagavaduddeśena kṛtaṃ kiñcideva karma sarvaṃ kāmyaṃ vā sarvaṃ nityaṃ vā sarvamiti vā nādyaḥ ekenaiva kāmyena nityena vā snānena tathā kṛtena tatphalasiddhau bahuvittādisādhye śrāddhādāvapravṛttyāpatteḥ /
nāparau aśakyatvāt /
na turyaḥ jāteṣṭyādernityatvābhāvāt /
tasmāt samyagagṛhasthāśramapālanasya tatphalaṃ samyaktantu sāmastyameva ato gayāśrāddhāderna brahmalokāvāptiḥ phalamiti sādhuktaṃ ``śāstradeśitaṃ phalaṃ anuṣṭhātarītyutsarga iti /
tacca phalaṃ kvacidvidhivākyaśrutaṃ kvaciccārthavādikamiti /
children.translated_text:
Here we state:
[When it says] 'action performed with dedication to the Lord' — [does this mean] some particular action, or all optional rites, or all obligatory rites, or everything? Not the first — because if the result were achieved by a single optional or obligatory [rite such as] bathing performed in that manner, there would be the undesirable consequence of non-engagement in rites like <s>śrāddha</s> etc. that require much wealth etc.
Not the second or third — because of impossibility.
Not the fourth — because rites like the birth-sacrifice (<s>jāteṣṭi</s>) etc. are not obligatory.
Therefore, the result belongs to the proper maintenance of the householder's stage of life; and 'proper' means the totality [of duties]. Hence, the attainment of <s>Brahmaloka</s> is not the result of [a single rite like] the <s>śrāddha</s> at <s>Gayā</s> etc. — as it has been well said: 'The result taught by scripture [goes] to the performer — this is the general principle.'
And that result is sometimes stated in the injunctive sentence itself, and sometimes in an explanatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>).

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 460)
children.translated_text: [page 460]

children.text: kāryānvitaśaktivādapūrvapakṣaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) of the doctrine of capacity-connected-with-obligation (<s>kāryānvitaśaktivāda</s>)

children.text:
nanvarthavādādīnāṃ siddhārthatayā na prāmāṇyam /
kāryanvita eva padānāṃ śakyavadhāraṇāt vṛddhavyavahārādeva sarveṣāmādyā vyutpattiḥ upāyāntarasya śabdavyutpattyadhīnatvāt /
tathā hi prayojakavākyoccāraṇānantaraṃ prayojyapravṛttimupalabhamāno bālaḥ prekṣāvadvākyoccāraṇasya prayojanajijñāsāyāṃ tadanvaya-vyatirekānuvidhāyitvādupasthitatvācca prayojyavṛddhapravṛttimeva prayojanamavadhārayati na cākiñcit kurvatastādarthyaṃ sambhavatīti tajjanyaṃ pravṛttyanukūlaṃ kāryatājñānameva kalpayati svapravṛttau ca tena kāryatājñānameva kalpayati svapravṛttau ca tena kāryatājñānasya hetutvāvadhāraṇāt nānyat pravṛtteḥ kāryatājñānāvaruddhatvāt /
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] Explanatory passages (<s>arthavāda</s>) etc., being about already-established matters, have no authoritative validity.
[This is because] the denotative capacity (<s>śakti</s>) of words is ascertained only as connected with obligation (<s>kāryānvita</s>); and the initial convention (<s>vyutpatti</s>) of all [words] is from the usage of elders (<s>vṛddhavyavahāra</s>) alone, because other means [of learning language] are dependent on prior knowledge of words.
Thus: a child, observing the activity of the person prompted [to act] after the utterance of a sentence by a purposeful speaker, and inquiring into the purpose of the purposeful person's utterance — since [the prompted activity] conforms to the presence and absence of that [utterance] and since [it is] presented [to the child's awareness] — determines the prompted elder's activity alone as the purpose [of the utterance]. And since nothing is purposeful without producing some [result], [the child] postulates an obligation-knowledge (<s>kāryatājñāna</s>) produced by that [utterance], which is favorable to the [prompted person's] activity. And since in his own activity [the child] ascertains that obligation-knowledge is the cause, [he concludes that] there is nothing other [than obligation-knowledge as the cause], because activity is invariably accompanied by obligation-knowledge.

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 465)
children.translated_text: [page 465]

children.text:
na caivaṃ śabdasya jñānadvārā pravṛttihetutvaṃ svapravṛttau bālena śabdāhitaviśeṣasya kāryatājñānasya hetutvenānavadhāraṇāt /
jñāne ca pratyakṣādinānopāyakatvadarśanāt śabdāpi kāryatājñānaheturityavadhārya tatraiva śaktiṃ kalpayati upasthitatvāt paścādāvāpoddhāreṇa kriyākārakapadānāṃ kāryānvitatattadartheṣu śaktiṃ gṛhṇāti prathamagrahītasāmānyaśaktyanurodhāt /
syādetat yadyapi vṛddhavyavahārādādau kāryānvitadhīranumitā tathāpyanvitamātraśaktyaiva kāryatāvācakapadasamabhivyāhārādākāṅkṣādimahimnā kāryānvitadhīsambhavāt na kāryāṃśe 'pi śaktiḥ paramparayāpi śabdasya kāryānvitajñānānukūlatvādarthāpattau anyathopapattirapi /
avaśyañcākāṅkṣādeḥ kāraṇatvaṃ kāryāṃśe śaktāvapi tadvyatirekādanvitābhidhānavyatirekaniyamāt /
children.translated_text:
Nor [should it be objected that] in this way, the word's being a cause of activity through knowledge [is established] — [this does not hold] because the child, in his own activity, does not ascertain the specific obligation-knowledge deposited by the word as the cause.
And since perception and other [means of knowledge] are seen not to be the instrumental cause of [obligation-]knowledge, [the child] determines that words too are a cause of obligation-knowledge, and postulates a [denotative] capacity [of words] for that very [obligation-knowledge], because [this explanation] is readily available. Afterwards, through the method of extraction and abstraction (<s>āvāpoddhāra</s>), [the child] grasps the capacity of action-words and case-words (<s>kriyākārakapada</s>) in their respective meanings as connected with obligation — in conformity with the general capacity initially grasped.
[Objection:] It may be said that even though the obligation-connected cognition is initially inferred from the usage of elders, the cognition connected with obligation is possible through the capacity to [denote] mere connection (<s>anvitamātra</s>) alone, through the force of expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>) etc. arising from co-utterance with an obligation-expressing word. Hence there is no [need for a separate] capacity in the obligation-aspect. And there is also an alternative explanation [available] through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), since the word is also indirectly conducive to obligation-connected knowledge.
But expectancy etc. must necessarily be causal — [yet] even when there is capacity in the obligation-aspect, [verbal cognition] is absent in the absence of that [expectancy], because of the rule that connected denotation (<s>anvitābhidhāna</s>) is absent without it.

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 468)
children.translated_text: [page 468]

children.text:
sati cākāṅkṣādau kāryavyatirekadarśanādanvitābhidhānavyatiriko na kvāpyasti /
anyathā gavādipadānāṃ vyaktāveva śaktiḥ syāt saṃskārādeva vyaktilābhadarśanānna tatheti yadi tadā kāryavācakapadādeva kāryānvitalābha iti kiṃ śaktyā vṛddhavyavahāre niyamataḥ kāryānvitajñānaṃ tatra dṛṣṭamiti tatra śaktikalpane vṛddhavyavahāre śabdopasthāpitenaivānvayabodhadarśanācchabdasannidherevānvayabodhahetutva kalpane dvāramityādau śabda evādhyāhriyate /
kvacidasampūrṇavākye vṛddhavyavahārādādyavyutpatteḥ śabdasannirvyabhicaratīti cet tarhi siddhārthe 'pyanvayapratītidarśanāt kāryatvamapi vyabhicāri /
na ca tatra lakṣaṇā bādhakābhāvāt /
śaktiklapanābhiyā hyanyatra lakṣaṇānumatā iha tu laghīyasyā ubhayasādharaṇāpadārthamātraśaktyā mukhyasyaivocitatvāt /
kiñca kāryavāciliṅgādīnāṃ ākāṅkṣādyupetapādarthānvitasvārthabodhakatvamavaśyaṃ vācyamato viśeṣāt padāntarāṇāmapi tathātvamastu lāghavāditi /
maivaṃ /
vyavahārahetutayānumite hi kāryānvitajñāne 'nvaya -vyatirekābhyāṃ śabdasya sākṣātkāraṇatvavadhārayati na paramparayā sākṣāttvasyautsirgikatvena tatsambhave paramparayā anyāyyatvāditi tatraiva śaktiṃ kalpayati nānvitajñāne padārthajñāne vā apravartakatayā pravṛttyā svakāraṇatvena tayoranupasthāpanāt /
na cānvitajñānaśaktāvapi paramparayā kāryatvadhīḥ sambhavatītyarthāpattyā saiva kalpyatāṃ lāghavāt na tu viśiṣṭajñāne śaktiranyalabhyatvāt iti vācyam /
arthāpatteḥ sākṣādupapādakamātraviṣayatvena nyūnādhikāgrāhakatvāt sākṣādupapādakakāryanvitajñāne śaktiḥ kalpyate liṅgādīnāṃ śakteralpanāt anyalabhyatvatarkasyāpyabhāvāt vā ādyavyutpattervicāryatvāt /
kiñca pravṛttikāraṇatayopasthitaṃ kāryanvitajñānamapahāyānupasthitānvitajñānamātre śaktikalpanamayuktaṃ hetvabhāvādupasthityantare ca gauravāt /
atha kāryanvitajñānopasthitāvapyanvitajñānamapyupasthitamiti lāghavāt kāryāṃśamapahāyānvite śaktirgṛhyatāmiti cet na jñāne hi padānāṃ śaktiḥ śakyatvānnārtheṣu anyacca kāryānvitajñānaṃ anyadevānvitajñānaṃ viṣayabhedena jñānabhedāt /
taduktamabhāvavāde anyadbhūtalajñānamanyacca ghaṭavadbhūtalajñānamiti anvitajñānamupasthāpya tatra śaktigraha iti gauravameva /
gaghuni śakye sambhavatyanyalabhyaṃ guru na tatheti cet na yugapadupasthitau tathātvāt /
na ca tasyāpyanupasthitiḥ puruṣaviśeṣadoṣāt sarvairevādyavyutpattau tathānavagamāt /
tathāpi na kāryānvite śaktiḥ kāryavāciliṅgādīnāṃ vyabhicārāditi cet na sarvapadānāṃ kāryatvaviśiṣṭadhījanakatvāt /
tacca kāryānvitasvārthāpratipādakatayetarānvitasvārthakāryapratipādakatayā veti /
evañca kāryānvitavyutpattau satyāmanākāṅkṣādau vyabhicārādākāṅkṣāderupādhitvam /
tathācopajīvyaprathamabhāvikāryānvitavyutpattyanurodhena vidhyaśrutāvapi kāryadhyāhāraḥ kvacillakṣaṇā kvacidasaṃsargāgraha iti siddhārthe 'nvayapratītidarśanāduttarakālamanvitamātre śaktireva kalpyatāṃ prācīnakāryānvitajñānaṃ bādhyatāmityapyata eva nirastam /
pūrvakalpanātaḥ kalpanāntaraprasaṅgāt uttarakālabhāvisiddhārthaprayogasya lakṣaṇādibhirapyupapatteḥ ananyathāsiddhatvābhāvena prācīnajñānābādhakatvāt upajīvyavyāghātācca /
atha siddhārthe 'pi vyutpattiḥ tathāhi upalabdhacaitraputrajanmā bālastādṛśenaiva vārtāhāreṇa samaṃ caitrasamīpaṃ gataścaiva putraste jāta iti vārtāhāravākyaṃ śṛṇvan caitrasya mukhaprasādaṃ gṛhṇan śroturharṣamanuminoti hārṣācca tatkāraṇaṃ putrajanmajñānaṃ kalpayati upasthitvādupapādakatvāda nyopasthitau gauravācca tatra vākyasya kāraṇatāṃ kalpayati lāghavāditi cet na harṣahetūnāṃ bahūnāṃ sambhavāt harṣeṇa liṅgena putrajanmajñānasya bālenānumātumaśakyatvāt priyāntarajñānasya pariśeṣayitumaśakyatvācca /
atha putrajanmajñānāvyabhicārivṛddhināddhādikriyāviśeṣadarśanāt putrajanmajñānānumānamiti cet tarhi putraste jāta iti vākyaṃ tat kriyākartavyaparameveti kāryānvitajñānajanakatvameva tasya prathamato gṛhyate uttarakālaṃ putrajanmajñānānumānamiti na vyutpattiḥ kāryaṃ jahāti yatrāpīha sahakāratarau madhuraṃ piko rautīti prasiddhārthapadasamānādhikaraṇyādibhirvyutpattistatrāpi vyavahāradhīnyutpattipūrvikā kāryānvita eva yuktā pikapadaśaktiḥ pūrvaṃ nāvadhṛteti cet na tatra pikamānayetyādau kasyacit kāryānvita eva vyutpatteḥ upajīvyajātītayā ca tasyā balavattvaṃ kiñcedamapi kāryānvitajñānaśaktaṃ padatvāditi sāmānyato 'vagataṃ svārthāviśeṣaḥ paraṃ nādhigataḥ sa idānīṃ suhṛdupadeśādibhiravagamyate /
ataḥ siddhaṃ pravṛttiparāṇāṃ śabdānāṃ pravartakajñānajanakatvaṃ tacca kvacit sākṣāt kāryānvayāt kvacit paramparayā kāryānvayāt ata eva vidhiśeṣībhūtārthavādānāṃ
children.translated_text:
And when expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>) and the like are present, since separation from being-an-effect (<s>kārya</s>) is not observed, there is nowhere a separation from <s>anvitābhidhāna</s> (connected denotation) [either].
Otherwise, the denotative power of words like 'cow' and the like would reside in the individual (<s>vyakti</s>) alone, since the apprehension of the individual is observed from the impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) alone; if [it is said] it is not so, then [we ask:] since the apprehension of the connection with being-an-effect is obtained from the very word denoting the effect, what need is there for [postulating] denotative power? [Reply:] Because in the usage of the learned (<s>vṛddhavyavahāra</s>), knowledge connected with being-an-effect is invariably observed, the denotative power is postulated there; and since in the usage of the learned, the cognition of connection is observed as produced by what is presented by the word alone, when the causality of the mere proximity of the word for producing the cognition of connection is postulated, in [expressions like] 'door' and the like, a word itself is supplied.
If [it is said that] in some [cases of] incomplete sentences, since the initial conventional learning (<s>ādyavyutpatti</s>) is from the usage of the learned, [one observes] invariable concomitance with the word — then, since the cognition of connection is observed even in the case of an established [non-effectual] meaning, being-an-effect too would deviate.
Nor is there figurative usage (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) there, due to the absence of an invalidating cognition.
For figurative usage is permitted elsewhere only out of reluctance to postulate [a new] denotative power; but here, since the primary [meaning] alone is appropriate through the lighter [postulation of] denotative power in mere word-meaning common to both [cases], [figurative usage is not needed].
Furthermore, since it must be stated that <s>liṅ</s> and other effect-denoting [suffixes] generate cognition of their own meaning connected with the word-meanings possessing expectancy and the like, by the particular [nature of these suffixes], let other words too have the same [capacity], due to simplicity.
Do not [say] so.
For when the knowledge connected with being-an-effect is inferred as the cause of behavior (<s>vyavahāra</s>), one determines through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>) the direct causality of the word for that [knowledge], not indirect causality — since directness is the default (<s>autsargika</s>), and when direct [causality] is possible, indirect [causality] is improper. Therefore, the denotative power is postulated precisely in that [knowledge connected with being-an-effect], not in mere connected knowledge or in word-meaning knowledge, since [the latter two] do not impel [action] and are not presented by activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) as its own causes.
Nor should it be said: even if the denotative power resides in connected knowledge, the cognition of being-an-effect is possible indirectly through presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>), so let that alone be postulated due to simplicity, and there is no [need for] denotative power in qualified knowledge since [connected knowledge] is obtainable otherwise —
because presumption, having as its scope only what directly justifies [the observed fact], does not apprehend more or less [than that]; hence the denotative power is postulated in the knowledge connected with being-an-effect, which is the direct justification, and because the postulation of denotative power for <s>liṅ</s> and other [suffixes separately] would be minimal, or because the reasoning from unobtainability-otherwise is also absent, or because the initial conventional learning is under examination.
Furthermore, it is improper to set aside the knowledge connected with being-an-effect, which is presented as the cause of activity, and postulate denotative power in mere connected knowledge, which is not presented — due to the absence of a reason and due to the cumbersomeness of [postulating] another form of presentation.
If [it is said:] when the knowledge connected with being-an-effect is presented, connected knowledge too is presented, so due to simplicity, setting aside the effect-component, let the denotative power be grasped in the connected [meaning alone] — no, for the denotative power of words resides in cognition, because [words] are capable [of producing cognition], not in objects; and the knowledge connected with being-an-effect is one thing, while mere connected knowledge is quite another, since cognitions differ when objects differ.
As stated in the section on absence (<s>abhāvavāda</s>): 'the knowledge of the ground is one thing, and the knowledge of the ground with a pot is another.' [Thus,] presenting connected knowledge [separately] and grasping the denotative power therein would be cumbersome indeed.
If [it is said:] when the lighter [alternative] is possible with respect to what is denotable, the heavier [alternative] that is obtainable otherwise is not [adopted] — no, because when both are presented simultaneously, the same [objection] applies.
Nor is there non-presentation [of the effect-connected knowledge] due to a defect of a particular person, since not everyone [similarly fails to] understand it at the stage of initial conventional learning.
If [it is said:] even so, the denotative power does not reside in [knowledge] connected with being-an-effect, due to deviation in <s>liṅ</s> and other effect-denoting [suffixes] — no, because all words generate cognition qualified by being-an-effect.
And that [qualification obtains] either because [the word] generates cognition of its own meaning connected with being-an-effect, or because [the word] generates cognition of [its own meaning connected with] the being-an-effect of [another's] own meaning connected [with it].
Thus, when conventional learning connected with being-an-effect obtains, since there is deviation in the absence of expectancy and the like, expectancy and the like serve as limiting conditions (<s>upādhi</s>).
And thus, in accordance with the prior and primary conventional learning connected with being-an-effect, which is presupposed [by all subsequent usage], even when there is no Vedic injunction heard, being-an-effect is supplied [by ellipsis]; in some cases figurative usage [applies]; in some cases there is non-apprehension of connection. [Objection:] Since the cognition of connection is observed even in established [non-effectual] meanings, at a later time let the denotative power be postulated in mere connection, and let the prior knowledge connected with being-an-effect be overridden — this too is refuted for the same reason,
since from a prior postulation there would be the unwanted consequence of yet another postulation; since the later-occurring usage with established meanings can be accounted for through figurative usage and the like; since [the later observation] does not invalidate the prior knowledge due to the absence of impossibility-of-being-otherwise; and since it would contradict what is presupposed.
If [it is said:] there is conventional learning even in established [meanings] — the explanation is as follows: a boy who has learned of the birth of <s>Caitra</s>'s son, going to <s>Caitra</s>'s presence together with the very news-bearer, hearing the news-bearer's sentence 'a son has been born to you,' observing the joy on <s>Caitra</s>'s face, infers the hearer's delight, and from the delight postulates its cause — the knowledge of the son's birth — due to its being presented, due to its being a justification, due to the cumbersomeness of [postulating] anything else not presented, and postulates the causality of the sentence for that [knowledge] due to simplicity. [Reply:] No, because since there are many possible causes of delight, the boy cannot infer the knowledge of the son's birth by the inferential mark of delight, and cannot eliminate [other possibilities like] knowledge of some other pleasing thing through the method of residues.
If [it is said:] the knowledge of the son's birth is inferred from observing the specific actions like rejoicing, giving gifts, and the like, which are invariably concomitant with the knowledge of the son's birth — then, the sentence 'a son has been born to you' is understood as having those actions as its purpose, and thus its capacity to generate knowledge connected with being-an-effect is what is grasped first; the inference of the knowledge of the son's birth [comes] later — hence the conventional learning does not abandon being-an-effect. Even in [the case of] 'on this tree full of supporting branches, the cuckoo sings sweetly,' where conventional learning [for the word 'cuckoo'] occurs through co-referentiality with words of established meaning and the like, even there the conventional learning that is preceded by behavioral cognition (<s>vyavahāradhī</s>) is properly [a learning of denotative power] in what is connected with being-an-effect alone. If [it is said:] the denotative power of the word <s>pika</s> (cuckoo) was not ascertained earlier — no, because in [expressions like] 'bring the cuckoo' (<s>pikamānaya</s>) and the like, someone's conventional learning is in what is connected with being-an-effect alone; and since that [prior learning] belongs to a presupposed class, it is stronger. Moreover, [the learner thinks:] 'this [word] too has denotative power in what is connected with being-an-effect, because it is a word' — thus [it is] known in general; the specific own-meaning alone has not been ascertained; that is now ascertained through the instruction of a friend and the like.
Therefore, it is established that words oriented toward activity (<s>pravṛttiparāṇāṃ śabdānām</s>) have the capacity to generate impelling knowledge (<s>pravartakajñāna</s>), and that [capacity operates] sometimes directly through connection with being-an-effect, and sometimes indirectly through connection with being-an-effect. For this very reason, <s>arthavādas</s> (explanatory passages) that are subsidiary to injunctions

children.text:
svargādipadaśaktigrāhakāṇāñca pravṛttiparatvena paramparayā kāryānvayāt kāryānvitasvārthābodhakatvamiti /
yatra purāṇa-bhāratādi pāṭhe phalaśrutirasti tatrārthavādakalpitavidhiśeṣībhūtatvena pravṛttiparatvameva teṣāmatiparamparayā kāryānvitasvārthabodhakatvaṃ svarūpākhyānaparāṇāntu kāvya-nāṭakādīnāṃ padārthāsaṃsargāgraheṇa saṃsargavyavahāro na saṃsargagraha iti /
children.translated_text:
and words like 'heaven' (<s>svarga</s>) and the like that serve as apprehenders of the denotative power — [all of these] generate cognition of their own meaning connected with being-an-effect, through indirect connection with being-an-effect by virtue of being oriented toward activity.
Wherever in <s>Purāṇas</s>, the <s>Mahābhārata</s>, and the like, a statement of result (<s>phalaśruti</s>) accompanies the recitation, there [those texts] are oriented toward activity by virtue of being subsidiary to injunctions postulated by <s>arthavāda</s>, and generate cognition of their own meaning connected with being-an-effect, though very indirectly. But for <s>kāvya</s> (poetry), <s>nāṭaka</s> (drama), and the like, which are oriented toward narrating their own form, the behavior regarding connection [of word-meanings] arises from non-apprehension of the connection of word-meanings [with being-an-effect] — not from the apprehension of connection.
