children.translated_text: [page 565]

children.text:
nanu jātiṃ vinā pratyakṣādinā vyaktijñānādanyaiva vyaktidhīsāmagrī jātiviśiṣṭajñānañcobhayajñāpakasāmagrīdvayasamājādārthaṃ /
ata eva vyaktiṃ vinā jātesmaraṇena jātismaraṇasya vyaktiviṣayatvaniyamāt jātijñāpakamātrameva vyaktijñāpakaṃ kalpyate sāmānyakalpanāyāṃ bādhakābhāvāditi parāstam /
jātiṃ vināpi vyaktismaraṇāttatrānyaiva sāmagrī cātiviśiṣṭasmaraṇañcobhayāṃśasmārakasamājāditi /
atra brūmaḥ / jāti-vyaktipratyakṣādibodhe tathaiva sāmagrīdvayasya pṛthaganvaya-vyatirekagrahācchābde tu vyaktibodhe jātiśaktijñānameva heturlāghavāt na sāmagṣantaraṃ tatsattve tena vinā vilambābhāvāt /
evañca jātiśaktatvena jñātaṃ padaṃ jātiviśiṣṭasya smārakamanubhāvakañca / nanu jñāne śaktiḥ śakyatvāt tathāca yasya jñāne śaktistacchakyaṃ jāti-vyaktijñāne ca śaktiriti jātivadvyaktirapi śakyeti cet na yadviṣayatayā hi jñātā jñāne śaktirupayujyate tat śaktijñāne viṣayatayā śakyatāvacchedakaṃ śakyaṃ jātijñānañca tatheti jātireva śakyā na tu vyaktijñānatvamapyacchedakaṃ gauravāt /
na ca śakyajñāne niyataviṣayatvameva śakyatvaṃ vyavahārānumita śakyānubhavaviṣayāṇāmanvaye tatsambandhimiti-mātṛṇāmapi śakyatāpatteḥ evañca jāti-vyaktijñānajanakakatvādubhayatrāpi śabdaśaktiḥ /
jātyaṃśe sa jñātā vyaktyaṃśe svarūpasato heturlāghavāditi kubjaśaktivādaḥ /
evañca saiva tadaiva tenaiva jñātā ajñātā ca vācikā avācikāvetyatra jātivyakyavacchedakabhedenāvirodhaḥ tvayāpyanvaye kubjaśaktisvīkārāt /
vyakteḥ śakyatve 'pi jñātaśaktiśabdajanitajñānaviṣayatvalakṣaṇaṃ vācyatvaṃ nāsti /
na caivaṃ paribhāṣā śabdajanyajñānaviṣayatvena vācyatve lākṣaṇikāderapi vācyatvāpatteḥ vyakteḥ śakyatve 'pi vyaktiśaktijñānaṃ na kāraṇaṃ vyaktiśaktijñānatvaṃ nāvacchedakamiti lāghavam /
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] Without the universal, through perception etc. there is a separate aggregate of conditions (<s>sāmagrī</s>) for the cognition of the individual; and the cognition qualified by the universal is a single entity arising from the conjunction of the two aggregates — the one that makes known the individual and the one that makes known the universal.
Precisely for this reason, without the individual, by merely recollecting the universal — since the recollection of the universal is necessarily restricted to having an individual as its content — whatever merely makes known the universal is postulated as also making known the individual. Because there is no sublating cognition against postulating the universal. [Reply:] This is set aside.
Even without the universal, from the recollection of the individual, there is another aggregate of conditions there [for individual-cognition]; and the recollection qualified by the universal is from the conjunction of the two sets of recollection-causes for both aspects.
Here we state: in the perceptual etc. cognition of universal and individual, two separate aggregates of conditions are grasped through separate agreement and difference. But in verbal cognition, the knowledge of the capacity for the universal alone is the cause of the cognition of the individual — because of parsimony — not another aggregate; because when [the knowledge of] capacity for the universal is present, there is no delay [in individual-cognition] without it.
Thus, the word known as having a capacity for the universal is a recollection-evoker and producer [of cognition] of [the entity] qualified by the universal. [Objection:] The capacity exists in the cognition, because [cognitiion] is the denotable. And thus, that in whose cognition the capacity exists is the denotable. And since the capacity exists in the cognition of both the universal and the individual, the individual too, like the universal, is the denotable. [Reply:] No — for the capacity that is known as having [something] as its content in the cognition is utilized [in verbal comprehension]; and that which, as a content-feature, is the delimiting condition of denotability in the cognition of capacity — is the denotable. And the cognition of the universal is such [a content]; hence the universal alone is the denotable, not the cognition of the individual as also a delimiting condition — because of prolixity.
Nor [should it be said] that denotability consists in being a necessary content of the cognition produced by the denotable — because then, from the agreement [that others who hear the word also cognize the object], even the mothers etc. [of the person] would have the status of denotable. And thus, since the word's capacity generates both the universal-cognition and the individual-cognition, the word's capacity is [present] in both.
[In the universal-aspect] it is known [as a capacity]; in the individual-aspect, it is a cause that is inherently present [but not known as capacity] — because of parsimony. This is the 'hunchback-capacity' doctrine (<s>kubjaśaktivāda</s>).
Thus, the same [capacity], at the same time, by the same [person], is both known and unknown, both expressive and non-expressive — there is no contradiction here, due to the difference of delimiting conditions (universal vs. individual). Even you [must accept] a hunchback-capacity in the [account of verbal] connection.
Even if the individual is the denotable, denotation (<s>vācyatva</s>) — defined as being the content of a cognition produced by a word whose capacity is known — does not apply [to the individual].
Nor is [denotation to be defined by] the rule [that] denotation consists in being the content of a word-produced cognition — because then even the secondarily signified (<s>lākṣaṇika</s>) etc. would have the status of denotable. Even if the individual is the denotable, the knowledge of the individual's capacity is not a cause [of verbal cognition], and the property of being-knowledge-of-the-individual's-capacity is not a delimiting condition — this is the parsimony.

children.text:
yattu tacchaktatvena jñātādeva tadarthabodhaḥ śaktibhramādapi dhīdarśanāt /
tathā yogyatādyanvayānupapattī vinā padādupasthitiḥ śaktisādhyeti vyaktirapi śakyeti /
tanna /
anyalabhye śakterakalpanāt anyathā tavānvaye 'pi śaktirlakṣaṇādyucchedaśca /
nanu na jātirarthaḥ; vyavahārābhāvena vyutpatterasiddheḥ kārakoparaktakriyā hi vyavahāragocaraḥ jatiśca na kriyā nityatvāt kārakaṃ na kartrādi kriyāyāstatrāsamavāyāt parasamavetakriyāphalabhāgitvābhāvāt kartṛtvavyāpārānāśrayatvāt acetanatvāt tayā saha vibhāgābhāvāt kriyānādhāratvācceti cet na vyaktivyavahārādeva uktanyāyena jātau śaktigrahāt jātisavikalpakādyavyāvṛttatayā jñātāyāṃ vyaktau kriyānvayaḥ savikalpakañcālocanadvārā jātijanyamiti paramparayā jāterapi kārakatvenānvayaḥ /
yadvā na kevalavyakteḥ kārakatvaṃ na hi gaurgacchatītyatra vyaktimātraṃ yātīti kasyacitpratītiḥ kintu jātiviśiṣṭāyāḥ tathācobhayamapi kārakam /
children.translated_text:
As for [the view] that the cognition of the meaning [of a word] arises from that [word] known as having denotative power (<s>śaktatva</s>), since cognition is observed even from an erroneous [attribution of] denotative power (<s>śaktibhrama</s>);
and that the presentation from a word, without [the conditions of] fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>) and the like being untenable for connection, is accomplished through denotative power — therefore the individual (<s>vyakti</s>) too is denotable —
that is wrong,
because denotative power is not postulated for what is obtainable otherwise; [and] otherwise, even on your [view], there would be denotative power in the connection [aspect] too, and the elimination of figurative usage (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) and the like [would follow].
[Objection:] The universal (<s>jāti</s>) is not the [word-]meaning, since the conventional learning (<s>vyutpatti</s>) is not established due to the absence of behavior [toward the universal]; for the object of behavior is action colored by a case-relation (<s>kāraka</s>); and the universal is not an action, due to its eternality; nor is it an agent (<s>kartṛ</s>) or the like [i.e., a case-relation], since the action does not inhere in it; because it does not share in the result of the action inhering in another; because it is not the locus of the operation of agenthood (<s>kartṛtvavyāpāra</s>); because it is unconscious (<s>acetana</s>); because there is no separation (<s>vibhāga</s>) of it [from the individual]; and because it is not the substratum of action. [Reply:] No, because by the principle stated above, the grasping of denotative power in the universal [occurs] from the behavior toward the individual itself. The connection with action is [established] for the individual known as undifferentiated from the universal [as grasped through] determinate cognition (<s>savikalpaka</s>) and the like; and determinate cognition is produced by the universal through the medium of perception (<s>ālocana</s>) — thus, even the universal has connection [with action] through case-relation-hood, indirectly.
Alternatively, case-relation-hood does not belong to the individual alone; for in 'the cow goes' (<s>gaur gacchati</s>), no one has the cognition that the mere individual goes, but rather the [individual] qualified by the universal; and thus both are case-relations.

children.text: śrīkarastu kevalajāti-vyakteyarakāratvāt kriyānvayovyakterāśrayatayā jāteravacchedakatayā āruṇyādivat evañca jātiśaktapadāt jāteranubhavaḥ śābdovyakteraupādānikaḥ aśakyatvāditi /
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīkara</s>, however, [holds that] since neither the universal nor the individual alone has case-relation-hood, the connection with action belongs to the individual as the substratum and to the universal as the delimitor (<s>avacchedaka</s>), like redness (<s>āruṇya</s>) and the like. Thus, from a word whose denotative power resides in the universal, the verbal cognition (<s>śābda</s>) is of the universal, while [the cognition] of the individual is incidental (<s>aupādānika</s>), since [the individual] is not denotable.

children.text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 470)
children.translated_text: (Bibl. Ind. 98, IV,2, p. 470)

children.text:
anye tu jātiśaktameva padaṃ-jāti-vyaktyoḥ smārakamanubhāvakañceti vyakterapi śābdatvam / na ca vṛttiṃ vinā anvayānubhave 'praveśānna vyakteḥ śābdatvaṃ vṛttiṃ vināpi ekavittivedyatvaniyamena jātiśaktādeva vyakteranubhāvāt anyathā jātyanvayo 'pi na syāt vyaktiṃ vinā jāterananubhavāt /
ata eva jātiśaktireva vyaktiṃ bodhayatīti guravaḥ /
kiñca śakyopasthāpitasyānvayānubhavaṃ prati padānāṃ kāraṇatvaṃ ato jātivadupasthāpitāyā vyakteranubhavaḥ padāt na tu tattacchaktoyapasthāpitasya gauravāt /
na caivamaśakyaparatve lakṣaṇā yathā hyanyata eva jñānānna śaktistathā lakṣaṇāpi na tat kimaśakye 'pi mukhyaḥ prayogaḥḥ satyaṃ śaktyā sākṣādupasthita eva tasya mukhyatvātsvaśaktyeti tvadhikam /
vastutastu jātiśaktādeva vyaktidhīsambhavānna vyaktau śaktiḥ /
yadi ca tato na taddhīstadā tatra śaktireva syāt anyathā taddhīrna syādeva /
nanu pada-jātibhyāmapyekojāti-vyaktyanubhavaḥ kriyate tatra jātyaṃśe padasya vyaktyaṃśe jāteranubhāvakatvamayameva upādānārthaṃ iti cet tarhi jāteḥ kāraṇatvāpekṣayā śaktijñāne upasthitavyakteravacchedakatvamātrakalpanaiva laghīyasī jāteḥ pramāṇāntaratvāpātaśca /
ata eva brīhīnavahantītyatra vyaktau na lakṣaṇā tatsādhyopasthiterjātiśaktita eva siddheḥ; /
astu vā gavāvacchedakatvenāruṇyādivadvrīhitve 'pyavaghātānvaya iti /
atrocyate /
gotvajñāne gojñāne vā śaktaṃ padamityākāraḥ /
śaktigrahaḥ tathāca śakyajñāne
children.translated_text:
Others, however, [hold that] the word has denotative power in the universal alone, but is both a reminder (<s>smāraka</s>) and a producer of experience (<s>anubhāvaka</s>) of both the universal and the individual — thus the individual too has verbal [cognition] status (<s>śābdatva</s>). Nor [should it be said that] since the individual does not enter [the scope of] the experience of connection without a semantic function (<s>vṛtti</s>), the individual does not have verbal [cognition] status — because even without a [separate] semantic function, the individual is cognized from the denotative power residing in the universal alone, through the rule of being cognizable in a single cognition (<s>ekavittivedyatvaniyama</s>); otherwise, even the connection of the universal [with action] would not [be established], since the universal cannot be cognized without the individual.
For this very reason, the teachers (<s>guravaḥ</s>) [hold that] the denotative power residing in the universal itself makes known the individual.
Furthermore, the causality of words is with respect to producing the experience of connection of what is presented through what is denotable; therefore, the experience of the individual, which is presented like the universal, [arises] from the word — not [the experience] of what is presented through denotative power in each respective [entity], due to cumbersomeness.
Nor is there figurative usage (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) in the orientation toward the non-denotable — just as from knowledge from another source there is no [postulation of] denotative power, similarly there is no figurative usage either. Then is there primary usage (<s>mukhya prayoga</s>) even for the non-denotable? Yes — what is directly presented through denotative power has primary status through its own denotative power; [in the case of the individual, this notion of] 'through its own denotative power' is [merely] additional [and unnecessary].
In reality, since the cognition of the individual is possible from the denotative power residing in the universal alone, there is no denotative power in the individual.
If the cognition of [the individual] did not arise from that [denotative power in the universal], then there would indeed be denotative power there [in the individual]; otherwise, the cognition of it would never arise at all.
[Objection:] By the word and the universal together, a single cognition of the universal-and-individual is produced; therein, the word is the producer of the universal-aspect and the universal is the producer of the individual-aspect — this is the purpose of [calling the individual-cognition] 'incidental' (<s>upādāna</s>). [Reply:] Then, in comparison to postulating causality for the universal, postulating merely the delimitor-hood of the individual presented in the cognition of the denotative power is simpler; and the universal would absurdly be another means of valid knowledge [separate from the word].
For this very reason, in 'they carry the rice-grains' (<s>brīhīn avahanti</s>), there is no figurative usage (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) with respect to the individual, since the presentation of [the individual] that is to be accomplished [through figurative usage] is already established from the denotative power residing in the universal alone.
Alternatively, let [the individual] have the status of delimitor for the threshing-connection, like redness (<s>āruṇya</s>) and the like, through the delimitor-hood of cow-hood (<s>gotvāvacchedakatva</s>); and similarly for rice-ness (<s>vrīhitva</s>) too.
Here it is replied:
The form [of the denotative power grasping] is: 'this word has denotative power in the cognition of cow-hood or in the cognition of a cow.'
The grasping of denotative power is thus; and in the cognition of the denotable,

children.text:
viṣayatayā jāteravacchedakatvaṃ vyaktimādāyaiva pratīyate na kevalāyāḥ vyaktiṃ vinā jāterapratīteḥ tathāca jāteravacchedakatve nāgṛhītaviśeṣaṇānyāyena vyakteravacchedakatvaṃ vajralepāyitamiti śaktijñāne viṣayatayā avacchedakatvāt jātivatsāpi śakyā tasmāt pariharaikavittivedyatvaniyamaṃ svīkuru vā vyaktervācyatvam /
api ca yaddharmavattayā jñāta eva yatra yasya jñānaṃ sa tatrāvacchedakaḥ vyaktijñānanatvena jñāta eva tatra jñāne śaktidhīriti vyaktirapi śakyā /
nanvādyavutpattau miti-mātṛviṣayatvena jñāta eva jñāne pravartakatvaṃ jñātaṃ na ca tayorjñānaṃ pravartakamato vyabhicāraḥ anyathā pravartakatvena miti-mātṛjñānamapi prayojyasyānumāya bālastatrāpi śaktiṃ gṛhṇīyāt evaṃ tavāpi kāryānvitajñāna eva śaktiḥ syāt tattvena jñāta eva jñāne śaktigrahāditi cet miti-mātṛjñānatvaṃ kāryānvitajñānatvañca vināpi pravartakajñāne ghaṭajñānatvādikaṃ jñātuṃ śakyamiti tayornāvacchedakatvaṃ kintu ghaṭajñānatvādikameva lāghavāt tayorapi tata eva prāpteśca /
kiñca padaṃ vyaktijñānārtha śakyajñāne viṣayatayā vyakteravacchedakatvamātraṃ kalpayati lāghavāt jātiviṣayatvavadvyaktiviṣayatvasya jñānavittivedyatvenāvaśyaṃ śīghropasthitatvāt na tu jātiśaktistadbodhe kāraṇāntaraṃ vā tadavacchedakaṃ gauravācchaktigrahakakāle kalpanīyopasthitikatvācca /
children.translated_text:
the delimitor-hood of the universal is cognized by way of being the object [of the cognition], [but] only together with the individual — not of [the universal] alone, since the universal cannot be cognized without the individual. And thus, in the delimitor-hood of the universal, by the principle that 'the delimitor-hood of an unapprehended qualifier is firmly established' (<s>agṛhītaviśeṣaṇānyāya</s>), the delimitor-hood of the individual is as firmly established as adamantine paste (<s>vajralepa</s>). Therefore, since [the individual] has delimitor-hood by way of being the object in the cognition of the denotative power, it too, like the universal, is denotable. Hence, either give up the rule of being cognizable in a single cognition, or accept the denotability of the individual.
Moreover, that by virtue of possessing which property something is known, and in whose cognition there is knowledge of something — that [property] is the delimitor of that [knowledge] therein. In cognition known as being knowledge of the individual, there is the cognition of the denotative power — therefore the individual too is denotable.
[Objection:] In the initial conventional learning, the causality [of the word] for cognition is known insofar as [the word] is known as having the cognition (<s>miti</s>) and the cognizer (<s>mātṛ</s>) as its objects; but the knowledge of those two [cognition and cognizer] is not the impeller [of behavior]; therefore there is deviation. Otherwise, [the learner] would infer by [the property of] impelling that the knowledge of cognition and cognizer [is also the cause], and the child would grasp the denotative power even therein. Similarly, on your view too, the denotative power would reside in the knowledge connected with being-an-effect alone, since the grasping of denotative power occurs in the cognition known as such. [Reply:] The properties of being knowledge-of-cognition-and-cognizer and of being knowledge-connected-with-being-an-effect — even without [knowing] these, in impelling knowledge, the property of being knowledge-of-a-pot and the like can be known; hence those [properties] do not have delimitor-hood, but rather the property of being knowledge-of-a-pot and the like alone [has delimitor-hood], due to simplicity, and because those [other properties] too are obtainable from that very [simpler property].
Furthermore, the word, [being] for the purpose of individual-cognition, postulates merely the delimitor-hood of the individual by way of being the object in the cognition of the denotable, due to simplicity — since the individual-objecthood [of the cognition], like the universal-objecthood, is necessarily and quickly presented [to awareness] by virtue of being cognizable as a property of the cognition. But neither the denotative power residing in the universal nor another cause is [to be postulated as] its delimitor for producing that cognition, due to cumbersomeness and because [such an entity] would need to be postulated as presented at the time of grasping the denotative power.

children.text:
anye tu prathamaṃ vyavahārānumitavyaktijñāne śabdānuvidhānāt padaṃ śaktamityavadhārayati na tu jātijñāne vyavahārājanakatve na tadā tasyānupasthiteḥ paścādvyaktervyāvṛttyarthaṃ anugamārthañca jātirapi tadviṣaya iti mānāntareṇa jñātvā jātijñāne 'pi tatpadasya kāraṇatāṃ pratyeti tathāca vyaktiśaktijñānamapi kāraṇaṃ na tu jātiśaktijñānenānyathāsiddhiḥ vyaktijñānakāraṇatāṃ upajīvya jātijñāne kāraṇatāgraha ityupajīvyavirodhāt /
etena jātirapi śakyā lāghavāt śaktigrahajanyasaṃskārasya vyaktiviṣayatvaniyamena padāt jātismaraṇamutpādyamānamavaśyaṃ vyaktiviṣayaṃ saṃskārasyāniyatodbokadhatve 'pi jātyaṃśodbodhakādeva vyaktaṃśodbodhaniyamakalpanā yathā padenodbuddhasaṃskārādeva niyatā śaktismṛtiḥ padaṃ vināpi sa sarvā jātismṛtirvyaktiviṣayā anyathā kevalajātimātrasmaraṇāpatteḥ /
saṃskārasahitāt padādeva jātiviśiṣṭānubhavo 'pīndriyadiva pratyabhijñā /
ata eva bhāṣyaṃ saṃskāra-śabdaśaktibhyāṃ viśiṣṭānubhavaityunnītamatamapāsta uktanyāyairjātivadvyakterapi śakyatvāt viśiṣṭanāmānantye 'pi ekatra viśiṣṭe tattvaṃ vihāya gotvamādāya gotvaviśiṣṭaṃ śakyamita śaktigrahaḥ yathā ca kvacideva dhūme dhūmovahnivyāpya iti buddhiḥ yathā va tathaiva kāryāṇāmānantye 'pi kvacit kārye tattvaṃ taṭasthīkṛtya kṛtimādāya dharmiṇi kāryaṃ śakyamiti liṅāderapūrvaṃ śaktigrahaḥ avacchedakaikyācchakterekatvaṃ tadvadeva yathā vā vyaktivācakapaśvādipadānāṃ atha vā gotvena sāmānyalakṣaṇayā jñāte sarvatra gavi gotvamādāya śaktigrahaḥ prameyatvena ca sarvajñāne sārvajñamiṣyata eva neṣyate tu ghaṭatvādi sarvaprakārakajñānavattvena sarvaikodasīnagoḥ śakyatvād yatkiñcidekopādāne 'nadhyavasāyo vā / anyathā tavāpyekavittivedyatayā sarvaikaparatve uktadoṣe kā gatiḥ kā vā gatirvyaktivācakapaśvādipadānāṃ /
bhaṭṭamate tu jātireva śakyā lāghavāt vyaktistvākṣepalabhyā /
nanu nākṣepa ekavittivedyatvāttayoḥ samānānāṃ hi bhāvaḥ sāmānyaṃ tacca vyaktiṃ vinā na bhāsate iti cet na svarūpeṇa śakyā jātiḥ na ca sāmānyatvaṃ tasyāḥ svarūpaṃ taddharmatvāt anyathā ālocane 'pi sā na bhāseta /
kathaṃ sāmānyatvenāpratītā jātirvyaktitobhinnatayā śabdanābhidhātavyeti cet na śabdena vyaktito bhinnatayā jāterabodhanāt /
nanu vyāvṛttā jātivyācyā vyāvṛttabuddhiṃ vinā vyaktiviśeṣānākṣepāt vyāvartikā tatra vyaktireva anugatatvamapyanugamyamānaṃ vinā na bhāsata iti jātivittivedyaiva vyaktiriti cet na svatovyāvṛttajātisvarūpasya vācyatvāt /
vyakterdharmāntarasya vā vyāvartakatve 'nyonyāśrayo 'navasthā vā /
nanu gauritipadāt jāti-vyakatyoryugapatpratītiḥ /
na ca sūkṣmakālabhedāgrahāt sā bhrāntā bādhakābhāvāt tathāca gopadādgotvadhīstataḥ krameṇa vyāpti-pakṣadharmatājñānaṃ tato vyaktyanumitiriti jñānaparamparakalpanādvaraṃ jātivittivedyatvaṃ vyakteriti cet na vyutpattyadhīnaṃ hi śabdasya bodhakatvaṃ ato vyutpattiparyālocanayā yugapajjñānamasiddham /
ata eva jñānaparamparākalpanamapi yuktaṃ anyathā karturapyākṣepona syāt śabdāt sakartṛ
children.translated_text:
Others, however, [hold that] initially, because the word conforms to the cognition of the individual inferred from usage, [the learner] determines that the word has capacity. But not in the cognition of the universal — because since the usage is not produced [by the universal], the [universal] is not presented at that time. Later, having known through another means of valid knowledge that the universal too is an object of that [word] — for the purpose of differentiation (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) and for the purpose of [providing] a common thread (<s>anugama</s>) to the individual — [the learner] comes to understand the word's causality in the cognition of the universal as well. And thus, the knowledge of the capacity for the individual is also a cause; there is no being-otherwise-established through the knowledge of the capacity for the universal, because the grasping of causality in universal-cognition depends upon (<s>upajīvya</s>) [the prior grasping of] causality in individual-cognition — and [this latter account is rejected] because of contradicting what is depended upon.
By this, [the view that] the universal too is the denotable, because of parsimony — [is answered as follows:] since the disposition produced from capacity-grasping is necessarily restricted to having an individual as its content, the recollection of the universal produced from the word is necessarily individual-directed. Even though the disposition has a non-determinate arousing factor, [we must] postulate the rule that the arousal of the individual-aspect [occurs] from the very [factor] that arouses the universal-aspect — just as the determinate recollection of the capacity [arises] from the very disposition aroused by the word [alone]. Without the word too, every recollection of the universal has an individual as its content — otherwise there would be the undesirable consequence of a recollection of the bare universal alone.
From the word together with the disposition, even the cognition qualified by the universal [arises] — like a recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>), as if from a sense-organ.
Precisely for this reason, the view raised [by some] from the <s>Bhāṣya</s> — 'the qualified cognition [arises] from the disposition and the capacity of the word' — is set aside. By the stated reasoning, since the individual too, like the universal, is the denotable — even though the universal-qualified [individuals] are infinite, in any one qualified [individual], setting aside the particular individual-ness and taking cow-ness, the capacity is grasped as: 'the universal-qualified is the denotable.' Just as, in some particular smoke, the cognition 'smoke pervades fire' [arises]; just as, even though effects are infinite, in some particular effect, setting aside its particular nature and taking the property of being produced by effort, the capacity is grasped from the optative suffix (<s>liṅ</s>) etc. as 'obligation is the denotable for the property-bearer.' The unity of the capacity [follows] from the unity of the delimiting condition — just like that. Or as in the words <s>paśu</s> ('animal') etc. that denote individuals. Alternatively, having known all cows through cow-ness by the general cognition (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇā</s>), capacity is grasped by taking cow-ness. And through the property of being knowable (<s>prameyatva</s>), omniscience regarding all cognitions is indeed accepted — but what is not accepted is omniscience in the sense of possessing knowledge with every mode (<s>prakāra</s>) such as pot-ness etc. Because every cow, being indifferent [regarding capacity], is the denotable — taking any particular one [as denotable leads to] indeterminacy. Otherwise, for you too, since by [the rule of] being objects of a single cognition all [cows are made] equivalent, the stated fault [would apply] — what is the solution? And what is the solution for words like <s>paśu</s> etc. that denote individuals?
In the <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> [Mīmāṃsā] view, however, the universal alone is the denotable, because of parsimony; and the individual is obtained through implication (<s>ākṣepa</s>).
[Objection:] There is no [separate] implication, because [the universal and individual] are objects of a single cognition. For the universal is the being (<s>bhāva</s>) of what is similar, and it does not appear without the individual. [Reply:] No — the universal is the denotable in its own form (<s>svarūpa</s>); and universality (<s>sāmānyatva</s>) is not its own form but a property of it — otherwise it would not appear even in indeterminate perception (<s>ālocana</s>).
[Objection:] How can the universal, which is not cognized as universal-ness, be said to be expressed by the word as distinct from the individual? [Reply:] No — because the word does not convey the universal as distinct from the individual.
[Objection:] The universal that is the denotation is differentiated [from other universals]; and without the cognition of differentiation, [it] does not imply a specific individual; the individual itself is the differentiator. And the property of being a common thread too does not appear without what is being tracked — hence the individual is necessarily an object of the cognition of the universal. [Reply:] No — because the own form of the intrinsically differentiated universal is the denotation.
If differentiation [were achieved] by the individual or by another property, [there would be] either mutual dependence or infinite regress.
[Objection:] From the word <s>gauḥ</s> ('cow'), the cognition of both the universal and the individual arises simultaneously.
Nor is that [simultaneous cognition] erroneous due to non-apprehension of a subtle temporal difference — because of the absence of a sublating cognition. And thus, from the word 'cow' [arises] the cognition of cow-ness, then sequentially the knowledge of the pervasion and the property-of-the-subject, then the inference of the individual — [but] rather than postulating such a chain of cognitions, [it is better to accept] that the individual is an object of the cognition of the universal. [Reply:] No — because the word's capacity to produce cognition depends on convention (<s>vyutpatti</s>); hence, upon examination of the convention, the simultaneous cognition is unestablished.
Precisely for this reason, the postulation of a chain of cognitions is also justified. Otherwise, even the agent (<s>kartṛ</s>) would not be obtained through implication — because from the word,

children.text:
kāyā eva kriyāyā avagamāt /
na ca jātijñānatvena vyaktiviṣayatāniyamaḥ pratyakṣādau tasya vyaktidhīhetusamājādhīnatvāt /
ata eva na jātidhīhetau vyaktidhīhetusahakāritāniyamaḥ samājasyārthasiddhatvāt gotvaṃ gavāviṣayapratītiviṣayaḥ jātitvāt gobhinnabhāvatvādveti jātimātradhīsiddheśca /
atha yat tatparatantraṃ tat tenaikāvittivedyaṃ yathārthaparatantraṃ jñānamarthena jātiśca paratantreti vyaktau bhāsamānāyāmeva bhāsata iti cet na paratantratvaṃ hi na parasamavetatvaṃ gandhādinā vyabhicārāt na taddhīnirūpyatvaṃ asiddheḥ nāpi tasmin bhāsamāna eva bhāsamānatvaṃ sādhyāviśeṣāt nāpi viśeṣaṇatvenaiva jñānaṃ gaurityeva
children.translated_text:
only the action together with the agent is understood.
Nor is there a rule that what has universal-cognition as its content must have an individual as its content — because in perception etc., [the individual-cognition] depends on the aggregate of causes of individual-cognition.
Precisely for this reason, there is no rule that the cause of universal-cognition must be assisted by the cause of individual-cognition — because the aggregate is purpose-served (<s>arthasiddha</s>, i.e. naturally present). Cow-ness is the content of a cognition [whose content is] not restricted to cows — because of being a universal; or because of being an entity different from cows — and because the cognition of the bare universal alone is established.
[Objection:] Whatever is dependent on another is an object of a single cognition with that [other] — just as cognition, being dependent on its object, [is cognized together with it]; and the universal, being dependent, appears only when the individual appears. [Reply:] No — for dependence (<s>paratantratva</s>) is not inherence-in-another (<s>parasamavetatva</s>) — because of deviation in the case of smell etc.; nor is it having-its-cognition-determined-by-another — because that is unestablished; nor is it appearing-only-when-that-appears — because that is no different from the thesis to be proved. Nor is [it] the cognition as a qualifier alone — because the cognition [from the word] 'cow' is simply 'cow.'

children.text:
pratīteḥ /
gavi gotvamiti kaścit pratyetīti cet na ālocane viśeṣaṇatvaṃ vināpi svarūpataḥ pratīteḥ jātimātraśaktāt padāt jāteḥ smaraṇamālocanameva jātiviśiṣṭagocarasaṃskārādeva padena jātyaṃśodbodhe sati jātimātrasmaraṇāt /
ata eva tato jātiṃ vināpi kadācit vyaktismṛtiḥ /
astu vā gurorivālocanamappi saṃskārajanakaṃ śabdavyutpattibalena jātimātrasmaraṇasiddheḥ /
na ca smaraṇasya viśiṣṭajñānatvameva anubhavasyāpi tathātvena nirvikalpakāsiddhiprasaṅgāt evavittavedyatve 'pi prathamadarśanavat śabdādugotvasmaraṇamālocanameva gotve govyaktivṛttitvādi vaiśiṣṭyasyāśakyatvena tadaviṣayatvāt /
na cālocanasyendriyajanyatvāt na smṛtitvaṃ jñānatvasākṣādvyāpyadharmatvena smṛtitvasyālocanavṛttitvāt /
nanvākṣepādvyaktidhīrna vyaktitvena na vā rūpāntareṇa gaurityeva pratīteḥ nāpi gotvena gotvasya gotvaviśiṣṭabhedenākṣepābhāvāditi cet na viśeṣaṇa-viśeṣyayorbhedenānumānāvirodhāt /
ata eva gotvaṃ vyaktyāśritaṃ jātitvāditi pakṣadharmatābalāt gotvāśravyaktisiddhiḥ arthāpattervā tatsiddhiḥ /
nanu vyaktyā vinā kimanupapannaṃ vyaktiṃ vināpi gotvasya tadbuddheśca siddheḥ kathamarthāpattiriti cet na vyāpakaṃ vinā vyāpyasyāsiddheḥ ucyate /
gāmanayetyato gotvaviśiṣṭasya kriyānvayabodhādgaurityākārakagoviśeṣyakabuddhiḥ kāraṇaṃ sā ca na śabdaṃ vinā ākṣepādvyaktyāśritaṃ gotvamiti dhīrna tu gauriti /
na caivaṃ vyakteḥ kriyānvayo 'pi gotvāśritatayā nirākaṅkṣatvāt rājapuruṣamānayetyatreva rājñaḥ anvaye vā vyaktimānayeti dhīḥ syāt na tu gāmiti /
kiñca gotvaṃ na vyaktivyāpyaṃ na hi yatra yadā vā gotvaṃ tatra tadā vyaktiryat sāmānyaṃ sā vyaktiriti vā niyamaḥ vyabhicārāt /
nāpi gotvaṃ gavāśritaṃ gotvādityanumitiḥ vyāptigrahaśarīratvāt /
na ca jātitvaṃ vyaktyāśritatve liṅgaṃ jātitvasya padādanupasthiteḥ tathātve vā jātivittivedyaiva vyaktiḥ /
api ca liṅgaṃ vyāpyamanupapannaṃ svāśraye vyāpakapapādakañca bodhayati / na ceha gotvāśraye vyaktibuddhiḥ /
vayantu brūmaḥ vyakterapadārthatve vibhaktyarthasaṅkhyā-karmatvādervyaktāvananvayaḥ syāt suvibhaktīnāṃ prakṛtyarthānvitasvārthabodhakatvasya vyutpattisiddhatvāt prakṛtitātparyaviṣaye tadanvayavyutpattau lakṣaṇocchedo gauravañca /
ākhyātārthasaṅkhyāpi nānumitenānveti kintu bhāvanānvayinā śuddhena prathamāntādupasthitena padāntarādupasthitireva tatrākṣepārthaḥ / ata eva na vyakterākṣepaḥ kintu lakṣaṇayā gopadādgauriti vyaktidhīriti maṇḍanaḥ /
yadāha ``jātāvastitva-nāstitve na hi viśeṣaṇe'' iti /
ucyate /
svārthādanyena rūpeṇa jñāte bhavati lakṣaṇā tīratvena jñāte gaṅgāpadasyeva /
na ceha gotvādanyena rūpeṇa vyakterupasthitiḥ kintu gotve naiva vyaktitvena sāsnādimattvena copalakṣyatve gopadādvyaktitvādirūpeṇa dhīḥ syānna tu gauriti /
nāpi gotvasambandhini gotvaviśiṣṭe lakṣaṇā gotve hi na sākṣādānayanādyanvaya iti vyaktyavacchedakatayā tasyānvaye 'mukhyatvam /
lakṣaṇayāpi gotvāvacchinnaiva vyaktiḥ kriyānvayinī pratīyate na kevalā vyaktiriti gotvaviśiṣṭasya lakṣyatve yugapadvṛttidvayavirodhaḥ gotve 'pi vā lakṣaṇā /
api ca jātimātre na śaktirna vā vyaktau lakṣaṇā jātau mukhyaprayogābhāvāt tayostanmūlakatvāt prayogo hi vyavahārahetujñānarthaḥ /
na ca jātimātranirvikalpakādvyaktimanādaya kevalajātau vyavahāraḥ tasya viśiṣṭajñānasādhyatvāt gāṃ paśya gaurastītyādāvapi gotvaviśiṣṭasyaiva jñānaṃ vyavahāraśca /
tasmādekavittivedyatvaniyamāt jātiviśiṣṭaṃ śakyam /
yadi ca tṛtīyāyāḥ karaṇaikatva iva go-gotve śakye tadā gotvaṃ govyaktiśceti dhīḥ syāt na tu gauriti vaiśiṣṭyañca sambandho vā jñāto ghaṭa ityatreva viśeṣaṇatāviśeṣor'thāntaraṃ vetyanyadetat /
jātiviśeṣavadavayavasaṃyogarūpākṛtirapi padaśakyā gopadāt jātyākṛtisadṛśākṛtau lakṣaṇā piṣṭakasaṃyogaviśeṣasyāśakyatvāt /
jātyākṛti -vyaktīnāṃ pratyekamātraparatve lakṣaṇaiva pratyekasya jātyākṛtiviśiṣṭānyatvāt yathā gurūṇāṃ kāryaśaktāyā liṅgo loke kāryatvaparatve /
ata eva vyaktyākṛti jātayastu padārtha iti pāramarṣasūtraṃ ekayaiva śaktyā ekavittivedyatvasūcanāya padārtha ityekavacanam /
jātiśaktivādaḥ evaṃ padmaṃ paṅkajapadaśakyaṃ tato niyamataḥ paṅkaja nikatṛpadmamiti pratīteḥ avayavānāṃ tatrāsāmarthyāt rūḍhiṃ vinā yogamātrāt kumude
prayogadhīprasaṅgācca /
nanu rūḍhāvapi yogāt kumude tau kuto na syātāṃ rūḍhyā pratibandhāditi prāñcaḥ /
children.translated_text:
— because of cognition.
[Objection:] Someone cognizes 'in a cow [there is] cow-ness.' [Reply:] No — because even in indeterminate perception (<s>ālocana</s>), [the universal is cognized] in its own form without [needing] the qualifier-relation. The recollection of the universal from a word having capacity for the universal alone is itself indeterminate perception — from the disposition having as its content [something] qualified by the universal, when the universal-aspect is aroused by the word, there is recollection of the bare universal alone.
Precisely for this reason, from that [word], sometimes there is recollection of the individual even without the universal.
Or let indeterminate perception too, like [the perception of] a teacher [at a distance], be a generator of dispositions — since the recollection of the bare universal alone is established through the force of verbal convention.
Nor [should it be said] that recollection is necessarily qualified cognition — because since experience (<s>anubhava</s>) too would be so, there would be the undesirable consequence of the non-establishment of indeterminate cognition (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>). Even when [the universal and individual] are objects of a single cognition, the recollection of cow-ness from the word is indeterminate perception, like first-time seeing — because qualifications such as cow-ness's occurring in cow-individuals etc. are not [part of] the denotation and hence not its content.
Nor [is the objection valid that] because indeterminate perception is produced by a sense-organ, it is not recollection — because recollection-ness, being a property that is a direct pervaded-property of cognition-ness, occurs in indeterminate perception.
[Objection:] If the cognition of the individual arises through implication (<s>ākṣepa</s>), it [arises] not through individual-ness, nor through another form — because the cognition is simply 'a cow.' Nor through cow-ness — because since cow-ness is [already present], there is no implication for something different from the cow-ness-qualified [universal]. [Reply:] No — because inference through the difference of qualifier and qualificand is non-contradictory.
Precisely for this reason, [through the inference:] 'cow-ness resides in an individual, because of being a universal' — through the force of the property-of-the-subject, the individual as substratum of cow-ness is established. Or that [individual] is established through presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>).
[Objection:] What is unexplained without the individual? Since cow-ness and its cognition are established even without the individual, how is there presumption? [Reply:] No — because it is said that the pervaded [cannot be established] without the pervader.
[Regarding the sentence] 'bring the cow' — from the cognition that the cow-ness-qualified [entity] is connected with the action, a cognition having the form 'a cow' with the cow as qualificand is the cause [of activity]. And that [cognition arises] not without the word — [whereas] through implication, [one gets only] the cognition 'cow-ness resides in an individual,' not 'a cow.'
Nor [should it be said that] since the connection of the individual with the action too [is established through] its being a substratum of cow-ness, [the universal] leaves nothing to be desired — [for then,] in 'bring the king's man,' there would be the cognition 'bring the king' when the king is connected [with the action]; or [there would be] the cognition 'bring an individual,' not 'bring a cow.'
Furthermore, cow-ness is not pervaded by individuality — for there is no rule that wherever or whenever there is cow-ness, there is [necessarily] an individual; or that whatever is a universal is [identical with] an individual — because of deviation.
Nor is [the proposition] 'cow-ness resides in a cow' [validly] inferred 'because of being cow-ness' — because that would be [merely asserting] the body of the pervasion-grasping [itself].
Nor is universal-ness an inferential mark for residing-in-an-individual — because universal-ness is not presented from the word. If it were, then the individual would be cognizable precisely through the cognition of the universal.
Furthermore, the inferential mark conveys its own substratum when the pervaded [is] unexplained, and also makes known the pervader as establishing [the mark]. But here there is no cognition of the individual in the substratum of cow-ness.
We, however, state: if the individual is not the word-meaning, there would be no connection of the case-ending meanings — number, object-ness (<s>karmatva</s>), etc. — with the individual; because the convention [establishes] that <s>sup</s> case-endings convey their own meaning connected with the stem-meaning. [If the individual is not the stem-meaning,] then in the convention of connection [of case-meanings] with the content of the stem's purport, there would be the destruction of secondary signification and prolixity.
The number [expressed by] the verb-ending too does not connect with the inferred [individual]; rather, [it connects] with the pure [stem-meaning] presented from the first-case ending [nominative] — the presentation from another word is itself the purpose of implication. Precisely for this reason, [according to] <s>Maṇḍana</s>, there is no implication of the individual; rather, there is cognition of the individual 'a cow' from the word 'cow' through secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>).
As he said: 'Existence and non-existence [are predicated] of the universal, not indeed of the qualifier.'
[Reply:] It is said:
Secondary signification occurs when [something is] known through a form other than its own meaning — as with the word <s>Gaṅgā</s> when [the bank] is known through the form of being-a-bank (<s>tīratva</s>).
But here, the individual is not presented through a form other than cow-ness; rather, in cow-ness itself, when [the individual is] indicated (<s>upalakṣya</s>) through individual-ness, dewlap-possessing-ness (<s>sāsnādimatva</s>), etc. — [then] from the word 'cow,' cognition in the form of individual-ness etc. would arise, not as 'a cow.'
Nor is there secondary signification toward the cow-ness-qualified, which is connected with cow-ness — for cow-ness does not directly connect with bringing etc.; and since [cow-ness] connects with the action [only] through the delimitation by the individual, [this connection] is non-primary (<s>amukhya</s>).
Even through secondary signification, it is the individual as delimited by cow-ness that is cognized as connected with the action — not the bare individual. Hence, if the cow-ness-qualified [entity] is the secondary referent, there would be the contradiction of two simultaneous functions; or there would be secondary signification in cow-ness as well.
Furthermore, there is neither capacity in the bare universal nor secondary signification toward the individual — because there is no primary usage [of a word] for the bare universal, and both [capacity and secondary signification] are grounded in that [primary usage]. For usage is for the purpose of knowledge that causes [practical] activity.
And from the indeterminate cognition of the bare universal, without taking an individual, there is no activity regarding the bare universal — because [activity] requires qualified cognition. Even in [sentences like] 'see the cow,' 'there is a cow,' etc., the cognition and the activity are of the cow-ness-qualified [entity] alone.
Therefore, because of the rule of being objects of a single cognition, the universal-qualified [entity] is the denotable.
And if, like the third case-ending [having capacity] for instrumentality alone, cow [and] cow-ness were [separately] denotable, then the cognition would be 'cow-ness and a cow-individual' — not 'a cow.' And whether the qualified-ness or the connection is [additionally] known — as in the cognition 'pot,' where [the question of] whether the qualifier-relation is a separate entity — that is another matter.
The configuration (<s>ākṛti</s>) — the form of the arrangement of parts (<s>avayavasaṃyoga</s>) — is also the denotable of the word, like a specific universal. From the word 'cow,' there is secondary signification toward a configuration similar to the universal-configuration — because the specific arrangement of parts like dough [in a figurine] is not the denotable.
When each of universal, configuration, and individual is separately the sole [denotable], secondary signification is needed for each — because each is other than the universal-configuration-qualified [entity]. Just as, for the teachers, when the optative suffix has obligation alone as its denotation [in worldly usage].
Precisely for this reason, the <s>Pāṇinian</s> sūtra 'individual, configuration, and universals are [all] the word-meaning' — by [using] the singular 'word-meaning' (<s>padārtha</s>), it indicates [that all three are] objects of a single cognition through a single capacity.
The <s>jātiśaktivāda</s> (doctrine of capacity for the universal). Thus, a lotus (<s>padma</s>) is the denotable of the word <s>paṅkaja</s> ('mud-born'); because there is a definite cognition 'a lotus that is mud-born' from that [word]; because the component parts [of the compound] are incapable [of denoting lotus on their own]; because without convention (<s>rūḍhi</s>), from mere etymology (<s>yoga</s>) alone, there would be the undesirable consequence of usage and cognition regarding a water-lily (<s>kumuda</s>) [which is also 'mud-born'].
[Objection:] Even with convention, why would [usage and cognition regarding the water-lily] not arise from etymology? [Reply:] Because of obstruction by convention — [say] the earlier [grammarians].

children.text:
vayantu niyamato rūḍhyā smṛtaṃ padmameva vyaktivācakaḍapratyayena paṅkajanikartṛtayānubhāvyate bādhakaṃ vinā vyaktivacanānāṃ sannihitaviśeṣaparatvaniyamāt yathāgneyīti ḍhagantapadena prakaraṇādinā sannihitā ḍhagabhihitā ṛgvyaktirbodhyate evañca sarvatra padmānubhavasāmagrīveti na kumude dhīrna vā tadarthaprayogaḥ /
nanvevaṃ rūḍhirevāstu tata evobhayalābhāt kiṃ yogarūḍhyā na avayavaśakteḥ kḷptatvāt yaugikārthānubhavācca /
yadi ca rūḍhyartha eva yaugikārtha eva vānubhūyate tadā vivāda eva syāt anubhavenaiva tadvicchedāt /
children.translated_text:
We, however, [state:] because of convention (<s>rūḍhi</s>), a lotus alone — definitely recalled [as the meaning] — is conveyed as 'mud-born' through the <s>ḍa</s> suffix denoting the individual, as one that has the nature of being born from mud. [This is] because, in the absence of a sublating cognition, words denoting individuals are necessarily restricted to referring to the specific [referent] that is present [through convention]. Just as through the <s>ḍhak</s>-suffixed word <s>āgneyī</s>, the specific <s>ṛk</s> verse that is presented through the context etc. — [and which is the referent] expressed by the <s>ḍhak</s> [suffix] — is conveyed. And thus, in all cases, the aggregate of conditions for the cognition of 'lotus' [from <s>paṅkaja</s>] is [complete] — hence there is no cognition [of a water-lily], nor usage of the word for that purpose.
[Objection:] If so, let convention alone suffice, since both [denotation and restriction to lotus] are obtained from that. What need is there for etymological convention (<s>yogarūḍhi</s>)? [Reply:] No — because the capacity of the component parts is established; and because the etymological meaning is experienced.
And if the conventional meaning alone is experienced, or the etymological meaning alone is experienced, then there would be a dispute [about which] — since experience itself would settle it.

children.text:
atra mīmāṃsakāḥ /
na tāvat smṛtyarthaṃ śaktiḥ paṅkajapadaprayogaviṣaye niyatapadmānubhavajanitasaṃskārāt smṛterevopapatteḥ smṛtestajjanyatvaniyamāt /
nāpyanubhavārthaṃ niyamataḥ smṛtaṃ padmamādāya vyaktivacananyāyenāvayavaiḥ paṅkajanikartṛ padmamityanubhavasambhavāt smṛtiśca rūḍhyā anyathā veti na kaścidviśeṣaḥ /
śaktiṃ vinā niyamataḥ prayoga eva kuta iti cet na pūrvaprayogamapekṣya avayavānumuktanyāyena padmānubhavajanakatvaniyamāt /
pūrvaprayogo 'pi tatpūrvaprayogamapekṣyetyanāditaiva /
athāniyatodbodhasya saṃskārasya śaktiṃ vinā niyatodbodhe hetvabhāvāt niyatā smṛtireva na syāditi cet na kadācicchaktito 'pi udbodhābhāvena śakyāsmaraṇāt śaktiṃ vināpi niyamataḥ śaktismaraṇācca /
udbodhakañca na niyataṃ sadṛśa-padaśakti-sambandhijñānānāṃ pratyekaṃ vyabhicārāt kintu yatra smṛtistatra tatkālotpannamaniyatamevodbodhakaṃ kalpyate phalabalāt kāryonneyadharmāṇāṃ yathākāryamunnayanāt /
na ca padmatvavattadvyāpakāderapi smṛtiprasaṅgaḥ smṛtibalenodbodhakalpanamiti tatra smṛtyabhāvena tadudbodhābhāvāt tasmācchaktiṃ vinā śakteriva padmatvasya niyatā smṛtiḥ /
na caivaṃ gavādipade 'pi na śaktiḥ syāt vyavahārakālīnasaṃskārādeva gavādismṛtisambhavāditi vācyam /
na hi tatra smṛtyarthaṃ śaktiḥ kintvanubhavārthaṃ padādanyato gavāderanubhavāsambhavādavyutpannasya tato 'nubhavāsambhavācca padmānubhavaśca yogādeveti na samudāyo heturanyathāsiddhatvāt ato nānubhavabalāt samudāye śaktikalpanam /
nanvevaṃ gavādipadānāṃ prameyatve śaktirastu gavādismṛtiḥ saṃskārāditi cet na govyavahāreṇa svopapādake gojñāne padasya śaktikalpanaṃ na tvanupapādake prameyatvena gojñāne gopadāt prameyo gaurityananubhavācca /
athaivaṃ saṃskārādeva tīrādismṛtisambhave gauṇalākṣaṇikocchedaḥ tīradyanubhavārthaṃ hi na tatkalpanaṃ tadanubhavasyetarapadādeva siddheḥ tayorananubhāvakatvāt tasmānniyatā smṛtiḥ vattisādhyeti tayoḥ kalpanāt tathā ca niyatapadmasmṛtyarthaṃ paṅkajapade 'pi vṛttitvena śaktikalpanamāvaśyakaṃ lakṣaṇādyabhāvāditi cet na gaṅgāyāmityādau vṛttiṃ vinā tīrāderapadārthatve vibhaktyarthānvayastatra na syāt vibhaktīnāṃ prakṛtyarthagatasvārthānvayabodhakatvavyutpatteḥ /
padmasya tu paṅkajavākyapratipādyatvena pācakāderiva vibhaktyarthānvayopapattiḥ /
children.translated_text:
Here the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> [argue]:
First, <s>śakti</s> (denotative power) is not needed for the purpose of <s>smṛti</s> (recollection), because in the domain of the usage of the word '<s>paṅkaja</s>' (lotus), <s>smṛti</s> is already explained by the <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) generated from the invariable experience of <s>padma</s> (lotus), since <s>smṛti</s> is necessarily produced by that [<s>saṃskāra</s>].
Nor is it needed for the purpose of <s>anubhava</s> (direct cognition), because taking the <s>padma</s> that is invariably recollected, by the principle of <s>vyaktivacana</s> (words denoting individuals), a direct cognition in the form 'the <s>padma</s> which is the producer of <s>paṅkaja</s>' is possible through the component words; and <s>smṛti</s> operates either through <s>rūḍhi</s> (conventional usage) or otherwise — there is no distinction.
If [one objects]: without <s>śakti</s>, how can there be invariable usage at all? [We reply]: No, because depending on prior usage, by the principle of inference from component parts (<s>avayavānumuktanyāya</s>), there is an invariable capacity to generate the cognition of <s>padma</s>.
Prior usage too depends on its own prior usage, and so on beginninglessly.
If [one objects]: since a <s>saṃskāra</s> whose awakening is not fixed, without <s>śakti</s> there is no cause for fixed awakening, so there would be no fixed <s>smṛti</s> — [we reply]: No, because sometimes even from <s>śakti</s> there is no awakening, so <s>śakti</s> cannot be remembered [as invariably operative]; and even without <s>śakti</s>, there is invariable recollection of <s>śakti</s> [which undermines the objection].
And the awakener is not fixed, because each of the cognitions of similarity, word-power, and relation individually deviates [from invariable concomitance]; rather, wherever there is <s>smṛti</s>, whatever non-fixed [factor] arises at that time is postulated as the awakener on the strength of the effect, since properties that are to be inferred from effects are inferred in accordance with the effect.
Nor is there the unwanted consequence that <s>padmatva</s> (lotus-ness) and its pervaders etc. would also be recollected, because the awakener is postulated on the strength of <s>smṛti</s>, and in those cases, since there is no <s>smṛti</s>, there is no awakening. Therefore, without <s>śakti</s>, <s>padmatva</s> has fixed <s>smṛti</s> just as <s>śakti</s> [would provide].
And it should not be said that in this way, even for words like '<s>go</s>' (cow) etc., there would be no <s>śakti</s>, because <s>smṛti</s> of cow etc. would be possible from <s>saṃskāra</s> alone at the time of practical usage.
For there, <s>śakti</s> is not for the purpose of <s>smṛti</s> but for the purpose of <s>anubhava</s> (direct cognition), because <s>anubhava</s> of cow etc. is not possible from anything other than the word for one who has not learned, and for one who has not learned, <s>anubhava</s> from that [word alone] is not possible; and the <s>anubhava</s> of <s>padma</s> is from <s>yoga</s> (combination of component words) alone, so the aggregate is not the cause since it is otherwise established — therefore, postulation of <s>śakti</s> in the aggregate on the strength of <s>anubhava</s> is not warranted.
If [one says]: let <s>śakti</s> exist for words like '<s>go</s>' etc. with respect to <s>prameyatva</s> (being an object of valid cognition); <s>smṛti</s> of cow etc. is from <s>saṃskāra</s> — [we reply]: No, through the practical usage of '<s>go</s>,' <s>śakti</s> of the word is postulated for the cognition of cow that it supports, not for the cognition of cow as a <s>prameya</s> that it does not support; and because there is no <s>anubhava</s> of the form 'cow is a <s>prameya</s>' from the word '<s>go</s>.'
If [one objects]: in this way, if <s>smṛti</s> of <s>tīra</s> (bank) etc. is possible from <s>saṃskāra</s> alone, there would be destruction of <s>gauṇa</s> (secondary meaning) and <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) — [we reply]: the postulation of those is not for the purpose of <s>anubhava</s> of <s>tīra</s> etc., because the <s>anubhava</s> of that [<s>tīra</s>] is established from the other word alone, since those two [<s>gauṇa</s> and <s>lakṣaṇā</s>] are not capable of producing <s>anubhava</s>.
Therefore, fixed <s>smṛti</s> is to be established by <s>vṛtti</s> (semantic function), hence the postulation of those two.
And if [one then argues]: for the purpose of the fixed <s>smṛti</s> of <s>padma</s>, even in the word '<s>paṅkaja</s>,' postulation of <s>śakti</s> as <s>vṛtti</s> is necessary, because there is no <s>lakṣaṇā</s> etc. — [we reply]: No, because in [expressions like] '<s>gaṅgāyām</s>' (on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>) etc., without <s>vṛtti</s>, if <s>tīra</s> (bank) etc. is not the word-meaning, the connection with the case-ending meaning would not be possible there, since the convention is that case-endings convey the connection of their own meaning with the meaning of the stem.
But for <s>padma</s>, since it is what is conveyed by the <s>paṅkaja</s>-sentence, the connection with the case-ending meaning is possible, just as in [the case of] <s>pācaka</s> (cook) etc.
